sec01-card-sec01-F001.front: You walk up to the ND driver-license counter to test. What four things do your ID and address papers have to prove before they let you sit down?
sec01-card-sec01-F001.expected_back: Testing requires identification proving legal presence, present name and birth date, together with evidence of a North Dakota residential address.

sec01-card-sec01-F002.front: Whether you are applying for a permit, a driver license, or a state ID card in North Dakota, what personal number has to go on the application?
sec01-card-sec01-F002.expected_back: The handbook requires a social security number on permit, license and identification-card applications.

sec01-card-sec01-F003.front: If you are under eighteen applying in North Dakota, who has to approve and sponsor your application — and what extra rule applies to a legal guardian?
sec01-card-sec01-F003.expected_back: For applicants younger than eighteen, a parent, legal guardian or designated person must approve and sponsor the application; guardians must show their papers.

sec01-card-sec01-F004.front: You are heading in for an office knowledge test. What is the latest cutoff time to arrive before closing — and before lunch if that office shuts at noon?
sec01-card-sec01-F004.expected_back: For office knowledge testing, arrive at least one hour before closing and, where the office closes for lunch, at least one hour before noon.

sec01-card-sec01-F005.front: What happens to your knowledge test score if you walk into the testing zone carrying your phone, smartwatch, or prohibited personal items?
sec01-card-sec01-F005.expected_back: Taking prohibited belongings or electronic devices into the knowledge-testing area results in a failed score; secure them before entering.

sec01-card-sec01-F006.front: Midway through the ND knowledge exam, you step out of the testing area before submitting your test. What happens?
sec01-card-sec01-F006.expected_back: Leaving the knowledge-testing area before finishing the examination results in failure.

sec01-card-sec01-F007.front: Pets are banned from the ND testing area, except for which two specific types of animals?
sec01-card-sec01-F007.expected_back: The testing-area animal exception covers medical-alert and service animals.

sec01-card-sec01-F008.front: What accessibility standard do all North Dakota driver-license offices meet, and what language help is available for general office business?
sec01-card-sec01-F008.expected_back: All driver-license offices are described as accessible under the ADA, and interpretation is available for general business.

sec01-card-sec01-F009.front: You pull up for your ND road test. Which three documents must you hand over before the drive starts?
sec01-card-sec01-F009.expected_back: Bring a valid North Dakota operator permit, current vehicle registration and current insurance evidence for the road test.

sec01-card-sec01-F010.front: If you are taking your ND road test before turning sixteen, what extra certificate and who in person must come with you?
sec01-card-sec01-F010.expected_back: Road-test applicants younger than sixteen must bring a driver-education training certificate and be accompanied by a parent or guardian.

sec01-card-sec01-F011.front: Before the examiner rides out onto the street with you, what check does your road-test car have to pass first?
sec01-card-sec01-F011.expected_back: The road-test vehicle must pass an equipment inspection before testing begins.

sec01-card-sec01-F012.front: Who and what must be cleared out of the car during your ND road test — and what is the lone animal exception?
sec01-card-sec01-F012.expected_back: Passengers, electronic devices and pets are excluded from the road-test vehicle, with an exception for medical-alert or service animals.

sec01-card-sec01-F013.front: Your family car has an automatic self-parking feature. What are your two options if you want to take the ND road test?
sec01-card-sec01-F013.expected_back: For a self-parking vehicle, disable that feature or use a different vehicle for the test.

sec01-card-sec01-F014.front: Who has to be allowed to inspect your vehicle before the North Dakota road test can start?
sec01-card-sec01-F014.expected_back: The examiner must be allowed to inspect the vehicle before the road test.

sec01-card-sec01-F015.front: During the pre-test check, which two brake systems and which three lighting systems on your car have to work?
sec01-card-sec01-F015.expected_back: Working stopping and parking brakes, high and low headlights, rear lights and turn signals are required for the test vehicle.

sec01-card-sec01-F016.front: Beyond brakes and lights, which four exhaust, door, belt, and windshield items must work on your road-test vehicle?
sec01-card-sec01-F016.expected_back: The test vehicle needs an exhaust system without leaks and a muffler, doors operable from both sides, seat belts and functioning wipers.

sec01-card-sec01-F017.front: What exact distance number applies to BOTH your horn loudness and your rear-mirror view on the ND road-test inspection?
sec01-card-sec01-F017.expected_back: The road-test inspection requires a horn audible at two hundred feet and mirrors allowing a view two hundred feet to the rear.

sec01-card-sec01-F018.front: When does cracked glass disqualify a car from being used for your North Dakota road test?
sec01-card-sec01-F018.expected_back: Cracked glass that impairs the driver's or examiner's view or safe operation makes the road-test vehicle unsuitable.

sec01-card-sec01-F019.front: What happens to your road test if the vehicle itself is unsafe or creates an unsafe working environment for the examiner?
sec01-card-sec01-F019.expected_back: An unsafe vehicle or unsafe working environment prevents administration of the road test.

sec01-card-sec01-F020.front: Outside the student, tourist, and military exceptions, how many consecutive days of living in North Dakota makes you a resident for licensing?
sec01-card-sec01-F020.expected_back: Apart from the stated nonresident-student, tourist and military exceptions, ninety consecutive days living in North Dakota establishes residency for licensing.

sec01-card-sec01-F021.front: Once you become a North Dakota resident, how long can you drive a Class D or Class M vehicle on your out-of-state license before getting an ND license?
sec01-card-sec01-F021.expected_back: After becoming a resident, a person may drive a Class D or M vehicle with another state's license for sixty days before obtaining the required North Dakota license.

sec01-card-sec01-F022.front: Once North Dakota issues your permit or driver license, what two things must you do with the physical card?
sec01-card-sec01-F022.expected_back: Sign your North Dakota license or permit and carry it whenever you drive.

sec01-card-sec01-F023.front: What minimum age and license requirement must a nonresident meet to legally drive in North Dakota under the visitor exemption?
sec01-card-sec01-F023.expected_back: A nonresident needs to be at least sixteen and possess a valid home-state or home-country license to use the listed licensing exemption.

sec01-card-sec01-F024.front: Which two groups driving government vehicles on official business are exempt from needing a North Dakota license?
sec01-card-sec01-F024.expected_back: The official-business exemption applies to federal employees and North Dakota National Guard personnel operating government vehicles.

sec01-card-sec01-F025.front: A North Dakota resident leaves on active military duty with a valid ND license. How long does that license stay valid after separation or discharge?
sec01-card-sec01-F025.expected_back: For residents serving on active military duty outside the state, a license valid when they left remains valid through thirty days after separation or discharge.

sec01-card-sec01-F026.front: If your driver license is currently suspended or revoked in another state, can you get a North Dakota license?
sec01-card-sec01-F026.expected_back: A suspended or revoked license in any state prevents obtaining a North Dakota license under the handbook's eligibility list.

sec01-card-sec01-F027.front: If an applicant has a history of seizures or episodes of lost consciousness, what two requirements unlock the handbook exception?
sec01-card-sec01-F027.expected_back: The stated exception for a history of seizures or lost consciousness requires at least six seizure-free months and submission to the required medical examination.

sec01-card-sec01-F028.front: Who is legally qualified to sit beside you and supervise when you drive on a North Dakota instruction permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F028.expected_back: A permit supervisor must hold the proper vehicle-class license, be eighteen or older, and have at least three years of driving experience.

sec01-card-sec01-F029.front: Where must your supervising driver sit while you drive on a permit — and when is anyone else allowed in the front seat?
sec01-card-sec01-F029.expected_back: The supervising driver sits beside the permit holder; another front-seat occupant is allowed only where the vehicle has no rear seat, with the supervisor still beside the learner.

sec01-card-sec01-F030.front: What is the minimum age to get a North Dakota instruction permit, and what two screenings must you pass?
sec01-card-sec01-F030.expected_back: To obtain an instruction permit, an applicant must be at least fourteen and pass the knowledge examination and vision screening.

sec01-card-sec01-F031.front: If a minor’s parent or guardian cannot appear in person to sign for a permit, how can they authorize a temporary signer — and who keeps financial responsibility?
sec01-card-sec01-F031.expected_back: For a minor's permit sponsorship, an absent parent or guardian may designate a temporary signer by notarized document while retaining financial responsibility.

sec01-card-sec01-F032.front: How can a minor be sponsored for a permit if neither parent nor a guardian is living?
sec01-card-sec01-F032.expected_back: When no parent or guardian is living, another adult may sponsor the minor by swearing responsibility.

sec01-card-sec01-F033.front: You ace the ND permit knowledge test online from home. Can you start driving right away, or what step is still required?
sec01-card-sec01-F033.expected_back: Passing the permit examination online still requires an appointment at a driver-license office to obtain the permit.

sec01-card-sec01-F034.front: If you get your permit at fourteen or fifteen, how long must you hold it before a road test or waiver — including the hard floor?
sec01-card-sec01-F034.memory_hook: Twelve months or sixteen, six-month floor
sec01-card-sec01-F034.expected_back: At fourteen or fifteen, hold the permit for twelve months or until sixteen, whichever occurs first, with an absolute minimum of six months before a road test or waiver.

sec01-card-sec01-F035.front: If you get your permit at sixteen or seventeen, how long must you hold it before taking the road test or using a waiver?
sec01-card-sec01-F035.expected_back: At sixteen or seventeen, hold the permit for six months or until eighteen, whichever occurs first, before the road test or waiver.

sec01-card-sec01-F036.front: Besides formal driver ed, how many supervised practice hours must a learner under sixteen log — and in what kind of conditions?
sec01-card-sec01-F036.expected_back: A learner younger than sixteen must complete at least fifty supervised practice hours in varied conditions, in addition to formal driver education.

sec01-card-sec01-F037.front: How does North Dakota verify those fifty practice hours when an under-sixteen learner shows up at the test site?
sec01-card-sec01-F037.expected_back: For the under-sixteen practice requirement, a parent or guardian must attend the test site and sign confirmation of the completed hours.

sec01-card-sec01-F038.front: To qualify for a road-test waiver certificate, how many classroom hours and how many actual behind-the-wheel hours must it document?
sec01-card-sec01-F038.expected_back: A road-test waiver requires an approved completion certificate documenting at least thirty classroom hours and six actual behind-the-wheel hours.

sec01-card-sec01-F039.front: How many driving-record points does the ND handbook assign if you drive in violation of your instruction-permit conditions?
sec01-card-sec01-F039.expected_back: Driving contrary to instruction-permit conditions brings a two-point driving-record penalty in this handbook.

sec01-card-sec01-F040.front: Under the school-program exception, when can a fourteen-year-old drive a driver-education car?
sec01-card-sec01-F040.expected_back: A student at least fourteen may drive an insured school driver-education vehicle with a certified instructor under the stated school-program exception.

sec01-card-sec01-F041.front: What form must your identity documents be in at the ND counter — and which two common items get rejected every time?
sec01-card-sec01-F041.expected_back: Identity documents must be originals or certified copies; photocopies and hospital birth certificates are not accepted.

sec01-card-sec01-F042.front: What must you bring if your current name does not match your identity document — and do photocopies count?
sec01-card-sec01-F042.expected_back: If the current name differs from the identity document, bring a certified marriage, adoption or court name-change document; photocopies do not qualify.

sec02-card-sec02-F001.front: What two details must your Social Security proof show at the North Dakota counter, and which four documents count as examples?
sec02-card-sec02-F001.expected_back: Social-security evidence must show both the applicant's name and complete number; accepted examples include the card, a W-two, a one thousand ninety-nine or a pay stub.

sec02-card-sec02-F002.front: How many approved documents do you need to prove your North Dakota residential address, and how current must they be?
sec02-card-sec02-F002.expected_back: North Dakota residential-address proof requires two of the listed documents, using the most recently issued versions.

sec02-card-sec02-F003.front: What two items must appear on your North Dakota address documents, and why will a post-office box fail?
sec02-card-sec02-F003.expected_back: Address evidence must include the person's name and physical home address; a post-office box cannot establish residence.

sec02-card-sec02-F004.front: If you use a school or college transcript as North Dakota address proof, how recently must it have been issued?
sec02-card-sec02-F004.expected_back: The address-document list includes a school or college transcript issued within the preceding six months.

sec02-card-sec02-F005.front: Who provides the car for a North Dakota road test, and whose instructions govern the drive from start to finish?
sec02-card-sec02-F005.expected_back: A road-test applicant supplies the vehicle and must follow the examiner's directions throughout testing.

sec02-card-sec02-F006.front: Which five core driving habits and maneuvers must you demonstrate cleanly to pass the North Dakota road test?
sec02-card-sec02-F006.expected_back: Passing the road test requires correct lane use, signals, parallel parking, driving posture and compliance with traffic controls and laws.

sec02-card-sec02-F007.front: If you do not pass a North Dakota driver exam on your first try, how soon are you allowed to retest?
sec02-card-sec02-F007.expected_back: After failing an examination, the applicant cannot retake it that same day.

sec02-card-sec02-F008.front: What are the two driver-training hour paths for a fourteen- or fifteen-year-old earning a North Dakota training certificate?
sec02-card-sec02-F008.expected_back: For a fourteen- or fifteen-year-old's training certificate, the handbook gives a school-program option of thirty classroom hours plus six driving hours, or six driving hours through an approved commercial school.

sec02-card-sec02-F009.front: When you pass your road test at fifteen, what license do you get and whose vehicles are you legally allowed to drive?
sec02-card-sec02-F009.expected_back: A fifteen-year-old who passes the road test receives a restricted Class D license limited to vehicles of a parent, guardian, grandparent, sibling, aunt or uncle.

sec02-card-sec02-F010.front: Between which night hours must a restricted fifteen-year-old have a parent, guardian, or adult at least eighteen riding along?
sec02-card-sec02-F010.expected_back: A restricted fifteen-year-old driver needs a parent, guardian or other adult at least eighteen during the period starting at the later of sunset or nine p.m. and ending at five a.m.

sec02-card-sec02-F011.front: Which three direct trips let a restricted fifteen-year-old drive solo during North Dakota's nighttime curfew window?
sec02-card-sec02-F011.expected_back: The fifteen-year-old nighttime restriction exempts direct travel to or from work, an official school activity or a religious activity.

sec02-card-sec02-F012.front: At what birthday does a North Dakota teen's restricted Class D license lift its age restrictions under the handbook rule?
sec02-card-sec02-F012.expected_back: At sixteen, the restricted Class D license becomes unrestricted under the handbook's age rule.

sec02-card-sec02-F013.front: Which two groups of North Dakota drivers are completely banned from using electronic communication devices behind the wheel?
sec02-card-sec02-F013.expected_back: Every instruction-permit driver, regardless of age, and every licensed driver younger than eighteen is barred from using electronic communication devices while driving.

sec02-card-sec02-F014.front: Under what three urgent situations may a permit holder or teen under eighteen legally use a phone while driving?
sec02-card-sec02-F014.expected_back: The device restriction allows use for emergency help, prevention of an apparently imminent crime, or a reasonable belief that someone's life or safety is threatened.

sec02-card-sec02-F015.front: What does checking the donor box on your North Dakota application cover, and who affirms that choice if you are under eighteen?
sec02-card-sec02-F015.expected_back: Choosing the donor box on the application indicates consent to organ, tissue and eye donation; a donor younger than eighteen has the decision affirmed by parents.

sec02-card-sec02-F016.front: If a minor's permit or license is canceled for alcohol or drugs, how does North Dakota treat their prior driving history?
sec02-card-sec02-F016.expected_back: After the described alcohol- or drug-related cancellation, a minor is treated as having had no previous permit or license and must satisfy the listed testing, education and permit-holding requirements.

sec02-card-sec02-F017.front: Once you finish every requirement after a license cancellation, does your North Dakota driving record drop back to zero points?
sec02-card-sec02-F017.expected_back: Completing cancellation requirements does not automatically reset the driver's point total to zero.

sec02-card-sec02-F018.front: On a North Dakota license, what do restriction codes one, two, and three each require when you drive?
sec02-card-sec02-F018.memory_hook: One lenses, two mirrors, three automatic
sec02-card-sec02-F018.expected_back: Restriction code one means corrective lenses; code two means outside mirrors, and code three means automatic transmission.

sec02-card-sec02-F019.front: What driving limits do North Dakota restriction codes four, five, and six stand for on a license?
sec02-card-sec02-F019.memory_hook: Four controls, five daylight, six financial
sec02-card-sec02-F019.expected_back: Restriction code four identifies special hand controls, five limits driving to daylight, and six requires financial-responsibility proof.

sec02-card-sec02-F020.front: If restriction code nine is printed on your North Dakota permit or license, where is that specific limitation explained?
sec02-card-sec02-F020.expected_back: Restriction code nine refers to another limitation explained on the reverse of the license or permit.

sec02-card-sec02-F021.front: Permanently losing the use of which five body parts must be reported to the North Dakota Driver License Division?
sec02-card-sec02-F021.expected_back: Permanently losing use of a hand, arm, foot, leg or eye must be reported to the Driver License Division.

sec02-card-sec02-F022.front: At what exact time and date does a North Dakota driver license expire — including for temporary-stay holders?
sec02-card-sec02-F022.expected_back: A license expires at midnight on the holder's birthday, or on the immigration duration-of-stay date subject to the usual licensing-cycle limit.

sec02-card-sec02-F023.front: How early can you renew a North Dakota license before it expires, and do you lose your remaining months?
sec02-card-sec02-F023.expected_back: Renewal is allowed ten months before expiration without forfeiting the old license's remaining time.

sec02-card-sec02-F024.front: How do you clear the vision requirement when renewing your North Dakota license, and how recent must a doctor's certificate be?
sec02-card-sec02-F024.expected_back: Renewal applicants need vision testing or a physician's or optometrist's vision certificate no older than six months.

sec02-card-sec02-F025.front: Which three card problems require you to apply for a replacement North Dakota license or permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F025.expected_back: Apply for a replacement license or permit if it is lost, contains incorrect information or is damaged beyond readability.

sec02-card-sec02-F026.front: After changing your name or moving to a new address, how many days do you have to notify the Driver License Division — and what must you include?
sec02-card-sec02-F026.expected_back: Notify the Driver License Division of a changed name or address within ten days, providing documentary evidence.

sec02-card-sec02-F027.front: How soon must a vehicle be registered in North Dakota once its owner or operator moves in or takes gainful employment here?
sec02-card-sec02-F027.expected_back: The handbook calls for immediate North Dakota vehicle registration when an owner or operator becomes resident or gainfully employed in the state.

sec02-card-sec02-F028.front: What insurance coverage must every North Dakota motor vehicle carry, and what duty falls on the vehicle's owner?
sec02-card-sec02-F028.expected_back: A vehicle must have liability insurance, and its owner must not allow it to be driven without that coverage.

sec02-card-sec02-F029.front: When can an out-of-state vehicle use North Dakota temporary registration instead of full permanent plates?
sec02-card-sec02-F029.expected_back: Temporary registration is an option for a short North Dakota stay when the vehicle's other-state registration remains current.

sec02-card-sec02-F030.front: What two lengths do North Dakota temporary vehicle permits come in, and what extra fee applies on top of registration each time?
sec02-card-sec02-F030.memory_hook: Six or twelve months, ten-dollar fee
sec02-card-sec02-F030.expected_back: The handbook describes temporary vehicle permits of six or twelve months, with a ten-dollar service charge in addition to registration fees for each purchase or renewal.

sec02-card-sec02-F031.front: Where must a vehicle's registration card be kept at all times?
sec02-card-sec02-F031.expected_back: Keep the registration card inside the vehicle at all times.

sec02-card-sec02-F032.front: Which license class does this North Dakota handbook prepare you for, and what is required for other classes?
sec02-card-sec02-F032.expected_back: The manual prepares readers for Class D; other license classes have their own examinations and driving-skill demonstrations.

sec02-card-sec02-F033.front: Under basic North Dakota Class D rules, what are the GVWR caps for the single vehicle and for a towed trailer?
sec02-card-sec02-F033.expected_back: The basic Class D category covers a single vehicle below twenty-six thousand one pounds GVWR towing a trailer no heavier than ten thousand pounds GVWR.

sec02-card-sec02-F034.front: When a Class D combination tops twenty-six thousand pounds under the handbook rule, what age or exemption must the driver meet?
sec02-card-sec02-F034.expected_back: For the Class D combined-weight rule above twenty-six thousand pounds, the driver must be eighteen or qualify for the farm exemption.

sec02-card-sec02-F035.front: When can a Class D driver legally tow a trailer rated above ten thousand pounds?
sec02-card-sec02-F035.expected_back: Class D also covers trucks towing trailers over ten thousand pounds when the gross combination weight rating does not exceed twenty-six thousand pounds.

sec02-card-sec02-F036.front: Which four license classes are off-limits on a standard Class D license unless you hold the required endorsement?
sec02-card-sec02-F036.expected_back: Class D does not authorize Class A, B, C or M operation without the required endorsement.

sec02-card-sec02-F037.front: Which five special vehicle or towing categories are listed as exceptions covered under a Class D license?
sec02-card-sec02-F037.expected_back: The listed Class D exceptions include emergency vehicles, recreational vehicles, campers, military-duty vehicles and personal-use travel-trailer towing.

sec02-card-sec02-F038.front: Under North Dakota's farm exemption, how far and up to what gross weight may a fifteen-year-old haul farm products or supplies?
sec02-card-sec02-F038.expected_back: Under the farm exemption, a fifteen-year-old may carry farm products or supplies in a farm vehicle within one hundred fifty miles of the farm with gross weight no greater than fifty thousand pounds.

sec04-card-sec04-F001.front: What tools do work-zone flaggers use to stop, slow, or guide cars, and how must you respond?
sec04-card-sec04-F001.expected_back: Work-zone flaggers use flags or stop-and-slow paddles to stop, slow or guide traffic; follow their directions.

sec04-card-sec04-F002.front: Which four roadway hazards can show up inside a work zone, and what two actions should you take?
sec04-card-sec04-F002.expected_back: Work zones may contain narrow lanes, uneven surfaces, loose gravel and heavy equipment, so pay close attention and slow down.

sec04-card-sec04-F003.front: Does North Dakota road construction happen only during daylight, or when should you watch for work zones?
sec04-card-sec04-F003.expected_back: Road work can occur after dark as well as by day; watch for work zones at any hour.

sec04-card-sec04-F004.front: What four navigation details do green highway signs with white lettering give you?
sec04-card-sec04-F004.expected_back: Green direction signs use white text to identify routes, junctions, destinations and distances.

sec04-card-sec04-F005.front: Where does a green highway milepost start counting its white mileage numbers from?
sec04-card-sec04-F005.memory_hook: Mileposts count from south, west, origin
sec04-card-sec04-F005.expected_back: A green milepost's white numbers measure miles from the route's state origin or the state's south or west boundary.

sec04-card-sec04-F006.front: What color scheme marks motorist service signs, and what does the access symbol tell travelers?
sec04-card-sec04-F006.expected_back: Blue service signs use white symbols, and the access symbol identifies facilities free of mobility barriers.

sec04-card-sec04-F007.front: What type of destination is marked by white symbols on a brown road sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F007.expected_back: White symbols on a brown sign identify a recreational area.

sec04-card-sec04-F008.front: Where must you stop for a steady red traffic light, and what two conditions let you move forward?
sec04-card-sec04-F008.expected_back: A steady red traffic light requires stopping at the stop line or before the crosswalk and remaining stopped until the signal permits movement and the intersection is clear.

sec04-card-sec04-F009.front: What exact transition does a steady yellow traffic light warn drivers is happening?
sec04-card-sec04-F009.expected_back: A yellow traffic light warns that green is ending and red is about to begin.

sec04-card-sec04-F010.front: Does a steady green traffic light let you go automatically, or what condition must be met first?
sec04-card-sec04-F010.expected_back: A green light permits movement only when the intersection is clear.

sec04-card-sec04-F011.front: When a green arrow lights up next to a red signal, can you go — and who still gets priority?
sec04-card-sec04-F011.expected_back: A green arrow permits its indicated movement, even alongside red, but drivers must yield to pedestrians and vehicles already within the intersection.

sec04-card-sec04-F012.front: Under what three conditions can you make a right turn on a steady red light?
sec04-card-sec04-F012.expected_back: After a complete stop, a right turn on red is permitted when vehicles and pedestrians are clear, unless a sign forbids it.

sec04-card-sec04-F013.front: In North Dakota, which exact street-to-street setup lets you turn left on a red light if no sign bans it?
sec04-card-sec04-F013.expected_back: The handbook allows a left turn on red between two one-way streets unless prohibited by a sign.

sec04-card-sec04-F014.front: You roll up to an intersection and the overhead traffic lights are completely unlit. What must you do?
sec04-card-sec04-F014.expected_back: At an unlit traffic signal, stop and yield to vehicles already in the intersection.

sec04-card-sec04-F015.front: How must you treat a flashing red traffic signal, and when may you pull out?
sec04-card-sec04-F015.expected_back: Treat a flashing red signal as a stop sign and proceed only when pedestrians and vehicles are clear.

sec04-card-sec04-F016.front: What does a flashing yellow intersection signal allow you to do?
sec04-card-sec04-F016.expected_back: A flashing yellow signal allows cautious passage through the intersection.

sec04-card-sec04-F017.front: On a dedicated left-turn signal, what do a steady red indication and a steady yellow indication each tell you?
sec04-card-sec04-F017.expected_back: For a left-turn signal, steady red requires waiting, while steady yellow warns that the arrow is changing to red.

sec04-card-sec04-F018.front: What does a flashing yellow left-turn arrow allow, and who gets the right of way first?
sec04-card-sec04-F018.expected_back: A flashing yellow left arrow permits a cautious left turn after yielding to approaching traffic and pedestrians.

sec04-card-sec04-F019.front: Which left-turn signal indication gives left-turning drivers the right of way?
sec04-card-sec04-F019.expected_back: A steady green left arrow gives left-turning traffic the right of way.

sec04-card-sec04-F020.front: On a two-way roadway, what two maneuvers are allowed across a single broken yellow centerline?
sec04-card-sec04-F020.expected_back: A broken yellow centerline on a two-way road may be crossed for passing or a left turn.

sec04-card-sec04-F021.front: When solid and broken yellow centerlines run side by side, what is forbidden and what stays legal if the solid line is beside your lane?
sec04-card-sec04-F021.expected_back: With adjacent solid and broken yellow lines, a driver beside the solid line cannot pass but may cross it to turn left.

sec04-card-sec04-F022.front: What does a double solid yellow centerline ban for both directions, and what crossing maneuver stays legal?
sec04-card-sec04-F022.memory_hook: Double yellow: turns yes, passing no
sec04-card-sec04-F022.expected_back: A double solid yellow centerline prohibits passing in both directions; crossing for a left turn remains permitted.

sec04-card-sec04-F023.front: When an intersection provides special turning lanes, how must you position your car before making a turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F023.expected_back: Use the designated turn lane for the direction you intend to turn when an intersection provides special turning lanes.

sec04-card-sec04-F024.front: Where must your front bumper stop when an intersection has a wide white stop line ahead of a marked crosswalk?
sec04-card-sec04-F024.expected_back: Stop before the wide white stop line, including when a marked crosswalk lies beyond it.

sec04-card-sec04-F025.front: If an intersection has no painted stop line or crosswalk stripes, where are the two fallback places to stop?
sec04-card-sec04-F025.expected_back: Without markings, stop before the sidewalk crossing area or, if there is no crosswalk, before entering the intersection.

sec04-card-sec04-F026.front: Which two white paint styles can mark a crosswalk, and where must your vehicle stay?
sec04-card-sec04-F026.expected_back: Crosswalks may use two white boundary lines or longitudinal white markings; keep your vehicle out of the pedestrian crossing.

sec04-card-sec04-F027.front: What four actions must kick in as soon as you reach a railroad advance warning sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F027.expected_back: At a railroad advance warning, reduce speed, look and listen, and prepare to stop.

sec04-card-sec04-F028.front: Why must you scan every set of rails before crossing multiple railroad tracks right after a train passes?
sec04-card-sec04-F028.expected_back: Before crossing multiple railroad tracks, check every track; another train may approach from the opposite direction after the first clears.

sec04-card-sec04-F029.front: Where must you make any required stop near a railway crossing, and what is forbidden on the rails?
sec04-card-sec04-F029.memory_hook: Never stop or park on tracks
sec04-card-sec04-F029.expected_back: Do not park or stop on railway tracks; make any required stop before reaching them.

sec04-card-sec04-F030.front: What is the minimum distance you must stop before a railroad crossing while a train is passing?
sec04-card-sec04-F030.expected_back: When a train is passing, stop at least fifteen feet before the crossing.

sec04-card-sec04-F031.front: What is the rule when red railroad crossing lights are flashing or the crossing gates are lowered?
sec04-card-sec04-F031.expected_back: Never cross with red railroad lights flashing or drive around lowered crossing gates.

sec04-card-sec04-F032.front: Which vehicles must stop fifteen to fifty feet from railroad tracks, and what must you never do while they are stopped there?
sec04-card-sec04-F032.expected_back: School buses, passenger buses and vehicles carrying explosives or flammable liquids must stop fifteen to fifty feet from railroad tracks; do not pass them while they are stopped there.

sec04-card-sec04-F033.front: At a passive railway crossing without gates or flashing lights, what three tasks fall on the driver?
sec04-card-sec04-F033.memory_hook: Spot crossing, check trains, confirm room
sec04-card-sec04-F033.expected_back: At a passive railway crossing, the driver must recognize the crossing, check for trains and decide whether sufficient clear space exists to cross safely.

sec04-card-sec04-F034.front: What three warning devices regulate vehicles at an active railroad crossing?
sec04-card-sec04-F034.memory_hook: Active crossings use lights, bells, gates
sec04-card-sec04-F034.expected_back: Active railroad crossings use devices such as flashing red lights, bells and gates to regulate vehicles.

sec04-card-sec04-F035.front: If your car gets trapped on railroad tracks with a train approaching, how do you move away and which two contacts do you call?
sec04-card-sec04-F035.expected_back: If trapped on tracks, leave the vehicle and move away at a forty-five-degree angle toward the approaching train, then report through the posted ENS number and call nine-one-one.

sec04-card-sec04-F036.front: Which posted contact should you use to report blocked tracks or malfunctioning railroad crossing lights or gates?
sec04-card-sec04-F036.expected_back: Use the posted railroad emergency notification contact to report obstructions or malfunctioning crossing lights or gates.

sec05-card-sec05-F001.front: How far ahead of a turn must your blinker stay on continuously before you turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F001.expected_back: Signal a turn continuously throughout the final one hundred feet before turning.

sec05-card-sec05-F002.front: Two cars reach an unsigned intersection at roughly the same moment. Which driver has to yield?
sec05-card-sec05-F002.expected_back: At an unsigned intersection reached by two vehicles at about the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

sec05-card-sec05-F003.front: How should you approach an intersection, and in what three-step order should you scan cross traffic?
sec05-card-sec05-F003.expected_back: Approach intersections prepared to yield, checking left, then right, then left again.

sec05-card-sec05-F004.front: At an uncontrolled T-shaped intersection, which drivers must yield the right of way?
sec05-card-sec05-F004.expected_back: At an uncontrolled T junction, traffic on the ending road yields to vehicles on the continuing roadway.

sec05-card-sec05-F005.front: When you are waiting to make a left turn, what must you do for oncoming vehicles?
sec05-card-sec05-F005.expected_back: A left-turning vehicle yields to traffic approaching from the opposite direction.

sec05-card-sec05-F006.front: Who goes first at a four-way stop, and what should you do if another driver jumps out of turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F006.expected_back: At a four-way stop, the first vehicle to stop proceeds first; yield even to an out-of-turn driver to avoid a collision.

sec05-card-sec05-F007.front: When a walker is in your travel lane at an intersection, does the crosswalk need painted lines for you to yield?
sec05-card-sec05-F007.expected_back: Yield to pedestrians occupying your travel lane in either marked or unmarked crosswalks.

sec05-card-sec05-F008.front: How must you stop and behave when a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog is crossing?
sec05-card-sec05-F008.expected_back: Stop behind a crosswalk to preserve an unobstructed route for a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, and do not distract the dog.

sec05-card-sec05-F009.front: Who has the right of way when you pull out of or cross a road from a private driveway?
sec05-card-sec05-F009.expected_back: Entering or crossing a road from a private drive requires yielding to approaching traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F010.front: In a business or residential area, where must you stop when pulling out of an alley, driveway, private road, or building?
sec05-card-sec05-F010.expected_back: When leaving a driveway, alley, private road or building in a business or residential district, stop before crossing the sidewalk or, without one, before entering the roadway.

sec05-card-sec05-F011.front: How much clear sight distance do you need near a curve or hillcrest for a U-turn to be legal?
sec05-card-sec05-F011.expected_back: A U-turn is forbidden near a hillcrest or curve where the driver cannot see at least five hundred feet.

sec05-card-sec05-F012.front: What must you do when an emergency or police vehicle approaches with its siren or flashing red, white, or blue lights?
sec05-card-sec05-F012.expected_back: For an approaching emergency or law-enforcement vehicle using its siren or flashing red, white or blue lights, stop at the right edge or curb and wait until it passes.

sec05-card-sec05-F013.front: If sirens catch you inside an intersection while clearing room for an emergency vehicle, what must you avoid doing?
sec05-card-sec05-F013.expected_back: Do not stop in an intersection when making room for an emergency vehicle.

sec05-card-sec05-F014.front: What does North Dakota require when you reach a crash scene with a parked emergency vehicle flashing its lights?
sec05-card-sec05-F014.expected_back: At a crash scene with a parked emergency vehicle displaying flashing lights, stop on the right; pass at your risk only when clear, obeying any officer directing traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F015.front: On an interstate or multilane highway, how must you react to a parked emergency, police, or NDDOT truck flashing emergency or work lights?
sec05-card-sec05-F015.expected_back: On an interstate or multilane highway, move to the opposite lane and use caution for a parked emergency, police or NDDOT maintenance vehicle displaying emergency or work lights.

sec05-card-sec05-F016.front: What do flashing yellow lights on tow trucks and slow-moving vehicles tell approaching drivers to do?
sec05-card-sec05-F016.expected_back: Flashing yellow lights on tow trucks and slow vehicles warn drivers to reduce speed.

sec05-card-sec05-F017.front: Which drivers must stop when a stopped school bus turns on its flashing red lights?
sec05-card-sec05-F017.expected_back: A stopped school bus showing flashing red lights requires approaching drivers in both directions to stop.

sec05-card-sec05-F018.front: Once you stop for a school bus with flashing red lights, which three signals let you start moving again?
sec05-card-sec05-F018.expected_back: After a school-bus stop, proceed only when the bus moves, the driver authorizes passage or the red lights stop flashing.

sec05-card-sec05-F019.front: What are flashing yellow caution lights on a school bus warning you is about to happen?
sec05-card-sec05-F019.expected_back: Yellow school-bus caution lights warn that the bus is preparing to stop and display red lights.

sec05-card-sec05-F020.front: Does a posted speed-limit sign guarantee that driving that fast is always safe and legal?
sec05-card-sec05-F020.expected_back: Drive below the posted maximum whenever conditions require a lower speed.

sec05-card-sec05-F021.front: Unless posted otherwise, what is North Dakota's speed limit when approaching a blind intersection or obstructed-view railroad crossing?
sec05-card-sec05-F021.expected_back: Unless signs state otherwise, the handbook gives twenty miles per hour for an obstructed-view railway approach or intersection approach.

sec05-card-sec05-F022.front: When no other speed is posted, what is the limit when passing a school — and during which student times does it apply?
sec05-card-sec05-F022.expected_back: Unless posted differently, the school-passing limit is twenty miles per hour during recess or while children arrive or leave at opening or closing.

sec05-card-sec05-F023.front: What is the unposted default speed limit in a North Dakota business or residential district?
sec05-card-sec05-F023.expected_back: The default business- or residential-district maximum is twenty-five miles per hour unless posted otherwise.

sec05-card-sec05-F024.front: Which two categories of North Dakota roads default to a fifty-five-mile-per-hour maximum when no different sign is posted?
sec05-card-sec05-F024.expected_back: The handbook gives fifty-five miles per hour for gravel, dirt and loose-surface roads unless otherwise signed, and for unsigned paved two-lane county or township roads.

sec05-card-sec05-F025.front: When can a rural paved two-lane highway in North Dakota have a sixty-five-mile-per-hour speed limit?
sec05-card-sec05-F025.expected_back: A rural paved two-lane highway may have a sixty-five-mile-per-hour maximum where posted for that speed.

sec05-card-sec05-F026.front: Unless posted otherwise, what are North Dakota's maximum speeds on paved divided multilane highways versus rural interstates?
sec05-card-sec05-F026.expected_back: Unless otherwise posted, paved divided multilane roads have a seventy-mile-per-hour maximum, and rural interstates have an eighty-mile-per-hour maximum.

sec05-card-sec05-F027.front: Before pulling out to pass another vehicle, what three questions plus sight-and-space check must you clear first?
sec05-card-sec05-F027.expected_back: Before passing, decide whether it is necessary, lawful and possible to finish with a clear view and sufficient room for approaching traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F028.front: When completing a pass on a two-way road, how much buffer must remain between you and any oncoming vehicle when you merge back?
sec05-card-sec05-F028.expected_back: After passing, return to your lane at least two hundred feet before reaching an oncoming vehicle.

sec05-card-sec05-F029.front: After overtaking a car, what visual check in your inside rearview mirror tells you it is safe to merge back?
sec05-card-sec05-F029.expected_back: Do not move back in after passing until the entire front of the passed vehicle appears in your inside mirror.

sec05-card-sec05-F030.front: Where must your tires stay while passing, and what are you forbidden to do when someone else passes you?
sec05-card-sec05-F030.expected_back: Stay on the main traveled road while passing, and never accelerate when another vehicle is passing you.

sec05-card-sec05-F031.front: Which road features, one-hundred-foot hazard buffers, and visibility conditions make passing strictly illegal?
sec05-card-sec05-F031.expected_back: Passing is forbidden near a hilltop or curve, within one hundred feet of an intersection, rail crossing or tunnel, in a marked no-passing area, or where weather obscures the view.

sec05-card-sec05-F032.front: What are the complete North Dakota steps for changing lanes safely on a multilane road?
sec05-card-sec05-F032.expected_back: For a lane change, signal, check mirrors and the shoulder blind spot, preserve safe spacing, and move just one lane at a time.

sec05-card-sec05-F033.front: Who carries the legal responsibility for a safe lane change, and what final step comes after merging in?
sec05-card-sec05-F033.expected_back: The driver changing lanes is responsible for doing so safely and should cancel the signal afterward.

sec05-card-sec05-F034.front: Roughly how many feet does the North Dakota handbook estimate it takes to stop from fifty-five miles per hour on dry pavement?
sec05-card-sec05-F034.expected_back: At fifty-five miles per hour on dry pavement, the handbook estimates about three hundred feet to stop.

sec05-card-sec05-F035.front: How do you measure the three-second following distance using a fixed roadside landmark?
sec05-card-sec05-F035.expected_back: For the three-second following check, time the gap from the leading vehicle's rear bumper passing a fixed point until your vehicle reaches it.

sec05-card-sec05-F036.front: What should you do if your car passes your chosen landmark before you finish counting three seconds?
sec05-card-sec05-F036.expected_back: If you reach the chosen point before three seconds elapse, increase the following gap.

sec05-card-sec05-F037.front: Which five road, vehicle, or traffic situations require stretching your following gap to four seconds or more?
sec05-card-sec05-F037.expected_back: Allow four seconds or more when roads are slippery, following motorcycles or view-blocking vehicles, carrying heavy loads or towing, or helping a following driver pass.

sec05-card-sec05-F038.front: What must you check before turning, and where should your car start and finish a right turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F038.expected_back: Before a turn, check both directions for vehicles and pedestrians; a right turn starts and finishes close to the right curb.

sec05-card-sec05-F039.front: When turning left from one one-way street onto another one-way street, which lane do you start from and where do you finish?
sec05-card-sec05-F039.expected_back: A left turn between one-way streets begins in the left lane and follows close to the left curb.

sec05-card-sec05-F040.front: When turning left from one two-way road onto another two-way road, where should your car approach before following the handbook turn path?
sec05-card-sec05-F040.expected_back: For a left turn between two-way roads, approach near the centerline and use the source diagram for the path into the destination roadway.

sec06-card-sec06-F001.front: When turning left from a two-way road onto a one-way street, where do you line up, where do you turn, and which lane do you enter?
sec06-card-sec06-F001.expected_back: For a left turn from a two-way road into a one-way street, approach near the centerline, turn before the intersection center and enter the one-way street's left lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F002.front: Which lane do you enter first when turning left from a two-way road onto a four-lane highway, and what should you do afterward?
sec06-card-sec06-F002.expected_back: A left turn from a two-way road into a four-lane highway enters the passing lane; move right when traffic makes that safe.

sec06-card-sec06-F003.front: In which direction does traffic circulate around the central island of a roundabout?
sec06-card-sec06-F003.expected_back: Roundabout traffic moves counterclockwise around the central island.

sec06-card-sec06-F004.front: How should you adjust your speed approaching a roundabout, and which three road users get the right-of-way before you enter?
sec06-card-sec06-F004.expected_back: Slow before a roundabout and yield to pedestrians, bicyclists and vehicles already circulating.

sec06-card-sec06-F005.front: When no special signs or pavement arrows say otherwise at a two-lane roundabout, which lane handles left turns, right turns, and going straight?
sec06-card-sec06-F005.expected_back: Unless signs or markings direct otherwise, use the left lane for a roundabout left turn, the right lane for a right turn and either lane for through movement.

sec06-card-sec06-F006.front: Once inside a roundabout, what is the rule on changing lanes and driving beside large trucks?
sec06-card-sec06-F006.memory_hook: Hold your lane, never pass trucks
sec06-card-sec06-F006.expected_back: Maintain your lane inside the roundabout and do not pass trucks, which may need all available space.

sec06-card-sec06-F007.front: What should you do if an emergency vehicle approaches before you enter a roundabout versus when you are already inside it?
sec06-card-sec06-F007.expected_back: Clear a roundabout for an emergency vehicle; do not enter when an emergency vehicle is approaching.

sec06-card-sec06-F008.front: Why is there a raised paved apron around the center island of a roundabout?
sec06-card-sec06-F008.expected_back: The roundabout's center apron provides space for the rear wheels of large trucks.

sec06-card-sec06-F009.front: Where do slower vehicles belong on the interstate, and what two things must you verify and do for every lane change?
sec06-card-sec06-F009.expected_back: On the interstate, slower drivers keep right and lane changes require both a signal and a clear destination lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F010.front: If your car has an emergency on the interstate, where must you pull over and how do you visibly signal for help?
sec06-card-sec06-F010.expected_back: For an interstate emergency, stop on the shoulder rather than in a travel lane, and raise the hood to signal trouble.

sec06-card-sec06-F011.front: You blow past your interstate exit. What is the only legal move, and which two shortcuts are strictly off-limits?
sec06-card-sec06-F011.expected_back: If you miss an interchange, continue to the next exit; never reverse or use a median crossover reserved for authorized vehicles.

sec06-card-sec06-F012.front: What should you do if you accidentally steer onto the wrong exit ramp on a freeway?
sec06-card-sec06-F012.expected_back: If you take the wrong exit, continue off the ramp and reenter by an entrance ramp; never back along a ramp.

sec06-card-sec06-F013.front: How should you use a freeway entrance ramp to join highway traffic, and when is the only time you stop?
sec06-card-sec06-F013.expected_back: Use an entrance ramp to match traffic speed and merge, stopping only if no gap is available.

sec06-card-sec06-F014.front: Who must yield when a vehicle on an entrance ramp merges onto the freeway, assuming no special signs apply?
sec06-card-sec06-F014.expected_back: An entering freeway vehicle yields to main-road traffic unless signs direct otherwise.

sec06-card-sec06-F015.front: Which two actions are banned once your vehicle is on a freeway exit ramp?
sec06-card-sec06-F015.expected_back: Do not stop or reverse on an exit ramp.

sec06-card-sec06-F016.front: During what daily window must your headlights be on in North Dakota — and when else outside those hours?
sec06-card-sec06-F016.expected_back: Use headlights between sunset and sunrise and whenever safe driving otherwise requires them.

sec06-card-sec06-F017.front: In rain, snow, fog, or other bad weather, how short does visibility get before North Dakota requires your headlights on?
sec06-card-sec06-F017.expected_back: During bad weather with visibility below one thousand feet, the handbook requires headlights.

sec06-card-sec06-F018.front: How do your headlight beams determine the fastest safe speed you can drive after dark?
sec06-card-sec06-F018.expected_back: At night, choose a speed permitting a stop within the distance illuminated by your headlights.

sec06-card-sec06-F019.front: What two quick cleaning habits cut nighttime glare and maximize how well your lights illuminate the road?
sec06-card-sec06-F019.expected_back: Clean both sides of the windshield to reduce glare and keep headlights clean for better illumination.

sec06-card-sec06-F020.front: Where should your eyes move while driving at night instead of locking onto the middle of your headlight beam?
sec06-card-sec06-F020.expected_back: Scan continuously at night for animals, walkers, cyclists and entering traffic rather than staring at the headlight beam's center.

sec06-card-sec06-F021.front: How should you handle speed in posted deer zones, and why should you resist yanking the wheel to dodge an animal?
sec06-card-sec06-F021.memory_hook: Slow down, brake straight, never swerve
sec06-card-sec06-F021.expected_back: Lower speed in deer-warning areas and avoid swerving around an animal, which may cause a worse crash.

sec06-card-sec06-F022.front: At what two distances must you dim your high beams — both for oncoming traffic and when following another car?
sec06-card-sec06-F022.memory_hook: Five hundred oncoming, three hundred behind
sec06-card-sec06-F022.expected_back: Change to low beams at least five hundred feet before meeting traffic and within three hundred feet behind another vehicle.

sec06-card-sec06-F023.front: Where should you shift your gaze if an oncoming driver forgets to dim their bright headlights?
sec06-card-sec06-F023.expected_back: If an approaching driver keeps bright beams on, look toward the road's right edge to reduce glare.

sec06-card-sec06-F024.front: What is the right call when drowsiness hits you during a nighttime drive?
sec06-card-sec06-F024.expected_back: Stop for rest when tired rather than continuing nighttime driving.

sec06-card-sec06-F025.front: How must your wheels be positioned and what is the maximum legal gap from the right curb when parallel parked?
sec06-card-sec06-F025.expected_back: For parallel parking, align the wheels with the curb and finish within one foot of its right-hand edge.

sec06-card-sec06-F026.front: Which way do you turn your front wheels when parking downhill next to a curb versus uphill next to a curb?
sec06-card-sec06-F026.expected_back: When parking downhill, aim the wheels toward the curb; uphill with a curb, aim them away from it.

sec06-card-sec06-F027.front: Which way do you turn your front wheels when parking uphill on a road that has no curb?
sec06-card-sec06-F027.expected_back: On an uphill grade without a curb, turn the wheels toward the shoulder.

sec06-card-sec06-F028.front: Before pulling out of a parked spot into the closest travel lane, what checks, signal, and right-of-way steps are required?
sec06-card-sec06-F028.expected_back: When leaving a parking place, check mirrors and over the shoulder, signal and yield to approaching vehicles before entering the nearest lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F029.front: Where should all four tires sit whenever space allows during a roadside emergency stop?
sec06-card-sec06-F029.expected_back: During an emergency stop, place all four wheels off the traveled pavement when possible.

sec06-card-sec06-F030.front: During what overnight window must a vehicle parked on a public highway show lights, what colors are required front and rear, and from how far away?
sec06-card-sec06-F030.expected_back: A vehicle parked on a public highway between half an hour after sunset and half an hour before sunrise needs a white or amber front light and a red rear light, visible from one thousand feet.

sec06-card-sec06-F031.front: Which four everyday street spots — involving walkways, property access, crossings, and double-parking — are always illegal for parking?
sec06-card-sec06-F031.expected_back: Do not park on a sidewalk, across a driveway, inside an intersection or alongside another parked vehicle.

sec06-card-sec06-F032.front: How many feet of clearance must you leave when parking near an intersection crosswalk or a fire hydrant?
sec06-card-sec06-F032.expected_back: Parking is prohibited on a crosswalk or within ten feet of an intersection crosswalk, and within ten feet of a fire hydrant.

sec06-card-sec06-F033.front: At least how far back must you park from a roadside stop sign, traffic light, or flashing beacon?
sec06-card-sec06-F033.expected_back: Keep parked vehicles at least fifteen feet from roadside stop signs, traffic signals and flashing beacons.

sec06-card-sec06-F034.front: What elevated structures, underground passages, work-zone hazards, and posted areas are completely off-limits for parking?
sec06-card-sec06-F034.expected_back: Do not park on bridges or overpasses, in tunnels or underpasses, beside excavations where traffic is blocked, or where an official sign prohibits parking.

sec06-card-sec06-F035.front: What credentials are required to use an accessible stall, and what is the rule for the striped diagonal zone next to it?
sec06-card-sec06-F035.expected_back: Accessible parking requires the proper placard or plate; the diagonal access area beside the space must remain clear.

sec06-card-sec06-F036.front: Where along the curb is parking banned around a pedestrian safety zone, including the distance past its ends?
sec06-card-sec06-F036.expected_back: Do not park between a pedestrian safety zone and the adjacent curb, or within fifteen feet of the curb points opposite the zone's ends.

sec06-card-sec06-F037.front: How does pulling a trailer change your braking needs, and how should you adjust when gusty winds pick up?
sec06-card-sec06-F037.expected_back: A trailer increases stopping distance, and strong winds are a reason to reduce towing speed.

sec06-card-sec06-F038.front: Above what speed must a towed trailer have safety chains or breakaway brakes capable of holding it if the hitch separates?
sec06-card-sec06-F038.expected_back: Above twenty-five miles per hour, a trailer needs safety chains or brakes able to hold it if the coupling fails.

sec06-card-sec06-F039.front: What rear lights and reflectors are required on the back of a trailer, and how far back must its taillights show?
sec06-card-sec06-F039.expected_back: Trailer rear equipment includes turn and brake lights, two red reflectors and two red taillights visible from one thousand feet.

sec06-card-sec06-F040.front: At what width must a trailer carry clearance lamps, and what colors go on the front versus the back?
sec06-card-sec06-F040.memory_hook: Eighty inches: amber front, red rear
sec06-card-sec06-F040.expected_back: A trailer at least eighty inches wide needs two amber front clearance lamps and two red rear clearance lamps.

sec06-card-sec06-F041.front: At least how far behind your vehicle must your rearview mirror let you see clearly?
sec06-card-sec06-F041.expected_back: A vehicle must have a mirror giving at least two hundred feet of rearward view.

sec06-card-sec06-F042.front: What two core safety standards must every towing hitch connection meet before you pull onto the road?
sec06-card-sec06-F042.expected_back: A towing connection must be strong and designed to prevent accidental separation.

sec06-card-sec06-F043.front: Is it legal in North Dakota to shift your transmission into neutral and coast down a hill?
sec06-card-sec06-F043.expected_back: Coasting downhill with the transmission in neutral is prohibited.

sec07-card-sec07-F001.front: When driving a truck or bus down a hill, what must the driver never do with the clutch?
sec07-card-sec07-F001.expected_back: Truck and bus drivers must not descend a grade with the clutch disengaged.

sec07-card-sec07-F002.front: Before putting your vehicle in reverse, what physical check should you do outside the car and what three things are you looking for?
sec07-card-sec07-F002.expected_back: Before reversing, walk around the vehicle to check for children, obstacles and available clearance.

sec07-card-sec07-F003.front: When you back out toward a street or travel lane, who carries the responsibility for avoiding traffic interference and entering safely?
sec07-card-sec07-F003.expected_back: The backing driver must avoid interfering with traffic and is responsible for entering a traffic lane safely.

sec07-card-sec07-F004.front: How big is the North Dakota fine for tossing trash or litter onto a public highway?
sec07-card-sec07-F004.expected_back: The handbook states a five-hundred-dollar fine for depositing litter on a public highway.

sec07-card-sec07-F005.front: Which crashes must be reported right away in North Dakota, and which law-enforcement agency do you call inside versus outside city limits?
sec07-card-sec07-F005.expected_back: Immediately report a crash causing at least four thousand dollars in combined damage, or any injury or death, to city police within a city or the highway patrol or county sheriff outside it.

sec07-card-sec07-F006.front: Right after a crash with injury or property damage, what four pieces of information must drivers swap at the scene?
sec07-card-sec07-F006.expected_back: After an injury or property-damage crash, exchange driver names, addresses, insurance companies and policy numbers.

sec07-card-sec07-F007.front: Suppose a borrower is hurt in a crash and cannot report it. How soon after finding out must the vehicle's owner file the crash notice and insurance info?
sec07-card-sec07-F007.expected_back: If an incapacitated driver is not the vehicle owner, the owner must provide the missing crash notice and insurance details within five days after learning of the crash.

sec07-card-sec07-F008.front: You bump an empty parked car in a lot. What must you try first, and what three details go on a visible note if you cannot find the owner?
sec07-card-sec07-F008.expected_back: After striking an unattended vehicle, locate and notify its owner immediately; if that is impossible, leave a conspicuous note with your name, address and insurer.

sec07-card-sec07-F009.front: What insurance coverage is mandatory to drive in North Dakota, and what two details must you give an officer when asked?
sec07-card-sec07-F009.expected_back: Driving requires an effective liability policy, and the driver must provide the insurer's name and policy number when an officer requests them.

sec07-card-sec07-F010.front: What are the North Dakota fines for a first uninsured-driving offense versus a repeat offense within three years — plus the license risk?
sec07-card-sec07-F010.expected_back: The handbook lists uninsured-driving fines of one hundred fifty dollars for a first violation and three hundred dollars for a further violation within three years, with possible suspension.

sec07-card-sec07-F011.front: After a no-insurance conviction, how long must you prove coverage, what happens to your license, and what two fees apply?
sec07-card-sec07-F011.expected_back: After a no-insurance conviction, the handbook requires insurance proof for one year and a restricted replacement license, with fifty-dollar fees both for that replacement and for later removing the restriction.

sec07-card-sec07-F012.front: On North Dakota highways, when do you dial nine-one-one versus five-one-one?
sec07-card-sec07-F012.expected_back: Use nine-one-one for emergency highway assistance and five-one-one for weather or road-condition information.

sec07-card-sec07-F013.front: If a North Dakota highway is officially closed for hazardous conditions, can you drive around the gate, and what is the fine?
sec07-card-sec07-F013.expected_back: A road officially closed for hazardous conditions must not be entered; the handbook states a two-hundred-fifty-dollar penalty.

sec07-card-sec07-F014.front: Before pulling out in winter, what two visibility steps come first, and why should you beware of spraying washer fluid in extreme cold?
sec07-card-sec07-F014.expected_back: Clear window ice and let the defroster warm up before winter driving; washer fluid can freeze across the windshield in extreme cold.

sec07-card-sec07-F015.front: How can you safely gauge road slickness early in a drive, and what should you do once you feel how much grip you have?
sec07-card-sec07-F015.expected_back: At low speed, gently check braking traction and adjust driving speed to the available grip.

sec07-card-sec07-F016.front: Even if your car has winter tires or tire chains on, what two driving adjustments are still required on snow and ice?
sec07-card-sec07-F016.expected_back: Winter tires or chains do not remove the need to slow down and double the normal following gap.

sec07-card-sec07-F017.front: Between which exact dates are studded snow tires legal to run on North Dakota roads?
sec07-card-sec07-F017.expected_back: The handbook allows studded snow tires from October fifteenth through April fifteenth.

sec07-card-sec07-F018.front: When a passing truck kicks up a blinding cloud of loose snow, how should you respond and what two things must you watch?
sec07-card-sec07-F018.expected_back: Passing trucks can create a cloud of snow that sharply reduces visibility; reduce speed and watch the road and following traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F019.front: Which two parts of a roadway ice over earlier and stay slick longer than the open pavement around them?
sec07-card-sec07-F019.expected_back: Bridges and shaded pavement freeze sooner and stay icy longer than nearby roadway.

sec07-card-sec07-F020.front: When stopping hard in a vehicle equipped with antilock brakes, how should your foot work the brake pedal?
sec07-card-sec07-F020.expected_back: With antilock brakes, maintain firm continuous pedal pressure instead of pumping or repeatedly releasing the pedal.

sec07-card-sec07-F021.front: What four specific winter emergency items does the North Dakota handbook tell drivers to keep in the vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-F021.expected_back: Carry winter emergency supplies, including warm clothes, footwear, a shovel and energy food.

sec07-card-sec07-F022.front: If a blizzard strands your car on a North Dakota road, should you hike out for help or stay put?
sec07-card-sec07-F022.expected_back: When stranded in a snowstorm, remain with the vehicle rather than wandering away.

sec07-card-sec07-F023.front: Why must you stay well back from a working snowplow — what three sudden actions can it take, and where is its blind spot?
sec07-card-sec07-F023.expected_back: Keep well behind a snowplow because it may stop, reverse or throw sanding material, and its driver cannot see directly behind it.

sec07-card-sec07-F024.front: On a multilane highway, which parts of the road might a snowplow be working in, and what must you confirm before moving past?
sec07-card-sec07-F024.expected_back: On a multilane road, a plow may occupy either lane or the shoulder, so establish its location before proceeding.

sec07-card-sec07-F025.front: What can a heavy snowdrift suddenly do to a moving snowplow, and what does that mean if you pass?
sec07-card-sec07-F025.expected_back: Snowdrifts can push a plow sideways; passing it requires exceptional caution.

sec07-card-sec07-F026.front: What should you do instead of driving straight into a blinding snow whiteout ahead of you?
sec07-card-sec07-F026.expected_back: Do not drive into a snow whiteout; wait until visibility returns and a safe opportunity exists to pass.

sec07-card-sec07-F027.front: Why can a winter road that looks freshly sanded still turn out to be dangerously slick underneath your tires?
sec07-card-sec07-F027.expected_back: A road that looks sanded may still be slick because sand can sink into packed snow.

sec07-card-sec07-F028.front: What is your primary defense against losing traction and skidding when roads turn slick?
sec07-card-sec07-F028.expected_back: Reduce speed on slippery roads to lower the risk of a skid.

sec07-card-sec07-F029.front: In a rear-wheel-drive skid, what three actions with the brakes, gas pedal, and steering wheel bring the car back inline?
sec07-card-sec07-F029.expected_back: For the handbook's rear-wheel-drive skid procedure, stay off the brakes, ease off acceleration gradually and steer in the direction the rear is sliding.

sec07-card-sec07-F030.front: Why are the first minutes of a fresh rainstorm extra slick compared to pavement after a long steady wash?
sec07-card-sec07-F030.expected_back: New rain combines with road oil and dirt to create an especially slippery surface.

sec07-card-sec07-F031.front: What happens between your tires and the pavement when your vehicle starts hydroplaning?
sec07-card-sec07-F031.expected_back: Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on water rather than contacting the road.

sec07-card-sec07-F032.front: What two hazards rise simultaneously in rainy weather, and what two habits must you bring to match them?
sec07-card-sec07-F032.expected_back: Rain reduces visibility and raises skid risk, requiring slower speed and close attention.

sec07-card-sec07-F033.front: Water is covering the road ahead, though it looks shallow from the driver's seat. What is the right move?
sec07-card-sec07-F033.expected_back: Turn around rather than drive across a flooded road, even when the water looks shallow.

sec07-card-sec07-F034.front: Why can you never trust how shallow floodwater looks over a submerged stretch of road?
sec07-card-sec07-F034.expected_back: Floodwater can conceal dips or a washed-out road foundation, making apparent depth unreliable.

sec07-card-sec07-F035.front: How little standing water does it take to hit the underside of most passenger cars and stall the engine or kill control?
sec07-card-sec07-F035.expected_back: The handbook warns that six inches of water can reach most passenger cars' underside and cause stalling or loss of control.

sec07-card-sec07-F036.front: What depth of moving floodwater is strong enough to float and sweep away most vehicles, even pickups and sport-utility vehicles?
sec07-card-sec07-F036.expected_back: Two feet of moving water can sweep away most vehicles, including pickups and sport-utility vehicles, according to the handbook.

sec07-card-sec07-F037.front: If rising floodwater cuts off the only road out and no detour exists, where should you go and what do you do?
sec07-card-sec07-F037.expected_back: When floodwater blocks the only route, go to higher ground and wait for it to recede.

sec07-card-sec07-F038.front: Besides a thumping sound, how can you tell a front-tire blowout apart from a rear-tire failure by how the car moves?
sec07-card-sec07-F038.expected_back: A tire failure may produce thumping; front-tire failure pulls toward the damaged side, while a rear failure may cause swaying.

sec07-card-sec07-F039.front: A tire blows at highway speed. What is the safe sequence for steering, gas, brakes, and pulling onto the shoulder?
sec07-card-sec07-F039.expected_back: After a blowout, grip the wheel, steer straight and ease off acceleration; wait for full control before braking, then move to the shoulder when nearly stopped.

sec07-card-sec07-F040.front: Your right wheels slip off the pavement edge onto a low shoulder. What mistake must you avoid, and how do you re-enter safely?
sec07-card-sec07-F040.expected_back: If a tire drops onto the shoulder, do not swerve back; ease off acceleration, regain control, check behind, signal and return gently.

sec07-card-sec07-F041.front: Your headlights suddenly cut out at night. Which other lights should you try right away as you slow down and exit the road?
sec07-card-sec07-F041.expected_back: If headlights fail, try parking lights and turn signals, slow down and leave the roadway as soon as possible.

sec07-card-sec07-F042.front: If your gas pedal sticks down while driving, how do you cut power to the wheels — and what ignition mistake must you never make?
sec07-card-sec07-F042.expected_back: For a stuck accelerator, disengage the clutch or select neutral and steer off safely; never select the ignition-lock position while moving.

sec07-card-sec07-F043.front: If you shut the engine off while your vehicle is still rolling, which two critical control systems can suddenly lose power assist?
sec07-card-sec07-F043.expected_back: Switching off the engine can remove power assistance for steering and brakes.

sec07-card-sec07-F044.front: How should you handle speed, braking, and steering when crossing potholes, ruts, broken asphalt, or loose gravel?
sec07-card-sec07-F044.expected_back: Slow for ruts, holes, broken pavement and gravel, avoiding abrupt braking or steering.

sec07-card-sec07-F045.front: A car drifts across the centerline straight into your lane. What do you do first, and where do you escape if it keeps coming?
sec07-card-sec07-F045.expected_back: If an oncoming vehicle enters your lane, slow and flash headlights; if it continues, move right and leave the road or stop on the far-right shoulder when conditions permit.

sec07-card-sec07-F046.front: Is texting behind the wheel allowed in North Dakota, and what dollar penalty does the handbook list for distracting activity that impairs control?
sec07-card-sec07-F046.expected_back: Texting while driving is prohibited, and the handbook lists a one-hundred-dollar penalty for the described distracting activity that impairs safe control.

sec07-card-sec07-F047.front: How many hands belong on the wheel, why should one foot work both pedals, and what mechanical damage does two-foot driving cause?
sec07-card-sec07-F047.expected_back: Hold the wheel with both hands, using one foot for accelerator and brake to avoid riding and overheating the brakes.

sec07-card-sec07-F048.front: When drowsiness hits behind the wheel, what is the safe remedy rather than pushing onward tired?
sec07-card-sec07-F048.expected_back: Sleep is the safe remedy for sleepiness behind the wheel; continuing tired increases collision risk.

sec08-card-sec08-F001.front: What seven physical and driving warning signs tell you fatigue is setting in behind the wheel?
sec08-card-sec08-F001.expected_back: Fatigue warnings include trouble focusing, missing recent-mile memories, lane drift, missed signs, unusual tailgating, repeated yawning and a nodding head.

sec08-card-sec08-F002.front: Even on dry pavement, how much distance can a loaded tractor-trailer need to come to a complete stop?
sec08-card-sec08-F002.expected_back: A loaded tractor-trailer can need more than four hundred feet to stop on dry pavement.

sec08-card-sec08-F003.front: How do a long truck's rear wheels track compared to its front wheels, and why might it swing left first?
sec08-card-sec08-F003.expected_back: A long vehicle's rear wheels take a shorter path than its front wheels, so a truck may first move left before turning right.

sec08-card-sec08-F004.front: Before you ever pass a truck on its right side, what two things must you check first?
sec08-card-sec08-F004.expected_back: Before passing a truck on the right, observe its signal and determine whether its initial leftward movement is preparation for a right turn.

sec08-card-sec08-F005.front: Where are a large truck's major blind areas located, and does the driver's high cab seat get rid of them?
sec08-card-sec08-F005.expected_back: Trucks have substantial blind areas beside the cab, immediately ahead and behind; a high driving position does not eliminate them.

sec08-card-sec08-F006.front: When driving near a large truck, how can you tell at a glance whether the trucker can see your car?
sec08-card-sec08-F006.expected_back: If the truck driver is not visible in the truck's side mirror, assume the driver cannot see your vehicle.

sec08-card-sec08-F007.front: What two dangerous habits around a truck's sides and front buffer should you avoid, especially near exits or narrow work zones?
sec08-card-sec08-F007.expected_back: Avoid lingering alongside a truck or cutting into its forward safety gap to reach an exit or narrow work zone.

sec08-card-sec08-F008.front: Which side should you use to pass a tractor-trailer, and how should you pace the pass once you start?
sec08-card-sec08-F008.expected_back: When passing a tractor-trailer, use the left and complete the maneuver rather than remaining beside it.

sec08-card-sec08-F009.front: Which three everyday maneuvers require noticeably more space for a large truck than for a passenger car?
sec08-card-sec08-F009.expected_back: A truck needs more room to stop, accelerate and turn than a passenger car.

sec08-card-sec08-F010.front: Why do drivers frequently misjudge how fast an oncoming truck is closing in before pulling out?
sec08-card-sec08-F010.expected_back: Do not underestimate an approaching truck's speed because its size can make it appear slower or farther away.

sec08-card-sec08-F011.front: Outside city limits on an interstate or multilane highway, how must you respond to a stranded car flashing its hazard lights?
sec08-card-sec08-F011.expected_back: For a stranded vehicle with flashing hazards on an interstate or multilane highway outside city limits, move safely into a nonadjacent lane; if that cannot be done, reduce speed and proceed cautiously.

sec08-card-sec08-F012.front: Can a passenger vehicle share part of a lane alongside a motorcycle, or how much lane width does the rider get?
sec08-card-sec08-F012.expected_back: Give a motorcycle the entire lane instead of attempting to drive beside it within that lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F013.front: Why is it harder to judge an approaching motorcycle's distance and speed compared to a full-size car?
sec08-card-sec08-F013.expected_back: A motorcycle's small profile can make its approach speed and distance difficult to judge.

sec08-card-sec08-F014.front: At which two driving moments does the handbook specifically warn you to check mirrors and blind spots for motorcycles?
sec08-card-sec08-F014.expected_back: Check mirrors and blind spots for motorcycles before changing lanes and when approaching intersections.

sec08-card-sec08-F015.front: An approaching motorcycle has its turn signal blinking. Why must you wait before pulling out in front of it?
sec08-card-sec08-F015.expected_back: Do not rely solely on a motorcycle's flashing indicator; wait to confirm the rider is actually turning.

sec08-card-sec08-F016.front: Which five road-surface hazards can force a motorcyclist ahead of you to suddenly change speed or shift lane position?
sec08-card-sec08-F016.expected_back: Potholes, gravel, slippery surfaces, seams and railway crossings may cause a rider to alter speed or lane position abruptly.

sec08-card-sec08-F017.front: How many seconds of following distance should you keep behind a motorcycle so you both have room for sudden moves?
sec08-card-sec08-F017.expected_back: The motorcycle-sharing advice calls for a three- or four-second following interval to allow emergency maneuvering.

sec08-card-sec08-F018.front: When overtaking a bicyclist, what speed adjustment and minimum side clearance are required — and when must you wait?
sec08-card-sec08-F018.expected_back: Slow near bicyclists and provide at least three feet of passing clearance, passing only when traffic and road conditions permit.

sec08-card-sec08-F019.front: After you pass a cyclist, how should you check before moving back right, and when do riders need even wider space?
sec08-card-sec08-F019.expected_back: After passing a bicyclist, check over the shoulder before returning to normal road position, giving additional clearance in bad weather.
