sec08-card-sec08-F020.front: Where should you watch extra closely for cyclists, and what specific check prevents cutting one off on a right turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F020.expected_back: Watch especially for bicyclists at intersections and check the blind spot before turning right.

sec08-card-sec08-F021.front: Under what single driving situation may your car use a marked bicycle lane, and what two steps come before entering it?
sec08-card-sec08-F021.expected_back: Use a bicycle lane only as needed for a safe right turn, signaling and looking before entering it.

sec08-card-sec08-F022.front: Why are young riders on bicycles extra hazardous to drive near, and what two adjustments should you make?
sec08-card-sec08-F022.expected_back: Children cycling may be difficult to see and unpredictable; expect sudden actions and reduce speed.

sec08-card-sec08-F023.front: During a collision or sudden swerve, what two protective jobs does a fastened seat belt perform for everyone inside?
sec08-card-sec08-F023.expected_back: Seat belts help retain occupants within the vehicle and in proper driving or riding position during a crash.

sec08-card-sec08-F024.front: Where should the lap strap and shoulder strap sit on your body, and how tight should the belt be?
sec08-card-sec08-F024.expected_back: Position a lap belt snugly low over the hips and the shoulder section across the chest and collarbone with minimal slack.

sec08-card-sec08-F025.front: If an older car slides a motorized shoulder strap into place automatically, what must you still buckle by hand?
sec08-card-sec08-F025.expected_back: An automatic shoulder belt still requires its separate lap belt to be fastened manually.

sec08-card-sec08-F026.front: Which seats inside a vehicle require occupants to wear a seat belt according to the North Dakota handbook?
sec08-card-sec08-F026.expected_back: The handbook requires seat belts for occupants in every seating position.

sec08-card-sec08-F027.front: If your vehicle has front and side airbags, can you skip buckling your lap-and-shoulder belt?
sec08-card-sec08-F027.expected_back: Airbags supplement seat belts; they do not replace the lap-and-shoulder restraint.

sec08-card-sec08-F028.front: Under what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster in North Dakota — and what height exception lets them use a regular belt early?
sec08-card-sec08-F028.expected_back: Children younger than eight require an appropriate car seat or booster, except that a child at least fifty-seven inches tall may use a seat belt instead.

sec08-card-sec08-F029.front: What is North Dakota's restraint rule for kids and teens ages eight through seventeen?
sec08-card-sec08-F029.expected_back: Children eight through seventeen must use a seat belt or child restraint correctly.

sec08-card-sec08-F030.front: What fine and driving-record penalty does the North Dakota handbook state for breaking the child-passenger restraint law?
sec08-card-sec08-F030.expected_back: The handbook gives a twenty-five-dollar fine and one license point for violating its child-passenger restraint law.

sec08-card-sec08-F031.front: How should a child safety seat and harness fit, and which two instruction guides must you follow when installing it?
sec08-card-sec08-F031.expected_back: Install the restraint tightly and secure the child snugly, following both the seat manufacturer's instructions and the vehicle manual.

sec08-card-sec08-F032.front: Under what age should kids sit in the back row, and what is the strict rule on rear-facing infant seats and front airbags?
sec08-card-sec08-F032.expected_back: Children younger than thirteen should ride in a rear seat, and a rear-facing infant seat must never face an active front airbag.

sec08-card-sec08-F033.front: What minimum age and minimum weight must a child meet together before moving up into a booster seat?
sec08-card-sec08-F033.expected_back: The handbook's booster-transition advice requires both at least four years of age and a weight of at least forty pounds.

sec08-card-sec08-F034.front: What two unsafe shortcuts with pickup trucks and seat belts must you never allow with child passengers?
sec08-card-sec08-F034.expected_back: Do not let children ride in a pickup cargo area or share one seat belt between two children.

sec09-card-sec09-F001.front: What quick habit must you perform every single time before locking your parked vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F001.expected_back: Before locking a parked vehicle, check the back seat for children.

sec09-card-sec09-F002.front: Even at home in the driveway, what two precautions keep children from climbing into a parked car alone?
sec09-card-sec09-F002.expected_back: Keep parked vehicles locked and keys inaccessible to children so they cannot enter unattended.

sec09-card-sec09-F003.front: Is a quick two-minute errand ever okay with a child left alone in the car — and what if you spot one?
sec09-card-sec09-F003.expected_back: Take action when a child is alone inside a vehicle; never leave a child unattended in a vehicle even briefly.

sec09-card-sec09-F004.front: Which three core driving abilities does alcohol impair, and what happens to that impairment as someone drinks more?
sec09-card-sec09-F004.expected_back: Alcohol impairs reactions, vision and concentration; greater consumption increases impairment.

sec09-card-sec09-F005.front: Which three factors determine how high a person's alcohol concentration climbs?
sec09-card-sec09-F005.expected_back: Alcohol concentration depends on the amount of alcohol, the time over which it is consumed and the person's lean body weight.

sec09-card-sec09-F006.front: Why can you never judge how much alcohol you consumed just by looking at the size of a mixed drink?
sec09-card-sec09-F006.expected_back: Mixed-drink alcohol content varies, so the apparent size of a drink does not establish its alcohol dose.

sec09-card-sec09-F007.front: What actually clears alcohol from your bloodstream — and do coffee, workouts, or cold showers speed it up?
sec09-card-sec09-F007.expected_back: Only time eliminates alcohol from the bloodstream; coffee, cold showers and exercise do not speed that process.

sec09-card-sec09-F008.front: How does alcohol trick a driver's brain when evaluating risky road situations?
sec09-card-sec09-F008.expected_back: Alcohol can dull judgment and create unwarranted confidence, making hazardous situations appear less dangerous.

sec09-card-sec09-F009.front: Under North Dakota implied consent, what substances are tested and which four body samples can officers require?
sec09-card-sec09-F009.expected_back: North Dakota's implied-consent rule covers chemical testing for alcohol or drugs using blood, breath, urine or saliva.

sec09-card-sec09-F010.front: For how long can North Dakota revoke your license if you refuse either the roadside screening breath test or the chemical test?
sec09-card-sec09-F010.expected_back: The handbook gives a revocation range of one hundred eighty days to three years for refusing the chemical test or the roadside preliminary breath test.

sec09-card-sec09-F011.front: What is North Dakota's alcohol-concentration threshold for adult drivers versus drivers under age twenty-one?
sec09-card-sec09-F011.expected_back: The handbook identifies an alcohol-concentration threshold of zero point zero eight percent generally and zero point zero two percent for drivers younger than twenty-one.

sec09-card-sec09-F012.front: How do administrative licensing action and criminal court conviction relate in a North Dakota DUI case?
sec09-card-sec09-F012.expected_back: Administrative licensing action and court conviction are separate DUI processes, and driving privileges may be suspended through either or both.

sec09-card-sec09-F013.front: On a first alcohol-concentration offense in seven years, how long is the standard license suspension — and what doubles it to one hundred eighty days?
sec09-card-sec09-F013.expected_back: For a first alcohol-concentration offense within seven years, the handbook states a ninety-one-day suspension, increasing to one hundred eighty days for a concentration of zero point one eight percent or more.

sec09-card-sec09-F014.front: If a driver gets a second alcohol-concentration offense within seven years, what are the base and elevated suspension lengths?
sec09-card-sec09-F014.memory_hook: Second offense: one or two years
sec09-card-sec09-F014.expected_back: For a second offense within seven years, the stated suspension is three hundred sixty-five days, or two years at an alcohol concentration of zero point one eight percent or higher.

sec09-card-sec09-F015.front: What suspension lengths apply to a third or subsequent offense within seven years — both standard and at zero point one eight percent or above?
sec09-card-sec09-F015.memory_hook: Third offense: two or three years
sec09-card-sec09-F015.expected_back: For a third or later offense within seven years, the handbook gives a two-year suspension, extended to three years at zero point one eight percent or higher.

sec09-card-sec09-F016.front: How many days of suspension must pass before you can seek a restricted license — normally versus inside the twenty-four-seven sobriety program?
sec09-card-sec09-F016.memory_hook: Thirty days, or fourteen in sobriety
sec09-card-sec09-F016.expected_back: The handbook describes restricted-license eligibility after at least thirty suspension days, or at least fourteen days with participation in the twenty-four-seven sobriety program.

sec09-card-sec09-F017.front: What minimum jail time and maximum fine hit a driver caught driving while suspended or revoked for an alcohol violation?
sec09-card-sec09-F017.expected_back: Driving while suspended or revoked after an alcohol violation carries a stated minimum of four jail days and a fine up to one thousand dollars.

sec09-card-sec09-F018.front: Besides your driver license, what items from your vehicle can be impounded during an alcohol-related suspension or revocation?
sec09-card-sec09-F018.expected_back: Vehicle plates and registration may be impounded for the duration of an alcohol-related suspension or revocation.

sec09-card-sec09-F019.front: What is the base court-conviction fine stated in the North Dakota handbook for a first DUI?
sec09-card-sec09-F019.expected_back: The handbook's first DUI court-conviction fine is five hundred dollars.

sec09-card-sec09-F020.front: At zero point one six percent or higher on a first DUI conviction, what minimum fine and jail sentence kick in — and how can jail be served?
sec09-card-sec09-F020.expected_back: For a first conviction with concentration at least zero point one six percent, the handbook lists at least a seven-hundred-fifty-dollar fine and two jail days, with imprisonment convertible to community service.

sec09-card-sec09-F021.front: What fine, jail sentence, and mandatory sobriety-program term come with a second DUI conviction within seven years?
sec09-card-sec09-F021.memory_hook: Thousand fine, ten days, year sobriety
sec09-card-sec09-F021.expected_back: A second conviction within seven years carries the stated one-thousand-dollar fine, ten jail days and at least twelve months of the twenty-four-seven sobriety program as a probation condition.

sec11-card-sec11-F001.front: How do traffic tickets affect your North Dakota driving record, and what determines how many points a ticket adds?
sec11-card-sec11-F001.memory_hook: Serious violations stack higher record points
sec11-card-sec11-F001.expected_back: Traffic violations add points to the driver's record, with more serious violations assigned higher values.

sec11-card-sec11-F002.front: At what point total does North Dakota send a notice of intended suspension and offer an administrative hearing?
sec11-card-sec11-F002.expected_back: A total of twelve or more points triggers notice of intended suspension and an opportunity for an administrative hearing.

sec11-card-sec11-F003.front: How many suspension days do you get at twelve points, and how is the length calculated at higher point totals?
sec11-card-sec11-F003.memory_hook: Seven days per point over eleven
sec11-card-sec11-F003.expected_back: The handbook's point schedule gives seven suspension days at twelve points and seven days for each point above eleven at higher totals.

sec11-card-sec11-F004.front: How long must you go without any newly recorded points to shave one point off your North Dakota record?
sec11-card-sec11-F004.memory_hook: Three clean months drops one point
sec11-card-sec11-F004.expected_back: One point can be removed for each three-month period without newly recorded points.

sec11-card-sec11-F005.front: How many points can you knock off your driving record by finishing an approved driver-improvement course?
sec11-card-sec11-F005.memory_hook: Approved improvement course cuts three points
sec11-card-sec11-F005.expected_back: Completing an approved driver-improvement course can reduce the record by three points.

sec11-card-sec11-F006.front: When can you choose a driver-improvement class instead of taking ticket points, how often, and what combo is barred?
sec11-card-sec11-F006.memory_hook: Five-point max yearly, never stack reductions
sec11-card-sec11-F006.expected_back: For a violation worth five points or fewer, a driver may elect an improvement course instead of points once per twelve months, without combining that option with the separate three-point course reduction.

sec11-card-sec11-F007.front: What happens if the parent or guardian who sponsored a minor's application withdraws their consent?
sec11-card-sec11-F007.memory_hook: Sponsor pulls consent, license gets canceled
sec11-card-sec11-F007.expected_back: A parent or guardian who sponsored a minor may withdraw consent at any time, causing cancellation of the permit or license.

sec11-card-sec11-F008.front: If parental consent was withdrawn and canceled a teen's license, what two paths let that teen drive legally again?
sec11-card-sec11-F008.memory_hook: Renewed parent consent or turning eighteen
sec11-card-sec11-F008.expected_back: After consent is withdrawn, a teen may regain driving authorization with renewed parental consent or upon reaching eighteen.

sec11-card-sec11-F009.front: Which five common new-driver risks should parents watch out for while coaching a teen behind the wheel?
sec11-card-sec11-F009.memory_hook: Watch speed, gaps, tailgating, distractions, inexperience
sec11-card-sec11-F009.expected_back: Parents should anticipate risks such as speeding, poor gap choices, tailgating, distractions and limited experience when coaching a teen.

sec11-card-sec11-F010.front: Why should parents keep riding along for supervised practice even after a teen passes driver ed and gets licensed?
sec11-card-sec11-F010.memory_hook: Driver ed starts learning, keep coaching
sec11-card-sec11-F010.expected_back: Continue supervised practice after licensing; formal driver education begins the learning process rather than completing it.

sec11-card-sec11-F011.front: Who should be in the car during early practice drives, and what tone should those sessions keep?
sec11-card-sec11-F011.memory_hook: Parent and teen only, stay calm
sec11-card-sec11-F011.expected_back: At first, practice with just the parent and teen to reduce distractions, keeping the session calm and focused.

sec11-card-sec11-F012.front: Which three foundational car-control maneuvers should a beginner master before tackling lane changes and highway merges?
sec11-card-sec11-F012.memory_hook: Park, reverse, turn before merging lanes
sec11-card-sec11-F012.expected_back: Begin with parking, reversing and turning before progressing to more complex lane-changing or merging skills.

sec11-card-sec11-F013.front: Under what lighting and weather conditions should teen practice start before working up to tougher conditions?
sec11-card-sec11-F013.memory_hook: Start clear daylight, add conditions gradually
sec11-card-sec11-F013.expected_back: Start practice in daylight and good weather, gradually introducing other weather, road types and times of day as skill improves.

sec11-card-sec11-F014.front: In what order of locations should practice drives step up from lowest risk to heavier traffic?
sec11-card-sec11-F014.memory_hook: Empty lots, quiet streets, then highways
sec11-card-sec11-F014.expected_back: Begin in low-risk areas such as empty lots or quiet roads, progressing toward neighborhoods and then busier highways.

sec11-card-sec11-F015.front: What four personal and scheduling conditions should both parent and teen meet before starting a practice drive?
sec11-card-sec11-F015.memory_hook: Rested, ready, good mood, enough time
sec11-card-sec11-F015.expected_back: Practice when both participants are rested, ready, in a suitable mood and have enough time.

sec11-card-sec11-F016.front: What four cabin adjustments come before shifting out of park, and when does the coaching checklist advise running headlights?
sec11-card-sec11-F016.memory_hook: Adjust cabin, buckle up, headlights always
sec11-card-sec11-F016.expected_back: Before moving, adjust the seat, mirrors, belts and steering position; the coaching checklist recommends belt use and headlights by day and night.

sec11-card-sec11-F017.front: At which two everyday intersection situations does the coaching checklist stress coming to a complete stop?
sec11-card-sec11-F017.memory_hook: Full stop at signs and red-rights
sec11-card-sec11-F017.expected_back: During practice, make complete stops at stop signs and before permitted right turns on red.

sec11-card-sec11-F018.front: How often should a teen check mirrors and surrounding traffic during practice instead of staring straight ahead?
sec11-card-sec11-F018.memory_hook: Scan mirrors every six to eight
sec11-card-sec11-F018.expected_back: The coaching checklist advises scanning mirrors and surrounding traffic every six to eight seconds while keeping the eyes moving.

sec11-card-sec11-F019.front: What following-time cushion and lane placement does North Dakota's family practice guide recommend?
sec11-card-sec11-F019.expected_back: The family practice guidance recommends a three- to four-second traffic gap and maintaining the vehicle near the lane's center.

sec11-card-sec11-F020.front: How can you tell right away whether your car is hiding inside a large truck's blind spot?
sec11-card-sec11-F020.memory_hook: No driver in mirror, invisible car
sec11-card-sec11-F020.expected_back: Stay out of truck blind spots, using whether the truck driver is visible in the mirror as a warning of whether your vehicle can be seen.

sec11-card-sec11-F021.front: What tool does the handbook recommend for spelling out clear family driving limits and revisiting them regularly?
sec11-card-sec11-F021.memory_hook: Write and review a parent-teen agreement
sec11-card-sec11-F021.expected_back: Set family driving limits explicitly and discuss them regularly, using a parent-teen agreement to make expectations clear.

sec11-card-sec11-F022.front: Which four non-negotiable safety rules belong in every family driving agreement?
sec11-card-sec11-F022.memory_hook: Belts, speed limits, sober, zero distractions
sec11-card-sec11-F022.expected_back: Family rules should require belts for everyone, compliance with speed limits and avoidance of alcohol, drugs and distracted driving.

sec11-card-sec11-F023.front: Beyond driving sober yourself, what passenger safety rule belongs in a parent-teen driving agreement?
sec11-card-sec11-F023.memory_hook: Never ride with an impaired driver
sec11-card-sec11-F023.expected_back: A teen should not ride with a driver who has used alcohol or drugs under the recommended family agreement.

sec11-card-sec11-F024.front: Before a teen heads out with the car keys, what three trip details should parents know?
sec11-card-sec11-F024.memory_hook: Share destination, passengers, and return time
sec11-card-sec11-F024.expected_back: Before each trip, parents should know the destination, companions and planned return time.

sec11-card-sec11-F025.front: When should family consequences for breaking driving rules be set, what should they connect to, and what coaching step can be included?
sec11-card-sec11-F025.memory_hook: Pre-set privilege limits plus extra coaching
sec11-card-sec11-F025.expected_back: Establish consequences in advance and relate them to driving privileges; additional supervised practice may be part of the response.

sec11-card-sec11-F026.front: What five classic beginner driving mistakes does the handbook highlight around path focus, speed, curves, intersections, and spacing?
sec11-card-sec11-F026.memory_hook: Path drift, speed, curves, intersections, tailgating
sec11-card-sec11-F026.expected_back: Common novice errors include poor attention to the travel path, excessive speed for conditions, unsafe curve speed, inadequate intersection searches and following too closely.

sec11-card-sec11-F027.front: Which five behaviors mark an aggressive driver on the road?
sec11-card-sec11-F027.memory_hook: Lane jumping, tailgating, blocking, running, gestures
sec11-card-sec11-F027.expected_back: Aggressive behavior includes repeated lane jumping, tailgating, blocking another driver's merge or pass, ignoring controls and threatening gestures.

sec11-card-sec11-F028.front: How should you handle your lane and speed if an aggressive driver tries to push or crowd you?
sec11-card-sec11-F028.memory_hook: Make room, never race or defend
sec11-card-sec11-F028.expected_back: When confronted by an aggressive driver, make room and avoid challenging them by racing or defending your lane position.

sec11-card-sec11-F029.front: If an angry driver waves or glares at you, what should you avoid doing and where should your focus stay?
sec11-card-sec11-F029.memory_hook: Ignore gestures and eyes, escape belted
sec11-card-sec11-F029.expected_back: Do not return an aggressive driver's gestures or make eye contact; keep your belt fastened and focus on escaping the conflict.

sec11-card-sec11-F030.front: What four details help police locate an aggressive driver, and what safety rule applies before calling nine-one-one?
sec11-card-sec11-F030.memory_hook: Car, plate, spot, direction when safe
sec11-card-sec11-F030.expected_back: Report aggressive driving with vehicle description, plate, location and travel direction, calling nine-one-one only when that can be done safely.

sec11-card-sec11-F031.front: How must the car be secured while the teen sits in the driver's seat for the driveway blind-spot drill?
sec11-card-sec11-F031.memory_hook: Parked stationary with engine turned off
sec11-card-sec11-F031.expected_back: For the blind-spot exercise, keep the vehicle stationary with its engine off while the teen sits at the wheel.

sec11-card-sec11-F032.front: During the front blind-spot drill, how far away from the front bumper does the adult step before placing a cone or cup?
sec11-card-sec11-F032.memory_hook: Step out until feet become visible
sec11-card-sec11-F032.expected_back: From near the front bumper, the adult moves backward until the teen can see the adult's feet, then marks the point with a cone or cup.

sec11-card-sec11-F033.front: After marking the front blind zone, which three other directions around the car do you map and measure — and how does the teen check behind?
sec11-card-sec11-F033.memory_hook: Map rear and both side boundaries
sec11-card-sec11-F033.expected_back: Repeat the visibility exercise behind the vehicle using the mirror or shoulder check, and from both passenger-door sides, marking and measuring the visible boundaries.

sec03-card-sec03-F001.front: What three main sign families appear on streets and highways, and which family gives mandatory legal instructions?
sec03-card-sec03-F001.expected_back: Streets and highways use regulatory, warning and guide signs, and regulatory signs govern traffic with mandatory driver instructions.

sec03-card-sec03-F002.front: What shape is a stop sign, and where must your wheels come to a complete halt when markings are painted?
sec03-card-sec03-F002.expected_back: The eight-sided stop sign requires a complete stop before the stop line or crosswalk.

sec03-card-sec03-F003.front: If an intersection with a stop sign has neither a painted stop line nor a crosswalk, where do you stop?
sec03-card-sec03-F003.expected_back: Where no stop line or crosswalk exists, stop before the intersection at the nearest position providing a safe view of approaching traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-F004.front: What two actions must you be ready to take at a yield sign when cross traffic or pedestrians are close?
sec03-card-sec03-F004.expected_back: At a yield sign, reduce speed and stop when needed to give other traffic the right of way.

sec03-card-sec03-F005.front: Does a posted speed-limit sign guarantee a safe speed in rain, snow, or heavy traffic?
sec03-card-sec03-F005.expected_back: A posted speed limit represents the maximum for ideal conditions, rather than a safe speed for every situation.

sec03-card-sec03-F006.front: How close to the farm must farm hazardous-material hauling stay to qualify under the exemption without a hazmat endorsement?
sec03-card-sec03-F006.expected_back: Under the farm exemption, farm hazardous-material transport within one hundred fifty miles of the farm does not require a hazardous-material endorsement.

sec03-card-sec03-F007.front: How far may a covered farm vehicle operate under the exemption when its greater GVW or GVWR is twenty-six thousand one pounds or less?
sec03-card-sec03-F007.expected_back: A covered farm vehicle weighing no more than twenty-six thousand one pounds by the greater of GVW and GVWR may operate nationwide under the described exemption.

sec03-card-sec03-F008.front: Where may a covered farm vehicle above twenty-six thousand one pounds operate under the exemption inside and outside its registration state?
sec03-card-sec03-F008.expected_back: For a covered farm vehicle above twenty-six thousand one pounds by the greater of GVW and GVWR, the exemption allows operation in its registration state or within one hundred fifty air miles of the farm or ranch outside that state.

sec03-card-sec03-F009.front: When you turn onto or drive along a posted one-way street, which direction may you travel?
sec03-card-sec03-F009.expected_back: On a one-way street, travel only in the direction indicated by the arrow.

sec03-card-sec03-F010.front: What urgent mistake is a Wrong Way sign telling you on a street, ramp, or freeway?
sec03-card-sec03-F010.expected_back: A Wrong Way sign warns that you are traveling against the authorized direction on a street, ramp or freeway.

sec03-card-sec03-F011.front: What does a Do Not Enter sign forbid you from doing at the roadway opening ahead?
sec03-card-sec03-F011.expected_back: Do Not Enter bars entry into the roadway section it controls.

sec03-card-sec03-F012.front: On a regulatory sign, what does a red circle with a diagonal red slash across a symbol mean?
sec03-card-sec03-F012.expected_back: A red slash through a red circle identifies the action that a regulatory sign forbids.

sec03-card-sec03-F013.front: Which side of the road holds the rectangular Do Not Pass sign, and which side holds the yellow no-passing pennant?
sec03-card-sec03-F013.expected_back: A rectangular Do Not Pass sign is placed to the right; the supplementary yellow pennant used by some states is placed to the left.

sec03-card-sec03-F014.front: What does a No Turn on Red sign forbid at an intersection — and does an illuminated electronic sign carry the same force?
sec03-card-sec03-F014.expected_back: No Turn on Red prohibits the indicated right turn at the controlled intersection, including when the message is electronic.

sec03-card-sec03-F015.front: Who may enter a two-way center left-turn lane, and what maneuver is strictly banned inside it?
sec03-card-sec03-F015.expected_back: A two-way center left-turn lane serves left-turning traffic from either direction and cannot be used to pass.

sec03-card-sec03-F016.front: What do yellow warning signs with dark lettering or symbols alert you to expect up the road?
sec03-card-sec03-F016.expected_back: Yellow warning signs with dark lettering call for additional caution because a hazard lies ahead.

sec03-card-sec03-F017.front: When should you slow down for a curve or turn warning sign, and what does the small advisory speed plaque tell you?
sec03-card-sec03-F017.expected_back: For curve or turn warnings, reduce speed before entering; an advisory speed plaque gives the recommended maximum for that curve or turn.

sec03-card-sec03-F018.front: When a warning sign shows your lane ending ahead, what action must you take?
sec03-card-sec03-F018.expected_back: A lane-reduction warning requires a safe move into the continuing lane.

sec03-card-sec03-F019.front: How does an added-lane warning sign differ from a standard merge sign for entering traffic?
sec03-card-sec03-F019.expected_back: An added-lane sign means entering traffic receives its own lane without a required merge.

sec03-card-sec03-F020.front: How do the divided-highway-begins and divided-highway-ends warning signs differ in what happens to opposing traffic?
sec03-card-sec03-F020.expected_back: A divided-highway-begins warning indicates opposing traffic will be separated; the corresponding ends warning indicates that separation stops.

sec03-card-sec03-F021.front: What specific danger are crossroad and side-road warning signs alerting you to watch for ahead?
sec03-card-sec03-F021.expected_back: Intersection warning signs call attention to traffic that may enter your path.

sec03-card-sec03-F022.front: What does a round yellow warning sign announce ahead, and how should you adjust your speed?
sec03-card-sec03-F022.expected_back: A circular yellow railroad warning sign means a crossing is ahead; slow enough to be able to stop for a train.

sec03-card-sec03-F023.front: What colors and shape mark a slow-moving vehicle emblem, and what top speed does that equipment travel?
sec03-card-sec03-F023.expected_back: The slow-moving-vehicle emblem is an orange triangle edged in reflective red on equipment traveling twenty-five miles per hour or less.

sec03-card-sec03-F024.front: Which two background colors are approved for pedestrian and school warning signs?
sec03-card-sec03-F024.expected_back: Pedestrian and school warning signs may use either standard yellow or fluorescent yellow-green.

sec03-card-sec03-F025.front: How does an advance school-ahead sign differ from a school-crosswalk sign posted right at the crossing?
sec03-card-sec03-F025.memory_hook: Ahead warns zone; crosswalk marks crossing
sec03-card-sec03-F025.expected_back: A school-ahead sign identifies an approaching school or marked school crossing; the school-crosswalk sign identifies a crossing used by children.

sec03-card-sec03-F026.front: Why does a bump warning sign tell you to drop your speed before hitting the rise?
sec03-card-sec03-F026.expected_back: A bump warning calls for lower speed to avoid losing vehicle control.

sec03-card-sec03-F027.front: What should you do when you see a slippery-when-wet warning sign and rain has slickened the road?
sec03-card-sec03-F027.expected_back: A slippery-when-wet sign means reduce speed when the pavement is wet.

sec03-card-sec03-F028.front: What two jobs do orange cones, drums, tubes, barricades, and vertical panels perform in a work zone?
sec03-card-sec03-F028.expected_back: Cones, drums, tubes, barricades and vertical panels warn of road work and channel traffic through it.

sec03-card-sec03-F029.front: How do you read diagonal stripes on a work-zone barricade or vertical panel to know which side to pass on?
sec03-card-sec03-F029.expected_back: On a striped barricade or panel, downward-right stripes direct traffic to its right; downward-left stripes direct traffic to its left.

sec03-card-sec03-F030.front: When can lighted work-zone arrow panels direct a lane change, and what non-arrow message can they also flash?
sec03-card-sec03-F030.memory_hook: Day or night arrows, plus caution
sec03-card-sec03-F030.expected_back: Work-zone arrow panels may direct a lane change during daylight or darkness and may also display a caution pattern.

sec03-card-sec03-F031.front: What color combination marks standard construction warning signs, and how can electronic work-zone signs behave?
sec03-card-sec03-F031.expected_back: Construction warning signs generally use black messages on orange backgrounds; electronic work-zone signs may change their messages.

sec03-card-sec03-F032.front: In North Dakota, what minimum fee kicks in if you speed through an active work zone while workers are present?
sec03-card-sec03-F032.expected_back: When work is underway and workers are present, the handbook gives a minimum eighty-dollar fee for violating a work-zone speed limit.

sec10-card-sec10-F001.front: After a DUI conviction in North Dakota, what assessment and follow-up step must you complete?
sec10-card-sec10-F001.expected_back: After a DUI conviction, the handbook requires an addiction evaluation and completion of any recommended treatment.

sec10-card-sec10-F002.front: Which two alcohol-related actions trigger North Dakota's requirement to file SR twenty-two proof of financial responsibility?
sec10-card-sec10-F002.memory_hook: Refusal or DUI requires SR twenty-two
sec10-card-sec10-F002.expected_back: Refusing an alcohol-concentration test or receiving a DUI conviction triggers the stated requirement for SR twenty-two financial-responsibility evidence.

sec10-card-sec10-F003.front: If someone spots or shows erratic driving that points to alcohol impairment, how can they report it to law enforcement?
sec10-card-sec10-F003.expected_back: Anyone who observes or exhibits unusual driving suggesting alcohol impairment may report it to law enforcement by calling nine-one-one.

sec10-card-sec10-F004.front: Who is barred from drinking alcohol in or on a motor vehicle, and where must any opened container be stored?
sec10-card-sec10-F004.memory_hook: No drinking aboard, open bottles trunked
sec10-card-sec10-F004.expected_back: Drivers and passengers may not drink alcohol in or on a motor vehicle; the handbook requires any opened container to be kept in the trunk.

sec10-card-sec10-F005.front: Under North Dakota's minor-alcohol rule, what three actions involving alcoholic drinks are off-limits if you are under twenty-one?
sec10-card-sec10-F005.memory_hook: Under twenty-one: never buy, hold, drink
sec10-card-sec10-F005.expected_back: People younger than twenty-one may not buy, possess or consume alcoholic beverages under the handbook's minor-alcohol rule.

sec10-card-sec10-F006.front: Why must you carefully read the directions on everyday medications like cold remedies before getting behind the wheel?
sec10-card-sec10-F006.memory_hook: Cold meds drowse, read directions first
sec10-card-sec10-F006.expected_back: Some medicines, including cold remedies, can cause drowsiness and impair driving, so read their directions carefully.

sec10-card-sec10-F007.front: How does North Dakota classify joggers on or near the street, and whose traffic rules do they have to follow?
sec10-card-sec10-F007.memory_hook: Joggers count as pedestrians on roads
sec10-card-sec10-F007.expected_back: Joggers are pedestrians and must obey pedestrian traffic rules.

sec10-card-sec10-F008.front: When the Don't Walk signal starts flashing, what should someone on the curb do versus someone already in the crosswalk?
sec10-card-sec10-F008.memory_hook: Flashing wait on curb, finish crossing
sec10-card-sec10-F008.expected_back: Do not begin crossing when Don't Walk is flashing; if already crossing, continue to the other side at a normal pace.

sec10-card-sec10-F009.front: Who has to yield when a person on foot crosses the street outside of a crosswalk?
sec10-card-sec10-F009.expected_back: A pedestrian crossing away from a crosswalk must yield to roadway vehicles.

sec10-card-sec10-F010.front: When is a pedestrian allowed to cut diagonally across an intersection?
sec10-card-sec10-F010.memory_hook: Never cross diagonally without official sign
sec10-card-sec10-F010.expected_back: Do not cross an intersection diagonally unless an official traffic device authorizes it.

sec10-card-sec10-F011.front: Where must you walk when a sidewalk is present, and how should you position yourself when there is no sidewalk?
sec10-card-sec10-F011.memory_hook: Take sidewalks, else walk facing traffic
sec10-card-sec10-F011.expected_back: Use sidewalks where available; otherwise face traffic and walk as far from the roadway as possible.

sec10-card-sec10-F012.front: When walking after dark, which direction should pedestrians face and what shades of clothing help drivers spot them?
sec10-card-sec10-F012.memory_hook: Face traffic wearing white or light
sec10-card-sec10-F012.expected_back: At night, pedestrians should face traffic and wear light-colored or white clothing for visibility.

sec10-card-sec10-F013.front: What is North Dakota's rule on standing in a traveled street or highway lane to ask for a ride?
sec10-card-sec10-F013.memory_hook: Never stand in lanes to hitchhike
sec10-card-sec10-F013.expected_back: Standing on a traveled street or highway lane to hitchhike is prohibited.

sec10-card-sec10-F014.front: When a ball rolls out into the street ahead of your car, what hazard should you anticipate right behind it?
sec10-card-sec10-F014.memory_hook: Rolling ball means child right behind
sec10-card-sec10-F014.expected_back: A ball entering the street may be followed by a child, so drivers must watch and be ready to respond.

sec10-card-sec10-F015.front: What four core duties apply to bicyclists sharing North Dakota streets regarding laws, lane side, pedestrians, and hand signals?
sec10-card-sec10-F015.memory_hook: Obey laws, keep right, yield, signal
sec10-card-sec10-F015.expected_back: Bicyclists must obey traffic law, keep right, yield to walkers and signal intended turns or stops.

sec10-card-sec10-F016.front: What is the maximum number of bicycles allowed side by side, and which riding formation is safest?
sec10-card-sec10-F016.memory_hook: Max two abreast, single file safest
sec10-card-sec10-F016.expected_back: Ride bicycles no more than two abreast; the handbook identifies single-file riding as safest.

sec10-card-sec10-F017.front: How old must you be to ride a motorized bicycle in North Dakota, and what credential do you have to carry?
sec10-card-sec10-F017.memory_hook: Age fourteen minimum with valid permit
sec10-card-sec10-F017.expected_back: A motorized bicycle operator must be at least fourteen and carry a qualifying license or permit.

sec10-card-sec10-F018.front: What is the passenger limit on a bicycle, and what steering rule applies whenever you carry a package?
sec10-card-sec10-F018.memory_hook: Seat limit only, one hand steering
sec10-card-sec10-F018.expected_back: Do not carry more bicycle passengers than its design permits, and keep at least one hand on the handlebar when carrying a bundle.

sec10-card-sec10-F019.front: What stopping equipment must bicycles and motorized bicycles have, and what towing shortcut is strictly banned?
sec10-card-sec10-F019.memory_hook: Working brakes required, never grab tows
sec10-card-sec10-F019.expected_back: Bicycles and motorized bicycles require brakes, and riders must not hold a moving vehicle to obtain a tow.

sec10-card-sec10-F020.front: Who is legally required to wear an approved helmet on a motorized bicycle, and what is recommended for all cyclists?
sec10-card-sec10-F020.memory_hook: Motorized under eighteen must wear helmets
sec10-card-sec10-F020.expected_back: A motorized-bicycle rider younger than eighteen must wear an approved helmet; helmet use is advised for all bicycle riders.

sec10-card-sec10-F021.front: To ride a bicycle at night, what front light, rear reflector, and optional taillight visibility distance are required?
sec10-card-sec10-F021.memory_hook: Five-hundred-foot headlight plus rear red reflector
sec10-card-sec10-F021.expected_back: For night use, a bicycle needs a headlight visible from five hundred feet and a rear red reflector; any fitted taillight must be visible from five hundred feet behind.

sec10-card-sec10-F022.front: Which three credential options qualify someone to operate an off-highway vehicle in North Dakota?
sec10-card-sec10-F022.memory_hook: License, permit, or Parks safety card
sec10-card-sec10-F022.expected_back: An off-highway vehicle operator must possess a valid license, permit or the stated Parks and Recreation safety certificate.

sec10-card-sec10-F023.front: Which off-highway vehicle riders must wear a helmet, and what safety standard must that helmet meet?
sec10-card-sec10-F023.memory_hook: Under eighteen wears federal-standard off-highway helmet
sec10-card-sec10-F023.expected_back: Off-highway riders younger than eighteen need a helmet meeting federal transportation standards.

sec10-card-sec10-F024.front: How must an off-highway vehicle rider stop, yield, and angle across an ordinary roadway?
sec10-card-sec10-F024.memory_hook: Stop before shoulder, yield, right-angle cross
sec10-card-sec10-F024.expected_back: For an off-highway vehicle road crossing, stop before the shoulder or traveled roadway, yield to road traffic and cross at roughly a right angle where the view is clear.

sec10-card-sec10-F025.front: Where is the only legal spot for an off-highway vehicle to cross a divided highway?
sec10-card-sec10-F025.memory_hook: Cross divided highways at intersections only
sec10-card-sec10-F025.expected_back: An off-highway vehicle may cross a divided highway only at an intersection with another road.

sec10-card-sec10-F026.front: When, if ever, can an off-highway vehicle enter a controlled-access highway right of way?
sec10-card-sec10-F026.memory_hook: Off-highway banned on controlled-access except emergencies
sec10-card-sec10-F026.expected_back: Except for emergencies, off-highway vehicles are barred from controlled-access highway rights of way.

sec10-card-sec10-F027.front: With a driver license and registration, which unpaved roads and which posted paved roads can a standard off-highway vehicle use?
sec10-card-sec10-F027.memory_hook: Loose roads or designated fifty-five paved
sec10-card-sec10-F027.expected_back: A licensed driver may use a registered off-highway vehicle on gravel, dirt or loose-surface roads, or a designated paved road posted no faster than fifty-five miles per hour.

sec10-card-sec10-F028.front: What age, credential, and posted speed limit apply to driving a registered Class Three off-highway vehicle on designated pavement?
sec10-card-sec10-F028.memory_hook: Over sixteen, Class Three, sixty-five paved
sec10-card-sec10-F028.expected_back: A licensed driver older than sixteen may operate a registered Class Three off-highway vehicle on a designated paved road posted no faster than sixty-five miles per hour.

sec10-card-sec10-F029.front: Before taking an off-highway vehicle onto allowed public roads, what vehicle-code standard must its gear meet?
sec10-card-sec10-F029.memory_hook: Public-road off-highway rides need code equipment
sec10-card-sec10-F029.expected_back: Off-highway vehicles used on the described public roads must satisfy the equipment rules in the cited vehicle-code chapter.

sec10-card-sec10-F030.front: What two credential options let you legally ride a snowmobile within a highway right of way?
sec10-card-sec10-F030.memory_hook: Carry license or snowmobile safety certificate
sec10-card-sec10-F030.expected_back: Highway-right-of-way snowmobile operation requires carrying a valid license or the stated snowmobile safety certificate.

sec10-card-sec10-F031.front: What lighting, stopping, and exhaust equipment must every snowmobile have?
sec10-card-sec10-F031.memory_hook: Lights, brakes, leak-free exhaust and muffler
sec10-card-sec10-F031.expected_back: A snowmobile needs front and rear lights, brakes and a leak-free exhaust with a muffler.

sec10-card-sec10-F032.front: Which snowmobile riders are required to wear a federally compliant safety helmet?
sec10-card-sec10-F032.memory_hook: Under eighteen wears compliant snowmobile helmet
sec10-card-sec10-F032.expected_back: Snowmobile riders younger than eighteen must wear a federally compliant safety helmet.

sec10-card-sec10-F033.front: Which parts of a regular road and which entire highway corridor are off-limits to snowmobiles?
sec10-card-sec10-F033.memory_hook: Off pavement, shoulders, inside banks, interstates
sec10-card-sec10-F033.expected_back: Snowmobiles must not use road pavement, shoulders or inside banks, or any part of an interstate right of way.

sec10-card-sec10-F034.front: When riding a snowmobile along a roadside ditch, which direction must you travel relative to the road beside you?
sec10-card-sec10-F034.memory_hook: Ride ditches matching adjacent traffic flow
sec10-card-sec10-F034.expected_back: In roadside ditches, snowmobile travel must match the adjacent roadway's traffic direction.

sec10-card-sec10-F035.front: Between which two calendar dates is snowmobile riding banned in every road right of way?
sec10-card-sec10-F035.memory_hook: Banned April first to November first
sec10-card-sec10-F035.expected_back: Snowmobile use of any road right of way is prohibited from April first to November first.

sec10-card-sec10-F036.front: What are the stop, yield, and angle steps for crossing a road by snowmobile — and the extra rule for divided highways?
sec10-card-sec10-F036.memory_hook: Stop, yield, right angle, divided intersections
sec10-card-sec10-F036.expected_back: To cross a road by snowmobile, stop before the shoulder, yield and cross at a right angle when clear; cross divided roads only at intersections.

sec10-card-sec10-F037.front: Besides impaired riding, what three harmful actions toward wildlife, vegetation, and private property are banned on a snowmobile?
sec10-card-sec10-F037.memory_hook: Sober riding: respect wildlife, plants, land
sec10-card-sec10-F037.expected_back: Do not operate a snowmobile impaired, harass animals, damage plants or enter private land without permission.

sec01-card-sec01-F001.question_text: You walk up to the ND driver-license counter to test. What four things do your ID and address papers have to prove before they let you sit down?
sec01-card-sec01-F001.teaching_text: Do not get bounced at the front desk before question one.

sec01-card-sec01-F002.question_text: Whether you are applying for a permit, a driver license, or a state ID card in North Dakota, what personal number has to go on the application?
sec01-card-sec01-F002.teaching_text: Know the digits or bring the card info in your folder so none of the three applications stall at check-in.

sec01-card-sec01-F003.question_text: If you are under eighteen applying in North Dakota, who has to approve and sponsor your application — and what extra rule applies to a legal guardian?
sec01-card-sec01-F003.teaching_text: Minors cannot solo-sign at the counter, and exam questions love testing that extra guardianship-paper requirement.

sec01-card-sec01-F004.question_text: You are heading in for an office knowledge test. What is the latest cutoff time to arrive before closing — and before lunch if that office shuts at noon?
sec01-card-sec01-F004.teaching_text: Slide in thirty minutes before close or before a noon lunch break and the counter turns you around at the door.

sec01-card-sec01-F005.question_text: What happens to your knowledge test score if you walk into the testing zone carrying your phone, smartwatch, or prohibited personal items?
sec01-card-sec01-F005.teaching_text: Even a muted phone in your hoodie pocket counts once you cross into the knowledge-testing area.

sec01-card-sec01-F006.question_text: Midway through the ND knowledge exam, you step out of the testing area before submitting your test. What happens?
sec01-card-sec01-F006.teaching_text: Handle restroom or water breaks before starting — walking out before submitting ends the attempt.

sec01-card-sec01-F007.question_text: Pets are banned from the ND testing area, except for which two specific types of animals?
sec01-card-sec01-F007.teaching_text: Exam distractors try sneaking comfort or family pets in; only working medical-alert and service animals qualify.

sec01-card-sec01-F008.question_text: What accessibility standard do all North Dakota driver-license offices meet, and what language help is available for general office business?
sec01-card-sec01-F008.teaching_text: Notice the scope trap: interpretation covers general counter business, separate from testing-room rules.

sec01-card-sec01-F009.question_text: You pull up for your ND road test. Which three documents must you hand over before the drive starts?
sec01-card-sec01-F009.teaching_text: Show up missing one paper in the glovebox and the road test gets canceled on the spot.

sec01-card-sec01-F010.question_text: If you are taking your ND road test before turning sixteen, what extra certificate and who in person must come with you?
sec01-card-sec01-F010.teaching_text: Testing before your sixteenth birthday adds extra check-in requirements on top of normal car papers.

sec01-card-sec01-F011.question_text: Before the examiner rides out onto the street with you, what check does your road-test car have to pass first?
sec01-card-sec01-F011.teaching_text: The road test starts in the parking stall — fail the equipment check and the drive never begins.

sec01-card-sec01-F012.question_text: Who and what must be cleared out of the car during your ND road test — and what is the lone animal exception?
sec01-card-sec01-F012.teaching_text: Friends, family, and phones wait inside the building so the cabin stays distraction-free for you and the examiner.

sec01-card-sec01-F013.question_text: Your family car has an automatic self-parking feature. What are your two options if you want to take the ND road test?
sec01-card-sec01-F013.teaching_text: The examiner grades your parking skills, not the car computer, so locate that off setting before test day.

sec01-card-sec01-F014.question_text: Who has to be allowed to inspect your vehicle before the North Dakota road test can start?
sec01-card-sec01-F014.teaching_text: Expect a safety walkaround in the parking lot before the examiner ever steps into the passenger seat.

sec01-card-sec01-F015.question_text: During the pre-test check, which two brake systems and which three lighting systems on your car have to work?
sec01-card-sec01-F015.teaching_text: Do a driveway walkaround the night before — one burned-out turn bulb or loose parking brake cancels the drive.

sec01-card-sec01-F016.question_text: Beyond brakes and lights, which four exhaust, door, belt, and windshield items must work on your road-test vehicle?
sec01-card-sec01-F016.teaching_text: A stuck passenger door, torn wiper, or leaky muffler can end your test before you leave the parking stall.

sec01-card-sec01-F017.question_text: What exact distance number applies to BOTH your horn loudness and your rear-mirror view on the ND road-test inspection?
sec01-card-sec01-F017.teaching_text: Test writers love pairing horn loudness and mirror visibility because both share the exact same distance.

sec01-card-sec01-F018.question_text: When does cracked glass disqualify a car from being used for your North Dakota road test?
sec01-card-sec01-F018.teaching_text: A tiny edge chip out of sight differs from a crack cutting across the driver or examiner sightline.

sec01-card-sec01-F019.question_text: What happens to your road test if the vehicle itself is unsafe or creates an unsafe working environment for the examiner?
sec01-card-sec01-F019.teaching_text: Examiners will not ride in a hazard inside or outside the cabin.

sec01-card-sec01-F020.question_text: Outside the student, tourist, and military exceptions, how many consecutive days of living in North Dakota makes you a resident for licensing?
sec01-card-sec01-F020.teaching_text: Do not mix up this ninety-day residency clock with the sixty-day license-swap clock that starts afterward.

sec01-card-sec01-F021.question_text: Once you become a North Dakota resident, how long can you drive a Class D or Class M vehicle on your out-of-state license before getting an ND license?
sec01-card-sec01-F021.teaching_text: This sixty-day swap countdown starts once North Dakota residency is established.

sec01-card-sec01-F022.question_text: Once North Dakota issues your permit or driver license, what two things must you do with the physical card?
sec01-card-sec01-F022.teaching_text: A photo of your permit on your camera roll will not satisfy a traffic stop.

sec01-card-sec01-F023.question_text: What minimum age and license requirement must a nonresident meet to legally drive in North Dakota under the visitor exemption?
sec01-card-sec01-F023.teaching_text: Even if another state issues younger learner permits, visiting nonresidents must meet North Dakota age-sixteen rules.

sec01-card-sec01-F024.question_text: Which two groups driving government vehicles on official business are exempt from needing a North Dakota license?
sec01-card-sec01-F024.teaching_text: Watch the official-business condition — personal errands in a private vehicle are never covered.

sec01-card-sec01-F025.question_text: A North Dakota resident leaves on active military duty with a valid ND license. How long does that license stay valid after separation or discharge?
sec01-card-sec01-F025.teaching_text: That thirty-day grace window gives returning service members time to renew home in North Dakota without a gap.

sec01-card-sec01-F026.question_text: If your driver license is currently suspended or revoked in another state, can you get a North Dakota license?
sec01-card-sec01-F026.teaching_text: States share driver records nationwide, so you cannot outrun an active suspension by crossing state lines.

sec01-card-sec01-F027.question_text: If an applicant has a history of seizures or episodes of lost consciousness, what two requirements unlock the handbook exception?
sec01-card-sec01-F027.teaching_text: Both boxes have to be checked together — time alone without the medical examination will not clear it.

sec01-card-sec01-F028.question_text: Who is legally qualified to sit beside you and supervise when you drive on a North Dakota instruction permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F028.teaching_text: Your seventeen-year-old friend with a fresh license fails both the age floor and the three-year experience rule.

sec01-card-sec01-F029.question_text: Where must your supervising driver sit while you drive on a permit — and when is anyone else allowed in the front seat?
sec01-card-sec01-F029.teaching_text: Putting your supervisor in the back while a friend rides shotgun violates your permit unless the vehicle has no rear seat.

sec01-card-sec01-F030.question_text: What is the minimum age to get a North Dakota instruction permit, and what two screenings must you pass?
sec01-card-sec01-F030.teaching_text: Passing the written questions is only half of check-in — expect the vision check at the counter too.

sec01-card-sec01-F031.question_text: If a minor’s parent or guardian cannot appear in person to sign for a permit, how can they authorize a temporary signer — and who keeps financial responsibility?
sec01-card-sec01-F031.teaching_text: Signing authority can be delegated on notarized paper, while financial liability stays on the parent or guardian.

sec01-card-sec01-F032.question_text: How can a minor be sponsored for a permit if neither parent nor a guardian is living?
sec01-card-sec01-F032.teaching_text: This backup rule keeps minors without a living parent or guardian from being locked out of getting a permit.

sec01-card-sec01-F033.question_text: You ace the ND permit knowledge test online from home. Can you start driving right away, or what step is still required?
sec01-card-sec01-F033.teaching_text: Passing on your laptop at home is not a permit in your pocket — driving before the office visit is illegal.

sec01-card-sec01-F034.question_text: If you get your permit at fourteen or fifteen, how long must you hold it before a road test or waiver — including the hard floor?
sec01-card-sec01-F034.teaching_text: Watch the trap for late-fifteen starters: turning sixteen never lets you skip the six-month minimum hold.
sec01-card-sec01-F034.must_match_memory_hook: Twelve months or sixteen, six-month floor

visual_sync.text_span: Twelve months or sixteen, six-month floor

sec01-card-sec01-F035.question_text: If you get your permit at sixteen or seventeen, how long must you hold it before taking the road test or using a waiver?
sec01-card-sec01-F035.teaching_text: Starting at sixteen or seventeen cuts the hold window to six months and caps it on your eighteenth birthday.

sec01-card-sec01-F036.question_text: Besides formal driver ed, how many supervised practice hours must a learner under sixteen log — and in what kind of conditions?
sec01-card-sec01-F036.teaching_text: Driver-ed class time never replaces family practice across night, highway, and weather conditions.

sec01-card-sec01-F037.question_text: How does North Dakota verify those fifty practice hours when an under-sixteen learner shows up at the test site?
sec01-card-sec01-F037.teaching_text: Do not show up solo with a scribbled log sheet — in-person parent or guardian sign-off is required at the site.

sec01-card-sec01-F038.question_text: To qualify for a road-test waiver certificate, how many classroom hours and how many actual behind-the-wheel hours must it document?
sec01-card-sec01-F038.teaching_text: Keep the two numbers in the right buckets — exam distractors love flipping classroom hours and wheel hours.

sec01-card-sec01-F039.question_text: How many driving-record points does the ND handbook assign if you drive in violation of your instruction-permit conditions?
sec01-card-sec01-F039.teaching_text: Driving solo or breaking front-seat rules hits your record before you even earn a full license.

sec01-card-sec01-F040.question_text: Under the school-program exception, when can a fourteen-year-old drive a driver-education car?
sec01-card-sec01-F040.teaching_text: This narrow exception applies strictly during certified school driver-ed lessons, never in a family car.

sec01-card-sec01-F041.question_text: What form must your identity documents be in at the ND counter — and which two common items get rejected every time?
sec01-card-sec01-F041.teaching_text: Classic test-day heartbreaker: parents bring a photocopy or a souvenir hospital footprint certificate and get turned away.

sec01-card-sec01-F042.question_text: What must you bring if your current name does not match your identity document — and do photocopies count?
sec01-card-sec01-F042.teaching_text: Any gap between birth record and current ID needs an official certified court, marriage, or adoption record to bridge it.

sec02-card-sec02-F001.question_text: What two details must your Social Security proof show at the North Dakota counter, and which four documents count as examples?
sec02-card-sec02-F001.teaching_text: Partial last-four printouts get rejected at check-in because examiners must verify every digit alongside your legal name.

sec02-card-sec02-F002.question_text: How many approved documents do you need to prove your North Dakota residential address, and how current must they be?
sec02-card-sec02-F002.teaching_text: Showing up with just one utility statement or outdated mail stalls your application right at the counter.

sec02-card-sec02-F003.question_text: What two items must appear on your North Dakota address documents, and why will a post-office box fail?
sec02-card-sec02-F003.teaching_text: Classic counter and exam trap: mail sent to a post-office box proves where letters land, not where you actually live.

sec02-card-sec02-F004.question_text: If you use a school or college transcript as North Dakota address proof, how recently must it have been issued?
sec02-card-sec02-F004.teaching_text: Last year's report card or an older transcript misses the freshness cutoff when proving residency as a student.

sec02-card-sec02-F005.question_text: Who provides the car for a North Dakota road test, and whose instructions govern the drive from start to finish?
sec02-card-sec02-F005.teaching_text: State offices never hand you a test car, and ignoring a prompt during the route costs points immediately.

sec02-card-sec02-F006.question_text: Which five core driving habits and maneuvers must you demonstrate cleanly to pass the North Dakota road test?
sec02-card-sec02-F006.teaching_text: Slouching one-handed on the wheel or skipping turn signals during parallel parking can sink an otherwise smooth drive.

sec02-card-sec02-F007.question_text: If you do not pass a North Dakota driver exam on your first try, how soon are you allowed to retest?
sec02-card-sec02-F007.teaching_text: Rushing back to the counter that afternoon will not work because state rules force at least an overnight reset.

sec02-card-sec02-F008.question_text: What are the two driver-training hour paths for a fourteen- or fifteen-year-old earning a North Dakota training certificate?
sec02-card-sec02-F008.teaching_text: Exam questions contrast the thirty-hour classroom school track against the six-hour behind-the-wheel commercial instructor path.

sec02-card-sec02-F009.question_text: When you pass your road test at fifteen, what license do you get and whose vehicles are you legally allowed to drive?
sec02-card-sec02-F009.teaching_text: Borrowing a friend's car at fifteen violates your restricted license even if that friend's parents say yes.

sec02-card-sec02-F010.question_text: Between which night hours must a restricted fifteen-year-old have a parent, guardian, or adult at least eighteen riding along?
sec02-card-sec02-F010.teaching_text: Summer sunsets stretch past nine in North Dakota, so watch the clock until five in the morning.

sec02-card-sec02-F011.question_text: Which three direct trips let a restricted fifteen-year-old drive solo during North Dakota's nighttime curfew window?
sec02-card-sec02-F011.teaching_text: Detouring for late-night fast food voids the exemption because travel must stay direct between home and the event.

sec02-card-sec02-F012.question_text: At what birthday does a North Dakota teen's restricted Class D license lift its age restrictions under the handbook rule?
sec02-card-sec02-F012.teaching_text: Turning sixteen ends the fifteen-year-old family-vehicle and night-curfew limits, though teen phone bans still apply until eighteen.

sec02-card-sec02-F013.question_text: Which two groups of North Dakota drivers are completely banned from using electronic communication devices behind the wheel?
sec02-card-sec02-F013.teaching_text: Even an adult holding an instruction permit falls under the exact same zero-device rule as teen license holders.

sec02-card-sec02-F014.question_text: Under what three urgent situations may a permit holder or teen under eighteen legally use a phone while driving?
sec02-card-sec02-F014.teaching_text: Checking maps or texting parents that you are running late never qualifies — only genuine safety or crime emergencies count.

sec02-card-sec02-F015.question_text: What does checking the donor box on your North Dakota application cover, and who affirms that choice if you are under eighteen?
sec02-card-sec02-F015.teaching_text: Teens can opt in on their first application, while state rules keep parents involved in affirming a minor's consent.

sec02-card-sec02-F016.question_text: If a minor's permit or license is canceled for alcohol or drugs, how does North Dakota treat their prior driving history?
sec02-card-sec02-F016.teaching_text: One impaired mistake wipes out prior progress, forcing you back through education, exams, and full permit-holding time.

sec02-card-sec02-F017.question_text: Once you finish every requirement after a license cancellation, does your North Dakota driving record drop back to zero points?
sec02-card-sec02-F017.teaching_text: Classic DMV true-or-false trap: earning your driving privilege back does not wipe existing violation points off your record.

sec02-card-sec02-F018.question_text: On a North Dakota license, what do restriction codes one, two, and three each require when you drive?
sec02-card-sec02-F018.teaching_text: Test writers mix up the first three number codes constantly, so pair glasses, outside mirrors, and automatic gearboxes in order.
sec02-card-sec02-F018.must_match_memory_hook: One lenses, two mirrors, three automatic

visual_sync.text_span: One lenses, two mirrors, three automatic

sec02-card-sec02-F019.question_text: What driving limits do North Dakota restriction codes four, five, and six stand for on a license?
sec02-card-sec02-F019.teaching_text: Memorize this middle trio together so exam questions cannot swap daylight-only limits with special hand-control equipment.
sec02-card-sec02-F019.must_match_memory_hook: Four controls, five daylight, six financial

visual_sync.text_span: Four controls, five daylight, six financial

sec02-card-sec02-F020.question_text: If restriction code nine is printed on your North Dakota permit or license, where is that specific limitation explained?
sec02-card-sec02-F020.teaching_text: Whenever a custom restriction does not fit standard codes, code nine tells officers to read the back of your card.

sec02-card-sec02-F021.question_text: Permanently losing the use of which five body parts must be reported to the North Dakota Driver License Division?
sec02-card-sec02-F021.teaching_text: Reporting permanent vision or limb changes lets examiners check whether mirrors, hand controls, or updated restrictions keep you safe.

sec02-card-sec02-F022.question_text: At what exact time and date does a North Dakota driver license expire — including for temporary-stay holders?
sec02-card-sec02-F022.teaching_text: Driving the morning after your expiration birthday means driving unlicensed, since validity cuts off right at midnight.

sec02-card-sec02-F023.question_text: How early can you renew a North Dakota license before it expires, and do you lose your remaining months?
sec02-card-sec02-F023.teaching_text: Renewing ahead of winter weather or college move-in keeps every remaining month from your current cycle intact.

sec02-card-sec02-F024.question_text: How do you clear the vision requirement when renewing your North Dakota license, and how recent must a doctor's certificate be?
sec02-card-sec02-F024.teaching_text: Skip the counter eye-chart surprise by bringing a signed optometrist or physician vision statement dated within six months.

sec02-card-sec02-F025.question_text: Which three card problems require you to apply for a replacement North Dakota license or permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F025.teaching_text: A cracked card peeled past readability or showing a typo will not pass muster during a roadside stop.

sec02-card-sec02-F026.question_text: After changing your name or moving to a new address, how many days do you have to notify the Driver License Division — and what must you include?
sec02-card-sec02-F026.teaching_text: Verbal updates alone are not enough, and exam questions routinely test the ten-day deadline against thirty-day distractors.

sec02-card-sec02-F027.question_text: How soon must a vehicle be registered in North Dakota once its owner or operator moves in or takes gainful employment here?
sec02-card-sec02-F027.teaching_text: Unlike driver-license grace windows, vehicle registration kicks in right away once you live or work for pay in state.

sec02-card-sec02-F028.question_text: What insurance coverage must every North Dakota motor vehicle carry, and what duty falls on the vehicle's owner?
sec02-card-sec02-F028.teaching_text: Handing your keys to a friend when coverage has lapsed still puts the vehicle owner squarely on the hook.

sec02-card-sec02-F029.question_text: When can an out-of-state vehicle use North Dakota temporary registration instead of full permanent plates?
sec02-card-sec02-F029.teaching_text: Expired out-of-state plates disqualify you from temporary permits, so your home registration has to stay active.

sec02-card-sec02-F030.question_text: What two lengths do North Dakota temporary vehicle permits come in, and what extra fee applies on top of registration each time?
sec02-card-sec02-F030.teaching_text: Budget for that extra ten-dollar service fee every single time you buy or renew a temporary vehicle permit.
sec02-card-sec02-F030.must_match_memory_hook: Six or twelve months, ten-dollar fee

visual_sync.text_span: Six or twelve months, ten-dollar fee

sec02-card-sec02-F031.question_text: Where must a vehicle's registration card be kept at all times?
sec02-card-sec02-F031.teaching_text: Filing your registration card in a desk drawer at home leaves you empty-handed during a routine traffic stop.

sec02-card-sec02-F032.question_text: Which license class does this North Dakota handbook prepare you for, and what is required for other classes?
sec02-card-sec02-F032.teaching_text: Commercial rigs and motorcycles require separate exams and skill tests beyond the standard everyday passenger-vehicle license.

sec02-card-sec02-F033.question_text: Under basic North Dakota Class D rules, what are the GVWR caps for the single vehicle and for a towed trailer?
sec02-card-sec02-F033.teaching_text: Watch that single-pound test boundary: twenty-six thousand is covered, whereas twenty-six thousand one steps past basic single-vehicle weight.

sec02-card-sec02-F034.question_text: When a Class D combination tops twenty-six thousand pounds under the handbook rule, what age or exemption must the driver meet?
sec02-card-sec02-F034.teaching_text: Sixteen- and seventeen-year-olds cannot haul heavy twenty-six-thousand-plus combinations on standard Class D unless they meet farm-exemption rules.

sec02-card-sec02-F035.question_text: When can a Class D driver legally tow a trailer rated above ten thousand pounds?
sec02-card-sec02-F035.teaching_text: A trailer past ten thousand pounds stays Class D legal as long as truck and trailer combined stay at or under twenty-six thousand.

sec02-card-sec02-F036.question_text: Which four license classes are off-limits on a standard Class D license unless you hold the required endorsement?
sec02-card-sec02-F036.teaching_text: Hopping onto a motorcycle or commercial rig with plain Class D plastic counts as driving outside your license class.

sec02-card-sec02-F037.question_text: Which five special vehicle or towing categories are listed as exceptions covered under a Class D license?
sec02-card-sec02-F037.teaching_text: Family motorhomes, personal travel trailers, and active military or emergency rigs do not force drivers into commercial licensing.

sec02-card-sec02-F038.question_text: Under North Dakota's farm exemption, how far and up to what gross weight may a fifteen-year-old haul farm products or supplies?
sec02-card-sec02-F038.teaching_text: Exam questions love swapping the mileage radius and weight cap, so lock in one hundred fifty miles and fifty thousand pounds.

sec04-card-sec04-F001.question_text: What tools do work-zone flaggers use to stop, slow, or guide cars, and how must you respond?
sec04-card-sec04-F001.teaching_text: Ignoring a human flagger puts road crews feet from your bumper in immediate danger.

sec04-card-sec04-F002.question_text: Which four roadway hazards can show up inside a work zone, and what two actions should you take?
sec04-card-sec04-F002.teaching_text: Tight lanes, rough pavement, loose rock, and heavy rigs leave zero margin if you rush through.

sec04-card-sec04-F003.question_text: Does North Dakota road construction happen only during daylight, or when should you watch for work zones?
sec04-card-sec04-F003.teaching_text: Crews often pave or repair lanes overnight when traffic drops, catching sleepy night drivers off guard.

sec04-card-sec04-F004.question_text: What four navigation details do green highway signs with white lettering give you?
sec04-card-sec04-F004.teaching_text: Knowing green means directional guidance helps you spot upcoming junctions and mileage before your exit.

sec04-card-sec04-F005.question_text: Where does a green highway milepost start counting its white mileage numbers from?
sec04-card-sec04-F005.teaching_text: Pinpointing your exact milepost lets dispatchers find you fast if your car breaks down on a rural highway.
sec04-card-sec04-F005.must_match_memory_hook: Mileposts count from south, west, origin

visual_sync.text_span: Mileposts count from south, west, origin

sec04-card-sec04-F006.question_text: What color scheme marks motorist service signs, and what does the access symbol tell travelers?
sec04-card-sec04-F006.teaching_text: Written distractors mix up blue, green, and brown backgrounds, so pair blue with roadside services and barrier-free access.

sec04-card-sec04-F007.question_text: What type of destination is marked by white symbols on a brown road sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F007.teaching_text: Color-coding questions love pairing green, blue, and brown together to check if you know parks and recreation.

sec04-card-sec04-F008.question_text: Where must you stop for a steady red traffic light, and what two conditions let you move forward?
sec04-card-sec04-F008.teaching_text: Rolling past the painted stop bar or creeping into the pedestrian path is a classic road-test deduction.

sec04-card-sec04-F009.question_text: What exact transition does a steady yellow traffic light warn drivers is happening?
sec04-card-sec04-F009.teaching_text: Treating steady yellow like a challenge to stomp the gas sets up high-speed intersection side-impact crashes.

sec04-card-sec04-F010.question_text: Does a steady green traffic light let you go automatically, or what condition must be met first?
sec04-card-sec04-F010.teaching_text: Launching blindly on a fresh green light puts you straight into late cross-traffic or lingering walkers.

sec04-card-sec04-F011.question_text: When a green arrow lights up next to a red signal, can you go — and who still gets priority?
sec04-card-sec04-F011.teaching_text: Protected arrows let your lane move while adjacent lanes wait, provided anyone still clearing the box goes first.

sec04-card-sec04-F012.question_text: Under what three conditions can you make a right turn on a steady red light?
sec04-card-sec04-F012.teaching_text: Rolling the corner or missing a posted no-turn-on-red plaque turns a legal right turn into an instant citation.

sec04-card-sec04-F013.question_text: In North Dakota, which exact street-to-street setup lets you turn left on a red light if no sign bans it?
sec04-card-sec04-F013.teaching_text: Exam questions try tricking you with two-way onto one-way turns, where turning left on red stays illegal.

sec04-card-sec04-F014.question_text: You roll up to an intersection and the overhead traffic lights are completely unlit. What must you do?
sec04-card-sec04-F014.teaching_text: Cruising through a dead signal during a power outage assumes cross traffic sees you, inviting a bad crash.

sec04-card-sec04-F015.question_text: How must you treat a flashing red traffic signal, and when may you pull out?
sec04-card-sec04-F015.teaching_text: Drivers sometimes confuse flashing red with cautious rolling, when a complete stop and clear path are mandatory.

sec04-card-sec04-F016.question_text: What does a flashing yellow intersection signal allow you to do?
sec04-card-sec04-F016.teaching_text: Stopping dead under a flashing yellow risks getting rear-ended, while cruising without scanning misses cross hazards.

sec04-card-sec04-F017.question_text: On a dedicated left-turn signal, what do a steady red indication and a steady yellow indication each tell you?
sec04-card-sec04-F017.teaching_text: Trying to beat a steady yellow turn arrow puts your passenger side directly across oncoming highway lanes.

sec04-card-sec04-F018.question_text: What does a flashing yellow left-turn arrow allow, and who gets the right of way first?
sec04-card-sec04-F018.teaching_text: Never mistake a flashing yellow arrow for a protected phase — oncoming cars still have green.

sec04-card-sec04-F019.question_text: Which left-turn signal indication gives left-turning drivers the right of way?
sec04-card-sec04-F019.teaching_text: Knowing the difference between steady green and flashing yellow arrows prevents hesitating or turning into oncoming traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F020.question_text: On a two-way roadway, what two maneuvers are allowed across a single broken yellow centerline?
sec04-card-sec04-F020.teaching_text: Yellow always divides opposing traffic directions, while dashed paint tells you crossing for turns or overtakes is permitted.

sec04-card-sec04-F021.question_text: When solid and broken yellow centerlines run side by side, what is forbidden and what stays legal if the solid line is beside your lane?
sec04-card-sec04-F021.teaching_text: Written traps test whether a solid yellow line on your side blocks driveway left turns — only passing is banned.

sec04-card-sec04-F022.question_text: What does a double solid yellow centerline ban for both directions, and what crossing maneuver stays legal?
sec04-card-sec04-F022.teaching_text: Neither direction may pull out to overtake slower cars, yet turning left across those twin lines stays legal.
sec04-card-sec04-F022.must_match_memory_hook: Double yellow: turns yes, passing no

visual_sync.text_span: Double yellow: turns yes, passing no

sec04-card-sec04-F023.question_text: When an intersection provides special turning lanes, how must you position your car before making a turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F023.teaching_text: Swinging a last-second turn from a straight-through lane sideswipes drivers who properly lined up in the turn pocket.

sec04-card-sec04-F024.question_text: Where must your front bumper stop when an intersection has a wide white stop line ahead of a marked crosswalk?
sec04-card-sec04-F024.teaching_text: Pulling past the wide white bar to stop at the crosswalk stripes still counts as running the stop line.

sec04-card-sec04-F025.question_text: If an intersection has no painted stop line or crosswalk stripes, where are the two fallback places to stop?
sec04-card-sec04-F025.teaching_text: Unpainted residential corners still carry invisible pedestrian paths from sidewalk to sidewalk that your hood cannot block.

sec04-card-sec04-F026.question_text: Which two white paint styles can mark a crosswalk, and where must your vehicle stay?
sec04-card-sec04-F026.teaching_text: Blocking either parallel-line or longitudinal striping forces walkers to step out into live moving lanes.

sec04-card-sec04-F027.question_text: What four actions must kick in as soon as you reach a railroad advance warning sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F027.teaching_text: Freight trains cannot swerve or brake like cars, so shedding speed early gives you room to stop cleanly.

sec04-card-sec04-F028.question_text: Why must you scan every set of rails before crossing multiple railroad tracks right after a train passes?
sec04-card-sec04-F028.teaching_text: The last car clearing one rail can hide a fast second train coming the opposite way on adjacent tracks.

sec04-card-sec04-F029.question_text: Where must you make any required stop near a railway crossing, and what is forbidden on the rails?
sec04-card-sec04-F029.teaching_text: Queueing onto the rails behind red-light traffic traps your car with nowhere to go if crossing bells start ringing.
sec04-card-sec04-F029.must_match_memory_hook: Never stop or park on tracks

visual_sync.text_span: Never stop or park on tracks

sec04-card-sec04-F030.question_text: What is the minimum distance you must stop before a railroad crossing while a train is passing?
sec04-card-sec04-F030.teaching_text: Trains overhang wider than the steel rails, so creeping closer than fifteen feet risks clipping your front bumper.

sec04-card-sec04-F031.question_text: What is the rule when red railroad crossing lights are flashing or the crossing gates are lowered?
