sec04-card-sec04-F031.teaching_text: Trains look slower than they travel, making zig-zagging around lowered arms one of the deadliest road gambles.

sec04-card-sec04-F032.question_text: Which vehicles must stop fifteen to fifty feet from railroad tracks, and what must you never do while they are stopped there?
sec04-card-sec04-F032.teaching_text: Expect buses and hazmat haulers to brake at clear crossings, and stay behind them until they finish checking.

sec04-card-sec04-F033.question_text: At a passive railway crossing without gates or flashing lights, what three tasks fall on the driver?
sec04-card-sec04-F033.teaching_text: Rural North Dakota crossings often lack bells or gates, so only your eyes verify train clearance and exit space.
sec04-card-sec04-F033.must_match_memory_hook: Spot crossing, check trains, confirm room

visual_sync.text_span: Spot crossing, check trains, confirm room

sec04-card-sec04-F034.question_text: What three warning devices regulate vehicles at an active railroad crossing?
sec04-card-sec04-F034.teaching_text: Exam questions contrast passive signs with active crossings that trigger electric or mechanical alerts when a train nears.
sec04-card-sec04-F034.must_match_memory_hook: Active crossings use lights, bells, gates

visual_sync.text_span: Active crossings use lights, bells, gates

sec04-card-sec04-F035.question_text: If your car gets trapped on railroad tracks with a train approaching, how do you move away and which two contacts do you call?
sec04-card-sec04-F035.teaching_text: Moving forty-five degrees toward the locomotive keeps flying crash debris behind you instead of sliding down the rails toward you.

sec04-card-sec04-F036.question_text: Which posted contact should you use to report blocked tracks or malfunctioning railroad crossing lights or gates?
sec04-card-sec04-F036.teaching_text: Calling the railroad's direct emergency placard alerts dispatchers to halt trains on that exact crossing right away.

sec05-card-sec05-F001.question_text: How far ahead of a turn must your blinker stay on continuously before you turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F001.teaching_text: Flicking your blinker at the corner gives drivers behind you zero warning before you hit the brakes.

sec05-card-sec05-F002.question_text: Two cars reach an unsigned intersection at roughly the same moment. Which driver has to yield?
sec05-card-sec05-F002.teaching_text: Memorize who yields so exam wording never flips you backward when two cars arrive together.

sec05-card-sec05-F003.question_text: How should you approach an intersection, and in what three-step order should you scan cross traffic?
sec05-card-sec05-F003.teaching_text: Cross traffic from the left enters your lane first, which is why your eyes start and finish left.

sec05-card-sec05-F004.question_text: At an uncontrolled T-shaped intersection, which drivers must yield the right of way?
sec05-card-sec05-F004.teaching_text: Even without a stop or yield sign, your dead-end stem never gets priority over continuous cross traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F005.question_text: When you are waiting to make a left turn, what must you do for oncoming vehicles?
sec05-card-sec05-F005.teaching_text: Cutting across an oncoming driver's lane is one of the fastest ways to cause a head-on intersection crash.

sec05-card-sec05-F006.question_text: Who goes first at a four-way stop, and what should you do if another driver jumps out of turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F006.teaching_text: Having technical priority never protects your fenders — let impatient out-of-turn drivers clear rather than trading paint.

sec05-card-sec05-F007.question_text: When a walker is in your travel lane at an intersection, does the crosswalk need painted lines for you to yield?
sec05-card-sec05-F007.teaching_text: Unpainted residential corners still protect walkers legally, so never assume missing white paint means cars go first.

sec05-card-sec05-F008.question_text: How must you stop and behave when a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog is crossing?
sec05-card-sec05-F008.teaching_text: Honking, calling out, or nosing into the crosswalk breaks a working guide dog's focus and blocks a safe crossing.

sec05-card-sec05-F009.question_text: Who has the right of way when you pull out of or cross a road from a private driveway?
sec05-card-sec05-F009.teaching_text: Main-road traffic expects clear lanes at street or highway speed, so wait for a wide gap before pulling out.

sec05-card-sec05-F010.question_text: In a business or residential area, where must you stop when pulling out of an alley, driveway, private road, or building?
sec05-card-sec05-F010.teaching_text: Rolling straight to the street curb sweeps right across joggers, strollers, and kids on the sidewalk.

sec05-card-sec05-F011.question_text: How much clear sight distance do you need near a curve or hillcrest for a U-turn to be legal?
sec05-card-sec05-F011.teaching_text: Flipping a blind turnaround near a crest traps your car broadside across both lanes before fast traffic can brake.

sec05-card-sec05-F012.question_text: What must you do when an emergency or police vehicle approaches with its siren or flashing red, white, or blue lights?
sec05-card-sec05-F012.teaching_text: Slowing down inside your travel lane still blocks responders — clear all the way to the right curb.

sec05-card-sec05-F013.question_text: If sirens catch you inside an intersection while clearing room for an emergency vehicle, what must you avoid doing?
sec05-card-sec05-F013.teaching_text: Freezing mid-intersection plugs every cross-street turn path the ambulance or fire rig might need to take.

sec05-card-sec05-F014.question_text: What does North Dakota require when you reach a crash scene with a parked emergency vehicle flashing its lights?
sec05-card-sec05-F014.teaching_text: Responders and tow crews walk live pavement around wrecks, and an officer's hand signals override everything else.

sec05-card-sec05-F015.question_text: On an interstate or multilane highway, how must you react to a parked emergency, police, or NDDOT truck flashing emergency or work lights?
sec05-card-sec05-F015.teaching_text: Highway wind blast and mirror strikes inches from a shoulder stop put troopers and road workers at severe risk.

sec05-card-sec05-F016.question_text: What do flashing yellow lights on tow trucks and slow-moving vehicles tell approaching drivers to do?
sec05-card-sec05-F016.teaching_text: Closing on a heavy tow rig or farm tractor at highway pace eats up your stopping gap in seconds.

sec05-card-sec05-F017.question_text: Which drivers must stop when a stopped school bus turns on its flashing red lights?
sec05-card-sec05-F017.teaching_text: Kids cross in front of the bumper from either side of the street, so oncoming traffic must stop too.

sec05-card-sec05-F018.question_text: Once you stop for a school bus with flashing red lights, which three signals let you start moving again?
sec05-card-sec05-F018.teaching_text: Counting heads yourself is not enough — wait until the red flashers turn off, the bus rolls, or the driver waves.

sec05-card-sec05-F019.question_text: What are flashing yellow caution lights on a school bus warning you is about to happen?
sec05-card-sec05-F019.teaching_text: Gassing it to squeeze past flashing yellow bus lights traps you illegally running the red stop phase seconds later.

sec05-card-sec05-F020.question_text: Does a posted speed-limit sign guarantee that driving that fast is always safe and legal?
sec05-card-sec05-F020.teaching_text: Posted numbers apply to ideal dry roads — glare, ice, rain, or heavy traffic demand easing off the gas.

sec05-card-sec05-F021.question_text: Unless posted otherwise, what is North Dakota's speed limit when approaching a blind intersection or obstructed-view railroad crossing?
sec05-card-sec05-F021.teaching_text: Exam questions love testing this lowest twenty-mile-per-hour statutory limit whenever trees, buildings, or curves hide cross hazards.

sec05-card-sec05-F022.question_text: When no other speed is posted, what is the limit when passing a school — and during which student times does it apply?
sec05-card-sec05-F022.teaching_text: Pair twenty miles per hour with recess plus arrival and dismissal windows when kids dart toward the curb.

sec05-card-sec05-F023.question_text: What is the unposted default speed limit in a North Dakota business or residential district?
sec05-card-sec05-F023.teaching_text: Do not confuse twenty-five on neighborhood and downtown streets with twenty around active schools and blind corners.

sec05-card-sec05-F024.question_text: Which two categories of North Dakota roads default to a fifty-five-mile-per-hour maximum when no different sign is posted?
sec05-card-sec05-F024.teaching_text: Loose gravel slides easily under hard braking, and unsigned county or township blacktop caps at fifty-five too.

sec05-card-sec05-F025.question_text: When can a rural paved two-lane highway in North Dakota have a sixty-five-mile-per-hour speed limit?
sec05-card-sec05-F025.teaching_text: Watch the trap: rural two-lane blacktop only steps up to sixty-five where signs explicitly post that limit.

sec05-card-sec05-F026.question_text: Unless posted otherwise, what are North Dakota's maximum speeds on paved divided multilane highways versus rural interstates?
sec05-card-sec05-F026.teaching_text: Keep the top two highway tiers straight — divided multilane caps at seventy while rural interstates allow eighty.

sec05-card-sec05-F027.question_text: Before pulling out to pass another vehicle, what three questions plus sight-and-space check must you clear first?
sec05-card-sec05-F027.teaching_text: Most bad two-lane passes start with impatience when overtaking saves seconds yet gambles against oncoming traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F028.question_text: When completing a pass on a two-way road, how much buffer must remain between you and any oncoming vehicle when you merge back?
sec05-card-sec05-F028.teaching_text: Two cars closing at highway speeds cover two hundred feet in roughly a single heartbeat.

sec05-card-sec05-F029.question_text: After overtaking a car, what visual check in your inside rearview mirror tells you it is safe to merge back?
sec05-card-sec05-F029.teaching_text: Cutting back in as soon as your door passes theirs clips their front fender or forces panic braking.

sec05-card-sec05-F030.question_text: Where must your tires stay while passing, and what are you forbidden to do when someone else passes you?
sec05-card-sec05-F030.teaching_text: Dropping onto gravel shoulders risks a spin, and speeding up traps the passing driver in oncoming lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F031.question_text: Which road features, one-hundred-foot hazard buffers, and visibility conditions make passing strictly illegal?
sec05-card-sec05-F031.teaching_text: Memorize the one-hundred-foot ban before intersections, rail tracks, and tunnels alongside hills, curves, signs, and bad weather.

sec05-card-sec05-F032.question_text: What are the complete North Dakota steps for changing lanes safely on a multilane road?
sec05-card-sec05-F032.teaching_text: Mirrors miss cars riding beside your rear quarter panel, and sweeping across multiple lanes hides fast mergers.

sec05-card-sec05-F033.question_text: Who carries the legal responsibility for a safe lane change, and what final step comes after merging in?
sec05-card-sec05-F033.teaching_text: Leaving a turn signal blinking down the highway tricks cross-street drivers into pulling out right in front of you.

sec05-card-sec05-F034.question_text: Roughly how many feet does the North Dakota handbook estimate it takes to stop from fifty-five miles per hour on dry pavement?
sec05-card-sec05-F034.teaching_text: Three hundred feet equals an entire football field from spotting danger to rolling to a dead stop.

sec05-card-sec05-F035.question_text: How do you measure the three-second following distance using a fixed roadside landmark?
sec05-card-sec05-F035.teaching_text: Timing seconds against a shadow, sign, or post scales your buffer automatically as highway speed rises.

sec05-card-sec05-F036.question_text: What should you do if your car passes your chosen landmark before you finish counting three seconds?
sec05-card-sec05-F036.teaching_text: Easing off the gas opens reaction room without brake-checking the traffic stacked behind you.

sec05-card-sec05-F037.question_text: Which five road, vehicle, or traffic situations require stretching your following gap to four seconds or more?
sec05-card-sec05-F037.teaching_text: Bikes stop shorter than cars, big trucks hide hazards ahead, and heavy trailers or slick pavement stretch braking.

sec05-card-sec05-F038.question_text: What must you check before turning, and where should your car start and finish a right turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F038.teaching_text: Swinging wide left to start or drifting into the far lane at the exit fails road tests fast.

sec05-card-sec05-F039.question_text: When turning left from one one-way street onto another one-way street, which lane do you start from and where do you finish?
sec05-card-sec05-F039.teaching_text: With zero oncoming traffic on either street, hugging the left curb keeps turning arcs tight and predictable.

sec05-card-sec05-F040.question_text: When turning left from one two-way road onto another two-way road, where should your car approach before following the handbook turn path?
sec05-card-sec05-F040.teaching_text: Positioning close to the centerline lets trailing cars pass on the right and sets up a clean entry lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F001.question_text: When turning left from a two-way road onto a one-way street, where do you line up, where do you turn, and which lane do you enter?
sec06-card-sec06-F001.teaching_text: Swinging wide past the center or drifting into a far lane puts you into cross-street traffic on test day.

sec06-card-sec06-F002.question_text: Which lane do you enter first when turning left from a two-way road onto a four-lane highway, and what should you do afterward?
sec06-card-sec06-F002.teaching_text: Cutting straight across to the outside lane mid-turn slices directly through fast-moving highway traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F003.question_text: In which direction does traffic circulate around the central island of a roundabout?
sec06-card-sec06-F003.teaching_text: Turning left directly against the splitter island sends your car head-on into circulating drivers.

sec06-card-sec06-F004.question_text: How should you adjust your speed approaching a roundabout, and which three road users get the right-of-way before you enter?
sec06-card-sec06-F004.teaching_text: Charging into the entry crosswalk or cutting off cars already inside the ring causes instant side-impact crashes.

sec06-card-sec06-F005.question_text: When no special signs or pavement arrows say otherwise at a two-lane roundabout, which lane handles left turns, right turns, and going straight?
sec06-card-sec06-F005.teaching_text: Picking your lane before entering keeps you from crossing another driver's path at the exit.

sec06-card-sec06-F006.question_text: Once inside a roundabout, what is the rule on changing lanes and driving beside large trucks?
sec06-card-sec06-F006.teaching_text: Long trailers sweep across extra pavement as they curve, squeezing any car trying to sneak alongside.
sec06-card-sec06-F006.must_match_memory_hook: Hold your lane, never pass trucks

visual_sync.text_span: Hold your lane, never pass trucks

sec06-card-sec06-F007.question_text: What should you do if an emergency vehicle approaches before you enter a roundabout versus when you are already inside it?
sec06-card-sec06-F007.teaching_text: Stopping mid-circle blocks the curved lane completely, so exiting clears a clean path for responders.

sec06-card-sec06-F008.question_text: Why is there a raised paved apron around the center island of a roundabout?
sec06-card-sec06-F008.teaching_text: Passenger cars should stay in the travel lane instead of cutting across that raised truck-tracking border.

sec06-card-sec06-F009.question_text: Where do slower vehicles belong on the interstate, and what two things must you verify and do for every lane change?
sec06-card-sec06-F009.teaching_text: Camping in the left lane stalls highway flow, and drifting over without signaling surprises fast-closing traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F010.question_text: If your car has an emergency on the interstate, where must you pull over and how do you visibly signal for help?
sec06-card-sec06-F010.teaching_text: Stopping in a live highway lane invites a high-speed rear-end crash before anyone spots your distress.

sec06-card-sec06-F011.question_text: You blow past your interstate exit. What is the only legal move, and which two shortcuts are strictly off-limits?
sec06-card-sec06-F011.teaching_text: Backing up or cutting across an official median turnaround puts slow traffic into freeway speed lanes.

sec06-card-sec06-F012.question_text: What should you do if you accidentally steer onto the wrong exit ramp on a freeway?
sec06-card-sec06-F012.teaching_text: Drivers decelerating off the highway cannot expect a car reversing straight back up the ramp toward them.

sec06-card-sec06-F013.question_text: How should you use a freeway entrance ramp to join highway traffic, and when is the only time you stop?
sec06-card-sec06-F013.teaching_text: Braking needlessly on an open acceleration lane forces you to merge from zero into fast highway traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F014.question_text: Who must yield when a vehicle on an entrance ramp merges onto the freeway, assuming no special signs apply?
sec06-card-sec06-F014.teaching_text: Highway drivers do not have to slam their brakes just because your blinker is on at the merge.

sec06-card-sec06-F015.question_text: Which two actions are banned once your vehicle is on a freeway exit ramp?
sec06-card-sec06-F015.teaching_text: Cars peeling off at highway speed have narrow sightlines and nowhere to dodge a halted vehicle.

sec06-card-sec06-F016.question_text: During what daily window must your headlights be on in North Dakota — and when else outside those hours?
sec06-card-sec06-F016.teaching_text: Parking lights or daytime running lamps alone leave your rear taillights dark in dusk or gloomy conditions.

sec06-card-sec06-F017.question_text: In rain, snow, fog, or other bad weather, how short does visibility get before North Dakota requires your headlights on?
sec06-card-sec06-F017.teaching_text: Headlights help oncoming drivers spot your car through road spray long before you can read signs.

sec06-card-sec06-F018.question_text: How do your headlight beams determine the fastest safe speed you can drive after dark?
sec06-card-sec06-F018.teaching_text: Outrunning your beams means if a stalled car or deer appears, you cannot stop before hitting it.

sec06-card-sec06-F019.question_text: What two quick cleaning habits cut nighttime glare and maximize how well your lights illuminate the road?
sec06-card-sec06-F019.teaching_text: Interior film scatters oncoming beams across your eyes while road grime dims your own headlights.

sec06-card-sec06-F020.question_text: Where should your eyes move while driving at night instead of locking onto the middle of your headlight beam?
sec06-card-sec06-F020.teaching_text: Fixating on the bright spot dulls peripheral awareness right where dark-clothed walkers or roadside wildlife enter.

sec06-card-sec06-F021.question_text: How should you handle speed in posted deer zones, and why should you resist yanking the wheel to dodge an animal?
sec06-card-sec06-F021.teaching_text: Jerking the steering wheel at highway speed rolls cars into ditches or oncoming lanes.
sec06-card-sec06-F021.must_match_memory_hook: Slow down, brake straight, never swerve

visual_sync.text_span: Slow down, brake straight, never swerve

sec06-card-sec06-F022.question_text: At what two distances must you dim your high beams — both for oncoming traffic and when following another car?
sec06-card-sec06-F022.teaching_text: Exam questions love swapping these two numbers, and blinding mirrors ahead is just as dangerous as dazzling oncoming eyes.
sec06-card-sec06-F022.must_match_memory_hook: Five hundred oncoming, three hundred behind

visual_sync.text_span: Five hundred oncoming, three hundred behind

sec06-card-sec06-F023.question_text: Where should you shift your gaze if an oncoming driver forgets to dim their bright headlights?
sec06-card-sec06-F023.teaching_text: Tracking the right pavement line protects your night vision while keeping your car centered in its lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F024.question_text: What is the right call when drowsiness hits you during a nighttime drive?
sec06-card-sec06-F024.teaching_text: Cold air or loud music cannot prevent microsleeps that drift a car off dark rural highways.

sec06-card-sec06-F025.question_text: How must your wheels be positioned and what is the maximum legal gap from the right curb when parallel parked?
sec06-card-sec06-F025.teaching_text: Leaving the tail sticking out past twelve inches narrows the travel lane and fails road-test scoring.

sec06-card-sec06-F026.question_text: Which way do you turn your front wheels when parking downhill next to a curb versus uphill next to a curb?
sec06-card-sec06-F026.teaching_text: Angling the tires properly lets the curb chock the front wheel immediately if the brakes slip.

sec06-card-sec06-F027.question_text: Which way do you turn your front wheels when parking uphill on a road that has no curb?
sec06-card-sec06-F027.teaching_text: Without a raised curb to catch the tire, turning away would let a rolling car drift across traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F028.question_text: Before pulling out of a parked spot into the closest travel lane, what checks, signal, and right-of-way steps are required?
sec06-card-sec06-F028.teaching_text: Pulling straight from the curb without a head check or yield walks right into blind-spot collisions.

sec06-card-sec06-F029.question_text: Where should all four tires sit whenever space allows during a roadside emergency stop?
sec06-card-sec06-F029.teaching_text: Even one tire overhanging the fog line clips passing mirrors or triggers a high-speed sideswipe.

sec06-card-sec06-F030.question_text: During what overnight window must a vehicle parked on a public highway show lights, what colors are required front and rear, and from how far away?
sec06-card-sec06-F030.teaching_text: An unlit car sitting beside dark rural pavement disappears until oncoming traffic is too close to swerve.

sec06-card-sec06-F031.question_text: Which four everyday street spots — involving walkways, property access, crossings, and double-parking — are always illegal for parking?
sec06-card-sec06-F031.teaching_text: Double-parking even briefly for a pickup still counts as parking alongside another car and earns a ticket.

sec06-card-sec06-F032.question_text: How many feet of clearance must you leave when parking near an intersection crosswalk or a fire hydrant?
sec06-card-sec06-F032.teaching_text: North Dakota uses ten feet for both hydrants and intersection crosswalks, unlike states that test fifteen.

sec06-card-sec06-F033.question_text: At least how far back must you park from a roadside stop sign, traffic light, or flashing beacon?
sec06-card-sec06-F033.teaching_text: Parking too close hides the sign or signal behind your roof until approaching drivers roll past it.

sec06-card-sec06-F034.question_text: What elevated structures, underground passages, work-zone hazards, and posted areas are completely off-limits for parking?
sec06-card-sec06-F034.teaching_text: Narrow structures and dug-up shoulders have zero escape room if traffic backs up or an emergency rig approaches.

sec06-card-sec06-F035.question_text: What credentials are required to use an accessible stall, and what is the rule for the striped diagonal zone next to it?
sec06-card-sec06-F035.teaching_text: Wheelchair lifts and ramps deploy onto those diagonal stripes, so crowding that aisle traps another driver outside.

sec06-card-sec06-F036.question_text: Where along the curb is parking banned around a pedestrian safety zone, including the distance past its ends?
sec06-card-sec06-F036.teaching_text: Leaving that curb lane open keeps transit vehicles and walkers visible around both ends of the island.

sec06-card-sec06-F037.question_text: How does pulling a trailer change your braking needs, and how should you adjust when gusty winds pick up?
sec06-card-sec06-F037.teaching_text: Extra weight pushes your tow vehicle forward under braking while crosswinds whip high-sided trailers into dangerous sway.

sec06-card-sec06-F038.question_text: Above what speed must a towed trailer have safety chains or breakaway brakes capable of holding it if the hitch separates?
sec06-card-sec06-F038.teaching_text: A loose trailer at road speed turns into an unguided battering ram without chains or emergency brakes.

sec06-card-sec06-F039.question_text: What rear lights and reflectors are required on the back of a trailer, and how far back must its taillights show?
sec06-card-sec06-F039.teaching_text: Because a trailer blocks the tow vehicle's rear lamps, drivers behind rely completely on the trailer's lighting.

sec06-card-sec06-F040.question_text: At what width must a trailer carry clearance lamps, and what colors go on the front versus the back?
sec06-card-sec06-F040.teaching_text: Clearance lights outline wide corners at night so oncoming traffic does not clip the trailer's outer edge.
sec06-card-sec06-F040.must_match_memory_hook: Eighty inches: amber front, red rear
