sec06-card-sec06-F041.question_text: At least how far behind your vehicle must your rearview mirror let you see clearly?
sec06-card-sec06-F041.teaching_text: If cargo or a tall camper blocks your center glass, extended side mirrors have to restore that sightline.

sec06-card-sec06-F042.question_text: What two core safety standards must every towing hitch connection meet before you pull onto the road?
sec06-card-sec06-F042.teaching_text: Improvised pins or mismatched hitch balls pop loose over railroad tracks and potholes when weight shifts.

sec06-card-sec06-F043.question_text: Is it legal in North Dakota to shift your transmission into neutral and coast down a hill?
sec06-card-sec06-F043.teaching_text: Dropping out of gear cuts engine braking, overheats your wheel brakes, and kills instant throttle control.

sec07-card-sec07-F001.question_text: When driving a truck or bus down a hill, what must the driver never do with the clutch?
sec07-card-sec07-F001.teaching_text: Coasting down a grade strips away engine braking and lets heavy vehicles pick up dangerous runaway momentum.

sec07-card-sec07-F002.question_text: Before putting your vehicle in reverse, what physical check should you do outside the car and what three things are you looking for?
sec07-card-sec07-F002.teaching_text: Mirrors and cameras leave low blind zones right behind the bumper where toddlers, toys, or curbs hide.

sec07-card-sec07-F003.question_text: When you back out toward a street or travel lane, who carries the responsibility for avoiding traffic interference and entering safely?
sec07-card-sec07-F003.teaching_text: Through traffic never owes a reversing car space, so exam questions always pin crash fault on the person backing out.

sec07-card-sec07-F004.question_text: How big is the North Dakota fine for tossing trash or litter onto a public highway?
sec07-card-sec07-F004.teaching_text: Tossing a wrapper or cup out the window triggers a steep ticket and creates road debris hazards behind you.

sec07-card-sec07-F005.question_text: Which crashes must be reported right away in North Dakota, and which law-enforcement agency do you call inside versus outside city limits?
sec07-card-sec07-F005.teaching_text: Watch the combined damage trap: add every vehicle's repair cost together, then call local police in town or sheriff and patrol outside.

sec07-card-sec07-F006.question_text: Right after a crash with injury or property damage, what four pieces of information must drivers swap at the scene?
sec07-card-sec07-F006.teaching_text: Snapping only a license plate leaves you short — you need both contact details and full policy info before anyone leaves.

sec07-card-sec07-F007.question_text: Suppose a borrower is hurt in a crash and cannot report it. How soon after finding out must the vehicle's owner file the crash notice and insurance info?
sec07-card-sec07-F007.teaching_text: Notice when the five-day clock starts ticking: it begins once the owner learns about the wreck, not the crash hour itself.

sec07-card-sec07-F008.question_text: You bump an empty parked car in a lot. What must you try first, and what three details go on a visible note if you cannot find the owner?
sec07-card-sec07-F008.teaching_text: Driving away turns a minor parking-lot scrape into hit-and-run trouble, and a phone number alone without address and insurer fails the rule.

sec07-card-sec07-F009.question_text: What insurance coverage is mandatory to drive in North Dakota, and what two details must you give an officer when asked?
sec07-card-sec07-F009.teaching_text: Keep digital or paper proof handy in the glovebox because saying your parents pay the bill will not satisfy a roadside stop.

sec07-card-sec07-F010.question_text: What are the North Dakota fines for a first uninsured-driving offense versus a repeat offense within three years — plus the license risk?
sec07-card-sec07-F010.teaching_text: A second ticket inside that three-year window doubles the fine and puts your driving privilege at risk of suspension.

sec07-card-sec07-F011.question_text: After a no-insurance conviction, how long must you prove coverage, what happens to your license, and what two fees apply?
sec07-card-sec07-F011.teaching_text: Exam writers love testing the double fee trap: you pay once to get the restricted card and again later to clear it.

sec07-card-sec07-F012.question_text: On North Dakota highways, when do you dial nine-one-one versus five-one-one?
sec07-card-sec07-F012.teaching_text: Mixing these up ties up emergency dispatchers when all you needed was a winter blizzard or closure check before leaving home.

sec07-card-sec07-F013.question_text: If a North Dakota highway is officially closed for hazardous conditions, can you drive around the gate, and what is the fine?
sec07-card-sec07-F013.teaching_text: Sneaking past a blizzard gate risks stranding both you and rescue crews while handing you a steep citation on top.

sec07-card-sec07-F014.question_text: Before pulling out in winter, what two visibility steps come first, and why should you beware of spraying washer fluid in extreme cold?
sec07-card-sec07-F014.teaching_text: Peeking through a tiny scraped porthole blinds you to cross traffic, and spraying cold glass can sheet over into instant opaque ice.

sec07-card-sec07-F015.question_text: How can you safely gauge road slickness early in a drive, and what should you do once you feel how much grip you have?
sec07-card-sec07-F015.teaching_text: Finding out the pavement is glazed ice at fifty miles per hour is way too late — feel it lightly while rolling slow.

sec07-card-sec07-F016.question_text: Even if your car has winter tires or tire chains on, what two driving adjustments are still required on snow and ice?
sec07-card-sec07-F016.teaching_text: Extra tread helps you get moving, yet overconfident drivers forget that stopping on slick pack still demands way more space.

sec07-card-sec07-F017.question_text: Between which exact dates are studded snow tires legal to run on North Dakota roads?
sec07-card-sec07-F017.teaching_text: Running metal studs into late spring chews up bare dry asphalt and can land you an out-of-season equipment ticket.

sec07-card-sec07-F018.question_text: When a passing truck kicks up a blinding cloud of loose snow, how should you respond and what two things must you watch?
sec07-card-sec07-F018.teaching_text: Slamming the brakes blind inside a truck's snow plume invites a rear-end hit from cars trailing right behind you.

sec07-card-sec07-F019.question_text: Which two parts of a roadway ice over earlier and stay slick longer than the open pavement around them?
sec07-card-sec07-F019.teaching_text: Cold air wraps under bridge decks from above and below, catching drivers off guard when regular pavement still feels wet.

sec07-card-sec07-F020.question_text: When stopping hard in a vehicle equipped with antilock brakes, how should your foot work the brake pedal?
sec07-card-sec07-F020.teaching_text: The computer pulses wheel grip automatically — pumping your foot defeats the system and stretches out your stopping distance.

sec07-card-sec07-F021.question_text: What four specific winter emergency items does the North Dakota handbook tell drivers to keep in the vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-F021.teaching_text: Sneakers and a light hoodie turn dangerous fast if your car slides into a rural prairie ditch during subzero wind.

sec07-card-sec07-F022.question_text: If a blizzard strands your car on a North Dakota road, should you hike out for help or stay put?
sec07-card-sec07-F022.teaching_text: Blowing snow erases landmarks in seconds, and rescuers spot a full-size car along the highway far faster than a person walking.

sec07-card-sec07-F023.question_text: Why must you stay well back from a working snowplow — what three sudden actions can it take, and where is its blind spot?
sec07-card-sec07-F023.teaching_text: Crowding a plow's tailgate puts you invisible in its rear blind zone right where flying grit or a sudden backup hits.

sec07-card-sec07-F024.question_text: On a multilane highway, which parts of the road might a snowplow be working in, and what must you confirm before moving past?
sec07-card-sec07-F024.teaching_text: Swirling snow hides wide wing blades that can straddle lanes or clear shoulders where impatient drivers try squeezing through.

sec07-card-sec07-F025.question_text: What can a heavy snowdrift suddenly do to a moving snowplow, and what does that mean if you pass?
sec07-card-sec07-F025.teaching_text: Hard-packed drifts jolt even massive plow trucks laterally toward the next lane, leaving zero margin if you crowd alongside.

sec07-card-sec07-F026.question_text: What should you do instead of driving straight into a blinding snow whiteout ahead of you?
sec07-card-sec07-F026.teaching_text: Guessing where lanes or stalled cars sit inside zero-visibility snow is how multi-car winter pileups start.

sec07-card-sec07-F027.question_text: Why can a winter road that looks freshly sanded still turn out to be dangerously slick underneath your tires?
sec07-card-sec07-F027.teaching_text: Dark grit on top tricks drivers into speeding up even after traffic and melt-freeze cycles bury the traction grains.

sec07-card-sec07-F028.question_text: What is your primary defense against losing traction and skidding when roads turn slick?
sec07-card-sec07-F028.teaching_text: Preventing a slide by easing your pace early beats trying to recover a spinning car once tire grip breaks.

sec07-card-sec07-F029.question_text: In a rear-wheel-drive skid, what three actions with the brakes, gas pedal, and steering wheel bring the car back inline?
sec07-card-sec07-F029.teaching_text: Panic-braking locks the wheels harder, whereas steering toward the sliding tail aligns the front tires with your travel path.

sec07-card-sec07-F030.question_text: Why are the first minutes of a fresh rainstorm extra slick compared to pavement after a long steady wash?
sec07-card-sec07-F030.teaching_text: Light initial showers float weeks of dripped grease and dust into a greasy film before heavier rain washes it off.

sec07-card-sec07-F031.question_text: What happens between your tires and the pavement when your vehicle starts hydroplaning?
sec07-card-sec07-F031.teaching_text: Once water wedges underneath the tread, steering and braking inputs go dead until speed drops enough for rubber to reconnect.

sec07-card-sec07-F032.question_text: What two hazards rise simultaneously in rainy weather, and what two habits must you bring to match them?
sec07-card-sec07-F032.teaching_text: Glare off wet asphalt hides lane lines and brake lights right when your tires need longer distances to stop.

sec07-card-sec07-F033.question_text: Water is covering the road ahead, though it looks shallow from the driver's seat. What is the right move?
sec07-card-sec07-F033.teaching_text: Drivers misjudge moving water constantly — turning back costs a detour, while gambling across can stall or float your car.

sec07-card-sec07-F034.question_text: Why can you never trust how shallow floodwater looks over a submerged stretch of road?
sec07-card-sec07-F034.teaching_text: Muddy runoff looks flat on top even when rushing currents have carved away the asphalt and roadbed underneath.

sec07-card-sec07-F035.question_text: How little standing water does it take to hit the underside of most passenger cars and stall the engine or kill control?
sec07-card-sec07-F035.teaching_text: Half a foot barely covers the curb, yet it reaches low exhausts, electronics, and tires fast enough to strand sedans.

sec07-card-sec07-F036.question_text: What depth of moving floodwater is strong enough to float and sweep away most vehicles, even pickups and sport-utility vehicles?
sec07-card-sec07-F036.teaching_text: High ground clearance will not save heavy pickups once buoyant rushing water lifts the tires off pavement.

sec07-card-sec07-F037.question_text: If rising floodwater cuts off the only road out and no detour exists, where should you go and what do you do?
sec07-card-sec07-F037.teaching_text: Forcing your only exit through rising currents turns an inconvenience into a swift-water rescue — park high and wait safely.

sec07-card-sec07-F038.question_text: Besides a thumping sound, how can you tell a front-tire blowout apart from a rear-tire failure by how the car moves?
sec07-card-sec07-F038.teaching_text: Exam questions love flipping front and rear cues: a blown front yanks steering sideways, while a blown rear fishtails.

sec07-card-sec07-F039.question_text: A tire blows at highway speed. What is the safe sequence for steering, gas, brakes, and pulling onto the shoulder?
sec07-card-sec07-F039.teaching_text: Stomping the brake pedal immediately after a blowout pitches weight onto the shredded wheel and spins the car out.

sec07-card-sec07-F040.question_text: Your right wheels slip off the pavement edge onto a low shoulder. What mistake must you avoid, and how do you re-enter safely?
sec07-card-sec07-F040.teaching_text: Jerking the wheel hard against a pavement lip slingshots the car straight across your lane into oncoming traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F041.question_text: Your headlights suddenly cut out at night. Which other lights should you try right away as you slow down and exit the road?
sec07-card-sec07-F041.teaching_text: Parking lamps or flashing blinkers run on separate circuits that give you enough glow and visibility to pull completely off.

sec07-card-sec07-F042.question_text: If your gas pedal sticks down while driving, how do you cut power to the wheels — and what ignition mistake must you never make?
sec07-card-sec07-F042.teaching_text: Shifting to neutral disconnects the racing engine safely, whereas twisting the key to lock freezes the steering wheel mid-motion.

sec07-card-sec07-F043.question_text: If you shut the engine off while your vehicle is still rolling, which two critical control systems can suddenly lose power assist?
sec07-card-sec07-F043.teaching_text: Both the wheel and brake pedal abruptly turn stiff and heavy right when you need firm control to pull over.

sec07-card-sec07-F044.question_text: How should you handle speed, braking, and steering when crossing potholes, ruts, broken asphalt, or loose gravel?
sec07-card-sec07-F044.teaching_text: Braking hard inside a pothole or jerking the wheel on loose gravel breaks tire grip and damages suspension parts.

sec07-card-sec07-F045.question_text: A car drifts across the centerline straight into your lane. What do you do first, and where do you escape if it keeps coming?
sec07-card-sec07-F045.teaching_text: Never dodge left into the oncoming lane where the drifting driver is likely to snap back at the last second.

sec07-card-sec07-F046.question_text: Is texting behind the wheel allowed in North Dakota, and what dollar penalty does the handbook list for distracting activity that impairs control?
sec07-card-sec07-F046.teaching_text: Looking down at a message for just a few seconds covers a football field blind and triggers an immediate citation.

sec07-card-sec07-F047.question_text: How many hands belong on the wheel, why should one foot work both pedals, and what mechanical damage does two-foot driving cause?
sec07-card-sec07-F047.teaching_text: Resting a left foot lightly on the brake drags the pads, overheats the rotors, and confuses drivers behind with constant brake lights.

sec07-card-sec07-F048.question_text: When drowsiness hits behind the wheel, what is the safe remedy rather than pushing onward tired?
sec07-card-sec07-F048.teaching_text: Cold air, loud music, and energy drinks mask tiredness briefly while microsleeps still send cars drifting off the highway.

sec08-card-sec08-F001.question_text: What seven physical and driving warning signs tell you fatigue is setting in behind the wheel?
sec08-card-sec08-F001.teaching_text: Forgetting the last few miles or missing highway signs means your brain is already tuning out before your eyes shut.

sec08-card-sec08-F002.question_text: Even on dry pavement, how much distance can a loaded tractor-trailer need to come to a complete stop?
sec08-card-sec08-F002.teaching_text: Cutting right in front of a loaded semi leaves it needing more than a full football field just to stop.

sec08-card-sec08-F003.question_text: How do a long truck's rear wheels track compared to its front wheels, and why might it swing left first?
sec08-card-sec08-F003.teaching_text: Drivers who misread that left swing as a lane change get pinched against the curb when the trailer cuts right.

sec08-card-sec08-F004.question_text: Before you ever pass a truck on its right side, what two things must you check first?
sec08-card-sec08-F004.teaching_text: Sneaking into the open gap along the right curb while a semi sets up a turn puts you in its crush zone.

sec08-card-sec08-F005.question_text: Where are a large truck's major blind areas located, and does the driver's high cab seat get rid of them?
sec08-card-sec08-F005.teaching_text: Sitting high up actually creates a deep hood blind spot in front while long trailers block direct views behind and alongside.

sec08-card-sec08-F006.question_text: When driving near a large truck, how can you tell at a glance whether the trucker can see your car?
sec08-card-sec08-F006.teaching_text: Mirrors work both ways — losing sight of the driver's reflection means you are sitting square inside a blind spot.

sec08-card-sec08-F007.question_text: What two dangerous habits around a truck's sides and front buffer should you avoid, especially near exits or narrow work zones?
sec08-card-sec08-F007.teaching_text: Diving across a semi's nose for a last-second ramp steals the braking cushion a heavy rig needs to avoid hitting you.

sec08-card-sec08-F008.question_text: Which side should you use to pass a tractor-trailer, and how should you pace the pass once you start?
sec08-card-sec08-F008.teaching_text: The driver's left-side blind zone is smaller than the right, and finishing promptly keeps you clear of tire blowouts or wind gusts.

sec08-card-sec08-F009.question_text: Which three everyday maneuvers require noticeably more space for a large truck than for a passenger car?
sec08-card-sec08-F009.teaching_text: Pulling out close ahead of a semi or crowding an intersection corner ignores how slowly heavy loads build or shed momentum.

sec08-card-sec08-F010.question_text: Why do drivers frequently misjudge how fast an oncoming truck is closing in before pulling out?
sec08-card-sec08-F010.teaching_text: Large objects trick human depth perception into thinking you have plenty of gap to turn left when the rig is flying.

sec08-card-sec08-F011.question_text: Outside city limits on an interstate or multilane highway, how must you respond to a stranded car flashing its hazard lights?
sec08-card-sec08-F011.teaching_text: North Dakota extends move-over protection beyond emergency lights to everyday disabled vehicles flashing hazards along fast rural highways.

sec08-card-sec08-F012.question_text: Can a passenger vehicle share part of a lane alongside a motorcycle, or how much lane width does the rider get?
sec08-card-sec08-F012.teaching_text: Riders shift left and right inside their lane to dodge potholes, wind gusts, and oil streaks — squeezing beside them leaves zero room.

sec08-card-sec08-F013.question_text: Why is it harder to judge an approaching motorcycle's distance and speed compared to a full-size car?
sec08-card-sec08-F013.teaching_text: A single headlight and slim silhouette make a bike look farther down the block right when drivers turn left across its path.

sec08-card-sec08-F014.question_text: At which two driving moments does the handbook specifically warn you to check mirrors and blind spots for motorcycles?
sec08-card-sec08-F014.teaching_text: A compact bike disappears easily behind a roof pillar or inside a side-mirror blind zone right before a lane shift.

sec08-card-sec08-F015.question_text: An approaching motorcycle has its turn signal blinking. Why must you wait before pulling out in front of it?
sec08-card-sec08-F015.teaching_text: Many motorcycle turn signals do not self-cancel after a previous corner, so pulling out on a stray blinker causes crashes.

sec08-card-sec08-F016.question_text: Which five road-surface hazards can force a motorcyclist ahead of you to suddenly change speed or shift lane position?
sec08-card-sec08-F016.teaching_text: Minor pavement grooves, loose pebbles, or angled rail tracks that barely rattle four tires can dump a two-wheeled bike instantly.

sec08-card-sec08-F017.question_text: How many seconds of following distance should you keep behind a motorcycle so you both have room for sudden moves?
sec08-card-sec08-F017.teaching_text: Motorcycles stop faster than sedans and swerve around debris without brake lights, so tight tailgating invites a rear-end collision.

sec08-card-sec08-F018.question_text: When overtaking a bicyclist, what speed adjustment and minimum side clearance are required — and when must you wait?
sec08-card-sec08-F018.teaching_text: Buzzing a rider close at full speed creates wind-blast wobble and leaves zero margin if the bike dodges road debris.

sec08-card-sec08-F019.question_text: After you pass a cyclist, how should you check before moving back right, and when do riders need even wider space?
sec08-card-sec08-F019.teaching_text: Cutting back over too early clips the rider's front wheel, and wind or slick rain makes bikes track wider.

sec08-card-sec08-F020.question_text: Where should you watch extra closely for cyclists, and what specific check prevents cutting one off on a right turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F020.teaching_text: Turning right straight across a cyclist rolling up along the curb is one of the most common urban intersection crashes.

sec08-card-sec08-F021.question_text: Under what single driving situation may your car use a marked bicycle lane, and what two steps come before entering it?
sec08-card-sec08-F021.teaching_text: Bike lanes are never travel or parking lanes for cars — treat entering one for a corner just like changing lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F022.question_text: Why are young riders on bicycles extra hazardous to drive near, and what two adjustments should you make?
sec08-card-sec08-F022.teaching_text: Kids sit low below parked-car rooflines and often swerve across driveways or streets without signaling or looking back.

sec08-card-sec08-F023.question_text: During a collision or sudden swerve, what two protective jobs does a fastened seat belt perform for everyone inside?
sec08-card-sec08-F023.teaching_text: Being thrown out of a rolling car is often fatal, and sliding out of the driver's seat kills any chance to steer.

sec08-card-sec08-F024.question_text: Where should the lap strap and shoulder strap sit on your body, and how tight should the belt be?
sec08-card-sec08-F024.teaching_text: Wearing a lap strap high across your stomach or tucking the shoulder strap behind your back causes severe internal crash injuries.

sec08-card-sec08-F025.question_text: If an older car slides a motorized shoulder strap into place automatically, what must you still buckle by hand?
sec08-card-sec08-F025.teaching_text: Relying on an automatic upper strap alone lets your lower body slide straight out from under the restraint in a wreck.

sec08-card-sec08-F026.question_text: Which seats inside a vehicle require occupants to wear a seat belt according to the North Dakota handbook?
sec08-card-sec08-F026.teaching_text: Unbelted rear passengers become human projectiles in a crash, slamming into front-seat riders even if the front row buckled.

sec08-card-sec08-F027.question_text: If your vehicle has front and side airbags, can you skip buckling your lap-and-shoulder belt?
sec08-card-sec08-F027.teaching_text: Airbags inflate fast expecting a belt to hold you back — hitting a deploying bag unrestrained can injure you badly.

sec08-card-sec08-F028.question_text: Under what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster in North Dakota — and what height exception lets them use a regular belt early?
sec08-card-sec08-F028.teaching_text: Adult belts ride up onto a small child's neck and belly until they hit four feet nine inches tall.

sec08-card-sec08-F029.question_text: What is North Dakota's restraint rule for kids and teens ages eight through seventeen?
sec08-card-sec08-F029.teaching_text: Graduating out of a booster never makes belts optional, and tucking the strap under an arm violates proper-use rules.

sec08-card-sec08-F030.question_text: What fine and driving-record penalty does the North Dakota handbook state for breaking the child-passenger restraint law?
sec08-card-sec08-F030.teaching_text: Unlike some non-moving tickets, a child-restraint violation hits both your wallet and your North Dakota license point total.

sec08-card-sec08-F031.question_text: How should a child safety seat and harness fit, and which two instruction guides must you follow when installing it?
sec08-card-sec08-F031.teaching_text: A loose car seat shifts violently on impact, and anchor locations vary between the seat maker's booklet and your car's manual.

sec08-card-sec08-F032.question_text: Under what age should kids sit in the back row, and what is the strict rule on rear-facing infant seats and front airbags?
sec08-card-sec08-F032.teaching_text: A front airbag blasts open at chest height for adults, striking the back of a rear-facing infant carrier with lethal force.

sec08-card-sec08-F033.question_text: What minimum age and minimum weight must a child meet together before moving up into a booster seat?
sec08-card-sec08-F033.teaching_text: Watch the word both on exam questions: hitting forty pounds at age three still keeps a toddler in a harnessed seat.

sec08-card-sec08-F034.question_text: What two unsafe shortcuts with pickup trucks and seat belts must you never allow with child passengers?
sec08-card-sec08-F034.teaching_text: Cargo beds offer zero crash protection, and buckling two kids inside one strap crushes them together during sudden braking.

sec09-card-sec09-F001.question_text: What quick habit must you perform every single time before locking your parked vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F001.teaching_text: Cabin temperatures climb dangerously fast in both summer sun and bitter North Dakota winter cold.

sec09-card-sec09-F002.question_text: Even at home in the driveway, what two precautions keep children from climbing into a parked car alone?
sec09-card-sec09-F002.teaching_text: Curious kids can trap themselves inside a hot trunk or knock a parked car out of gear.

sec09-card-sec09-F003.question_text: Is a quick two-minute errand ever okay with a child left alone in the car — and what if you spot one?
sec09-card-sec09-F003.teaching_text: Quick errands turn into emergencies fast, and bystanders are expected to speak up right away.

sec09-card-sec09-F004.question_text: Which three core driving abilities does alcohol impair, and what happens to that impairment as someone drinks more?
sec09-card-sec09-F004.teaching_text: Impairment starts dulling eye tracking and braking reflexes well before someone reaches the legal limit.

sec09-card-sec09-F005.question_text: Which three factors determine how high a person's alcohol concentration climbs?
sec09-card-sec09-F005.teaching_text: Two people drinking the same beverage at different speeds or lean weights hit totally different concentrations.

sec09-card-sec09-F006.question_text: Why can you never judge how much alcohol you consumed just by looking at the size of a mixed drink?
sec09-card-sec09-F006.teaching_text: One cocktail glass can hold multiple shots of liquor, making drink counting completely unreliable.

sec09-card-sec09-F007.question_text: What actually clears alcohol from your bloodstream — and do coffee, workouts, or cold showers speed it up?
sec09-card-sec09-F007.teaching_text: Caffeine and cold water only create a wide-awake impaired driver while your liver works at one fixed pace.

sec09-card-sec09-F008.question_text: How does alcohol trick a driver's brain when evaluating risky road situations?
sec09-card-sec09-F008.teaching_text: Feeling fine to drive is the exact trap because judgment fails first while physical skills keep dropping.

sec09-card-sec09-F009.question_text: Under North Dakota implied consent, what substances are tested and which four body samples can officers require?
sec09-card-sec09-F009.teaching_text: Driving on North Dakota roads automatically agrees to chemical testing for both alcohol and impairing drugs.

sec09-card-sec09-F010.question_text: For how long can North Dakota revoke your license if you refuse either the roadside screening breath test or the chemical test?
sec09-card-sec09-F010.teaching_text: Saying no at the roadside still costs your license from one hundred eighty days up to three years.

sec09-card-sec09-F011.question_text: What is North Dakota's alcohol-concentration threshold for adult drivers versus drivers under age twenty-one?
sec09-card-sec09-F011.teaching_text: For anyone under twenty-one, even trace alcohol from a single drink crosses that tiny threshold.

sec09-card-sec09-F012.question_text: How do administrative licensing action and criminal court conviction relate in a North Dakota DUI case?
sec09-card-sec09-F012.teaching_text: Beating or delaying a courtroom charge does not automatically stop the licensing division from suspending your driving privileges.

sec09-card-sec09-F013.question_text: On a first alcohol-concentration offense in seven years, how long is the standard license suspension — and what doubles it to one hundred eighty days?
sec09-card-sec09-F013.teaching_text: Hitting zero point one eight percent or higher triggers the harsher half-year penalty right on offense number one.

sec09-card-sec09-F014.question_text: If a driver gets a second alcohol-concentration offense within seven years, what are the base and elevated suspension lengths?
sec09-card-sec09-F014.teaching_text: Crossing zero point one eight percent doubles that full-year suspension straight to twenty-four months off the road.
sec09-card-sec09-F014.must_match_memory_hook: Second offense: one or two years

visual_sync.text_span: Second offense: one or two years

sec09-card-sec09-F015.question_text: What suspension lengths apply to a third or subsequent offense within seven years — both standard and at zero point one eight percent or above?
sec09-card-sec09-F015.teaching_text: Repeat violations inside a seven-year lookback stack multi-year license losses that climb to three full years.
sec09-card-sec09-F015.must_match_memory_hook: Third offense: two or three years

visual_sync.text_span: Third offense: two or three years

sec09-card-sec09-F016.question_text: How many days of suspension must pass before you can seek a restricted license — normally versus inside the twenty-four-seven sobriety program?
sec09-card-sec09-F016.teaching_text: Enrolling in daily sobriety monitoring cuts the mandatory hard-suspension wait more than in half.
sec09-card-sec09-F016.must_match_memory_hook: Thirty days, or fourteen in sobriety

visual_sync.text_span: Thirty days, or fourteen in sobriety

sec09-card-sec09-F017.question_text: What minimum jail time and maximum fine hit a driver caught driving while suspended or revoked for an alcohol violation?
sec09-card-sec09-F017.teaching_text: Sneaking behind the wheel during an alcohol suspension turns a licensing penalty into mandatory time behind bars.

sec09-card-sec09-F018.question_text: Besides your driver license, what items from your vehicle can be impounded during an alcohol-related suspension or revocation?
sec09-card-sec09-F018.teaching_text: Losing your tags grounds the vehicle itself for the entire length of the suspension or revocation.

sec09-card-sec09-F019.question_text: What is the base court-conviction fine stated in the North Dakota handbook for a first DUI?
sec09-card-sec09-F019.teaching_text: Do not confuse this base five-hundred-dollar court fine with the higher fine triggered by extreme alcohol levels.

sec09-card-sec09-F020.question_text: At zero point one six percent or higher on a first DUI conviction, what minimum fine and jail sentence kick in — and how can jail be served?
sec09-card-sec09-F020.teaching_text: Notice the court penalty jumps at zero point one six percent, slightly lower than the administrative suspension jump.

sec09-card-sec09-F021.question_text: What fine, jail sentence, and mandatory sobriety-program term come with a second DUI conviction within seven years?
sec09-card-sec09-F021.teaching_text: A second conviction locks in ten days of jail plus a full year of continuous sobriety monitoring on probation.
sec09-card-sec09-F021.must_match_memory_hook: Thousand fine, ten days, year sobriety

visual_sync.text_span: Thousand fine, ten days, year sobriety

sec11-card-sec11-F001.question_text: How do traffic tickets affect your North Dakota driving record, and what determines how many points a ticket adds?
sec11-card-sec11-F001.teaching_text: Every moving ticket leaves a score on your state file, and major safety offenses climb toward suspension much faster than minor ones.
sec11-card-sec11-F001.must_match_memory_hook: Serious violations stack higher record points

visual_sync.text_span: Serious violations stack higher record points

sec11-card-sec11-F002.question_text: At what point total does North Dakota send a notice of intended suspension and offer an administrative hearing?
sec11-card-sec11-F002.teaching_text: Hitting a dozen points puts your license on the chopping block immediately, though you still get a window to request a hearing.

sec11-card-sec11-F003.question_text: How many suspension days do you get at twelve points, and how is the length calculated at higher point totals?
sec11-card-sec11-F003.teaching_text: Do not multiply all twelve points by seven on the exam; the formula counts seven days for every point above eleven.
sec11-card-sec11-F003.must_match_memory_hook: Seven days per point over eleven

visual_sync.text_span: Seven days per point over eleven

sec11-card-sec11-F004.question_text: How long must you go without any newly recorded points to shave one point off your North Dakota record?
sec11-card-sec11-F004.teaching_text: Staying ticket-free pays off steadily each quarter, letting a careful driver work down old points before reaching the suspension zone.
sec11-card-sec11-F004.must_match_memory_hook: Three clean months drops one point

visual_sync.text_span: Three clean months drops one point

sec11-card-sec11-F005.question_text: How many points can you knock off your driving record by finishing an approved driver-improvement course?
sec11-card-sec11-F005.teaching_text: Taking an approved class gives drivers sitting uncomfortably close to twelve points a three-point cushion against losing their license.
sec11-card-sec11-F005.must_match_memory_hook: Approved improvement course cuts three points

visual_sync.text_span: Approved improvement course cuts three points

sec11-card-sec11-F006.question_text: When can you choose a driver-improvement class instead of taking ticket points, how often, and what combo is barred?
sec11-card-sec11-F006.teaching_text: Test questions love two limits here: violations above five points never qualify, and you cannot double-dip with the three-point reduction.
sec11-card-sec11-F006.must_match_memory_hook: Five-point max yearly, never stack reductions

visual_sync.text_span: Five-point max yearly, never stack reductions

sec11-card-sec11-F007.question_text: What happens if the parent or guardian who sponsored a minor's application withdraws their consent?
sec11-card-sec11-F007.teaching_text: Adult sponsorship is an ongoing co-sign rather than a one-day signature, so pulling approval immediately cancels driving privileges.
sec11-card-sec11-F007.must_match_memory_hook: Sponsor pulls consent, license gets canceled

visual_sync.text_span: Sponsor pulls consent, license gets canceled

sec11-card-sec11-F008.question_text: If parental consent was withdrawn and canceled a teen's license, what two paths let that teen drive legally again?
sec11-card-sec11-F008.teaching_text: Until your eighteenth birthday removes the minor sponsorship requirement, getting back behind the wheel takes fresh parent approval.
sec11-card-sec11-F008.must_match_memory_hook: Renewed parent consent or turning eighteen

visual_sync.text_span: Renewed parent consent or turning eighteen

sec11-card-sec11-F009.question_text: Which five common new-driver risks should parents watch out for while coaching a teen behind the wheel?
sec11-card-sec11-F009.teaching_text: Spotting rushed left-turn gaps or creeping speed from the passenger seat lets a parent coach calmly before a close call happens.
sec11-card-sec11-F009.must_match_memory_hook: Watch speed, gaps, tailgating, distractions, inexperience

visual_sync.text_span: Watch speed, gaps, tailgating, distractions, inexperience

sec11-card-sec11-F010.question_text: Why should parents keep riding along for supervised practice even after a teen passes driver ed and gets licensed?
sec11-card-sec11-F010.teaching_text: Passing a class and road exam proves basic control, not years of seasoned judgment across every surprise road condition.
sec11-card-sec11-F010.must_match_memory_hook: Driver ed starts learning, keep coaching

visual_sync.text_span: Driver ed starts learning, keep coaching

sec11-card-sec11-F011.question_text: Who should be in the car during early practice drives, and what tone should those sessions keep?
sec11-card-sec11-F011.teaching_text: Leaving younger siblings, friends, and backseat chatter at home lowers stress so a new driver can process coaching cues cleanly.
sec11-card-sec11-F011.must_match_memory_hook: Parent and teen only, stay calm

visual_sync.text_span: Parent and teen only, stay calm

sec11-card-sec11-F012.question_text: Which three foundational car-control maneuvers should a beginner master before tackling lane changes and highway merges?
sec11-card-sec11-F012.teaching_text: Building steering feel and spatial judgment at slow speeds prevents panic when fast traffic later demands smooth merges.
sec11-card-sec11-F012.must_match_memory_hook: Park, reverse, turn before merging lanes

visual_sync.text_span: Park, reverse, turn before merging lanes

sec11-card-sec11-F013.question_text: Under what lighting and weather conditions should teen practice start before working up to tougher conditions?
sec11-card-sec11-F013.teaching_text: Mastering vehicle basics under clear skies first ensures rain, glare, or night darkness will not overwhelm a beginner all at once.
sec11-card-sec11-F013.must_match_memory_hook: Start clear daylight, add conditions gradually

visual_sync.text_span: Start clear daylight, add conditions gradually

sec11-card-sec11-F014.question_text: In what order of locations should practice drives step up from lowest risk to heavier traffic?
sec11-card-sec11-F014.teaching_text: An empty lot forgives wide turns or choppy braking while a teen learns pedal feel long before facing highway speeds.
sec11-card-sec11-F014.must_match_memory_hook: Empty lots, quiet streets, then highways

visual_sync.text_span: Empty lots, quiet streets, then highways

sec11-card-sec11-F015.question_text: What four personal and scheduling conditions should both parent and teen meet before starting a practice drive?
sec11-card-sec11-F015.teaching_text: Squeezing a rushed lesson in when either person is exhausted or irritated turns constructive coaching into tense arguments.
sec11-card-sec11-F015.must_match_memory_hook: Rested, ready, good mood, enough time

visual_sync.text_span: Rested, ready, good mood, enough time

sec11-card-sec11-F016.question_text: What four cabin adjustments come before shifting out of park, and when does the coaching checklist advise running headlights?
sec11-card-sec11-F016.teaching_text: Setting mirrors and seat reach while parked stops mid-drive fumbling, and daytime headlights help oncoming traffic spot your car earlier.
sec11-card-sec11-F016.must_match_memory_hook: Adjust cabin, buckle up, headlights always

visual_sync.text_span: Adjust cabin, buckle up, headlights always

sec11-card-sec11-F017.question_text: At which two everyday intersection situations does the coaching checklist stress coming to a complete stop?
sec11-card-sec11-F017.teaching_text: Rolling through a right turn on red is one of the fastest ways to fail a road exam or clip a crosswalk walker.
sec11-card-sec11-F017.must_match_memory_hook: Full stop at signs and red-rights

visual_sync.text_span: Full stop at signs and red-rights

sec11-card-sec11-F018.question_text: How often should a teen check mirrors and surrounding traffic during practice instead of staring straight ahead?
sec11-card-sec11-F018.teaching_text: Locking into a tunnel-vision stare hides cars creeping into adjacent lanes until the moment you suddenly need an escape path.
sec11-card-sec11-F018.must_match_memory_hook: Scan mirrors every six to eight

visual_sync.text_span: Scan mirrors every six to eight

sec11-card-sec11-F019.question_text: What following-time cushion and lane placement does North Dakota's family practice guide recommend?
sec11-card-sec11-F019.teaching_text: New drivers often hug one painted line or crowd bumpers, shrinking both side margin and braking time at once.

sec11-card-sec11-F020.question_text: How can you tell right away whether your car is hiding inside a large truck's blind spot?
sec11-card-sec11-F020.teaching_text: Lingering beside a semi trailer where you cannot spot the driver's face means that rig could merge straight into your lane.
sec11-card-sec11-F020.must_match_memory_hook: No driver in mirror, invisible car

visual_sync.text_span: No driver in mirror, invisible car

sec11-card-sec11-F021.question_text: What tool does the handbook recommend for spelling out clear family driving limits and revisiting them regularly?
sec11-card-sec11-F021.teaching_text: Putting household ground rules in writing ahead of time prevents guesswork and regularly updates privileges as real-world skill grows.
sec11-card-sec11-F021.must_match_memory_hook: Write and review a parent-teen agreement

visual_sync.text_span: Write and review a parent-teen agreement

sec11-card-sec11-F022.question_text: Which four non-negotiable safety rules belong in every family driving agreement?
sec11-card-sec11-F022.teaching_text: Unbuckled friends, speeding, impairment, and phone glances drive the majority of serious teen crashes, making them top household priorities.
sec11-card-sec11-F022.must_match_memory_hook: Belts, speed limits, sober, zero distractions

visual_sync.text_span: Belts, speed limits, sober, zero distractions

sec11-card-sec11-F023.question_text: Beyond driving sober yourself, what passenger safety rule belongs in a parent-teen driving agreement?
sec11-card-sec11-F023.teaching_text: You do not have to hold the keys to get hurt in an impaired crash, so teens need a no-questions safe ride home.
sec11-card-sec11-F023.must_match_memory_hook: Never ride with an impaired driver

visual_sync.text_span: Never ride with an impaired driver

sec11-card-sec11-F024.question_text: Before a teen heads out with the car keys, what three trip details should parents know?
sec11-card-sec11-F024.teaching_text: Checking in on where you are headed, who is riding along, and curfew keeps small delays from turning into family panic.
sec11-card-sec11-F024.must_match_memory_hook: Share destination, passengers, and return time

visual_sync.text_span: Share destination, passengers, and return time

sec11-card-sec11-F025.question_text: When should family consequences for breaking driving rules be set, what should they connect to, and what coaching step can be included?
sec11-card-sec11-F025.teaching_text: Agreeing on privilege curfews and extra coached drives ahead of time keeps accountability focused on building safer habits instead of surprise punishments.
sec11-card-sec11-F025.must_match_memory_hook: Pre-set privilege limits plus extra coaching

visual_sync.text_span: Pre-set privilege limits plus extra coaching

sec11-card-sec11-F026.question_text: What five classic beginner driving mistakes does the handbook highlight around path focus, speed, curves, intersections, and spacing?
sec11-card-sec11-F026.teaching_text: Notice how nearly every rookie crash stems from looking too late or carrying too much speed into curves, intersections, and traffic.
sec11-card-sec11-F026.must_match_memory_hook: Path drift, speed, curves, intersections, tailgating

visual_sync.text_span: Path drift, speed, curves, intersections, tailgating

sec11-card-sec11-F027.question_text: Which five behaviors mark an aggressive driver on the road?
sec11-card-sec11-F027.teaching_text: Spotting weavers, lane blockers, and sign-runners early lets you drop back and create space before their temper targets your car.
sec11-card-sec11-F027.must_match_memory_hook: Lane jumping, tailgating, blocking, running, gestures

visual_sync.text_span: Lane jumping, tailgating, blocking, running, gestures

sec11-card-sec11-F028.question_text: How should you handle your lane and speed if an aggressive driver tries to push or crowd you?
sec11-card-sec11-F028.teaching_text: Treating your lane like turf to guard escalates a rude stranger into a high-speed collision that pride will never win.
sec11-card-sec11-F028.must_match_memory_hook: Make room, never race or defend

visual_sync.text_span: Make room, never race or defend

sec11-card-sec11-F029.question_text: If an angry driver waves or glares at you, what should you avoid doing and where should your focus stay?
sec11-card-sec11-F029.teaching_text: Staring back or trading hand signs pours fuel on road rage, whereas staying buckled and calmly creating distance ends the confrontation.
sec11-card-sec11-F029.must_match_memory_hook: Ignore gestures and eyes, escape belted

visual_sync.text_span: Ignore gestures and eyes, escape belted

sec11-card-sec11-F030.question_text: What four details help police locate an aggressive driver, and what safety rule applies before calling nine-one-one?
sec11-card-sec11-F030.teaching_text: Fumbling with a phone at highway speed creates a second hazard, so pull somewhere safe or let a passenger make the call.
sec11-card-sec11-F030.must_match_memory_hook: Car, plate, spot, direction when safe

visual_sync.text_span: Car, plate, spot, direction when safe

sec11-card-sec11-F031.question_text: How must the car be secured while the teen sits in the driver's seat for the driveway blind-spot drill?
sec11-card-sec11-F031.teaching_text: An adult will be walking inches from the bumpers during this drill, so shutting the engine completely off eliminates rollaway danger.
sec11-card-sec11-F031.must_match_memory_hook: Parked stationary with engine turned off

visual_sync.text_span: Parked stationary with engine turned off

sec11-card-sec11-F032.question_text: During the front blind-spot drill, how far away from the front bumper does the adult step before placing a cone or cup?
sec11-card-sec11-F032.teaching_text: Seeing how far out that cone lands shocks most beginners who never realized how much pavement disappears below the hood.
sec11-card-sec11-F032.must_match_memory_hook: Step out until feet become visible

visual_sync.text_span: Step out until feet become visible

sec11-card-sec11-F033.question_text: After marking the front blind zone, which three other directions around the car do you map and measure — and how does the teen check behind?
sec11-card-sec11-F033.teaching_text: Measuring behind with mirrors and shoulder checks plus both side doors reveals the full hidden ring where kids, bikes, or cars vanish.
sec11-card-sec11-F033.must_match_memory_hook: Map rear and both side boundaries

visual_sync.text_span: Map rear and both side boundaries

sec03-card-sec03-F001.question_text: What three main sign families appear on streets and highways, and which family gives mandatory legal instructions?
sec03-card-sec03-F001.teaching_text: Warning and guide signs inform you, whereas ignoring a regulatory sign breaks traffic law and draws a ticket.

sec03-card-sec03-F002.question_text: What shape is a stop sign, and where must your wheels come to a complete halt when markings are painted?
sec03-card-sec03-F002.teaching_text: Rolling past the painted bar or creeping onto the crosswalk counts as failing to stop on a road test.

sec03-card-sec03-F003.question_text: If an intersection with a stop sign has neither a painted stop line nor a crosswalk, where do you stop?
sec03-card-sec03-F003.teaching_text: Nosing into cross-traffic lanes before stopping creates a T-bone hazard, so halt right before entering where sightlines open.

sec03-card-sec03-F004.question_text: What two actions must you be ready to take at a yield sign when cross traffic or pedestrians are close?
sec03-card-sec03-F004.teaching_text: Treating a yield sign like a free merge causes crashes whenever cross traffic already holds the right of way.

sec03-card-sec03-F005.question_text: Does a posted speed-limit sign guarantee a safe speed in rain, snow, or heavy traffic?
sec03-card-sec03-F005.teaching_text: Driving the full posted number on glare ice or blinding rain can still earn a too-fast-for-conditions citation.

sec03-card-sec03-F006.question_text: How close to the farm must farm hazardous-material hauling stay to qualify under the exemption without a hazmat endorsement?
sec03-card-sec03-F006.teaching_text: Cross beyond that one-hundred-fifty-mile farm radius with agricultural chemicals or fuel and full hazmat endorsement rules apply.

sec03-card-sec03-F007.question_text: How far may a covered farm vehicle operate under the exemption when its greater GVW or GVWR is twenty-six thousand one pounds or less?
sec03-card-sec03-F007.teaching_text: Lighter covered farm trucks enjoy coast-to-coast exemption freedom without hitting the out-of-state air-mile boundary placed on heavier rigs.

sec03-card-sec03-F008.question_text: Where may a covered farm vehicle above twenty-six thousand one pounds operate under the exemption inside and outside its registration state?
sec03-card-sec03-F008.teaching_text: Notice the exam detail for heavier farm rigs crossing state lines: distance is measured in air miles, not road miles.

sec03-card-sec03-F009.question_text: When you turn onto or drive along a posted one-way street, which direction may you travel?
sec03-card-sec03-F009.teaching_text: Check arrow signs before turning at unfamiliar downtown intersections so you never swing nose-to-nose into oncoming lanes.

sec03-card-sec03-F010.question_text: What urgent mistake is a Wrong Way sign telling you on a street, ramp, or freeway?
sec03-card-sec03-F010.teaching_text: Spotting this sign on an exit ramp means oncoming highway traffic is coming straight toward your hood.

sec03-card-sec03-F011.question_text: What does a Do Not Enter sign forbid you from doing at the roadway opening ahead?
sec03-card-sec03-F011.teaching_text: Posted at exit ramps and restricted openings, this sign stops you at the threshold before wrong-way travel starts.

sec03-card-sec03-F012.question_text: On a regulatory sign, what does a red circle with a diagonal red slash across a symbol mean?
sec03-card-sec03-F012.teaching_text: Whether the inner icon shows a left arrow, U-turn, or truck, that red slash bans the pictured move.

sec03-card-sec03-F013.question_text: Which side of the road holds the rectangular Do Not Pass sign, and which side holds the yellow no-passing pennant?
sec03-card-sec03-F013.teaching_text: Placing the yellow pennant on the left shoulder keeps it visible even when a tall truck blocks right-side signs.

sec03-card-sec03-F014.question_text: What does a No Turn on Red sign forbid at an intersection — and does an illuminated electronic sign carry the same force?
sec03-card-sec03-F014.teaching_text: Drivers often overlook light-up blank-out signs beside signals, yet an electronic message carries identical legal weight as metal.

sec03-card-sec03-F015.question_text: Who may enter a two-way center left-turn lane, and what maneuver is strictly banned inside it?
sec03-card-sec03-F015.teaching_text: Using the shared middle lane to overtake slower cars risks a head-on crash with opposing drivers preparing to turn.

sec03-card-sec03-F016.question_text: What do yellow warning signs with dark lettering or symbols alert you to expect up the road?
sec03-card-sec03-F016.teaching_text: Spotting standard yellow ahead gives you early reaction time to ease off the gas and scan before reaching trouble.

sec03-card-sec03-F017.question_text: When should you slow down for a curve or turn warning sign, and what does the small advisory speed plaque tell you?
sec03-card-sec03-F017.teaching_text: Braking hard mid-curve upsets tire grip, especially on gravel or frost, so shed speed while still rolling straight.

sec03-card-sec03-F018.question_text: When a warning sign shows your lane ending ahead, what action must you take?
sec03-card-sec03-F018.teaching_text: Waiting until the painted pavement disappears traps you against the shoulder, so signal early and blend smoothly.

sec03-card-sec03-F019.question_text: How does an added-lane warning sign differ from a standard merge sign for entering traffic?
sec03-card-sec03-F019.teaching_text: Exam questions pit merge against added-lane icons — watch for two separate arrow stems continuing side by side.

sec03-card-sec03-F020.question_text: How do the divided-highway-begins and divided-highway-ends warning signs differ in what happens to opposing traffic?
sec03-card-sec03-F020.teaching_text: Confusing the island position at the top versus bottom of the diamond is a classic sign-identification exam trap.

sec03-card-sec03-F021.question_text: What specific danger are crossroad and side-road warning signs alerting you to watch for ahead?
sec03-card-sec03-F021.teaching_text: Rural trees or hills often hide side roads until the last second, so cover the brake and scan both approaches.

sec03-card-sec03-F022.question_text: What does a round yellow warning sign announce ahead, and how should you adjust your speed?
sec03-card-sec03-F022.teaching_text: Only advance railroad warnings use a yellow circle, giving you space to ease down before reaching the tracks.

sec03-card-sec03-F023.question_text: What colors and shape mark a slow-moving vehicle emblem, and what top speed does that equipment travel?
sec03-card-sec03-F023.teaching_text: Closing on a farm tractor at highway pace eats up gap fast, so brake immediately when that triangle appears.

sec03-card-sec03-F024.question_text: Which two background colors are approved for pedestrian and school warning signs?
sec03-card-sec03-F024.teaching_text: Bright fluorescent yellow-green pops sharply in dawn fog or afternoon shade where kids and walkers step off curbs.

sec03-card-sec03-F025.question_text: How does an advance school-ahead sign differ from a school-crosswalk sign posted right at the crossing?
sec03-card-sec03-F025.teaching_text: One gives early notice that a school zone is coming, while the downward arrow pinpoints where children step across.
sec03-card-sec03-F025.must_match_memory_hook: Ahead warns zone; crosswalk marks crossing

visual_sync.text_span: Ahead warns zone; crosswalk marks crossing

sec03-card-sec03-F026.question_text: Why does a bump warning sign tell you to drop your speed before hitting the rise?
sec03-card-sec03-F026.teaching_text: Hitting frost heaves or sharp pavement rises at full speed can bounce your tires and jerk steering off line.

sec03-card-sec03-F027.question_text: What should you do when you see a slippery-when-wet warning sign and rain has slickened the road?
sec03-card-sec03-F027.teaching_text: Bridges and polished asphalt lose grip quickly in rain, where sudden steering or hard braking triggers hydroplaning.

sec03-card-sec03-F028.question_text: What two jobs do orange cones, drums, tubes, barricades, and vertical panels perform in a work zone?
sec03-card-sec03-F028.teaching_text: Stay smoothly inside their marked path because workers or open pavement drops often sit inches behind those markers.

sec03-card-sec03-F029.question_text: How do you read diagonal stripes on a work-zone barricade or vertical panel to know which side to pass on?
sec03-card-sec03-F029.teaching_text: Picture a raindrop sliding down the diagonal stripes — whichever side it falls toward is the open travel side.

sec03-card-sec03-F030.question_text: When can lighted work-zone arrow panels direct a lane change, and what non-arrow message can they also flash?
sec03-card-sec03-F030.teaching_text: Bright flashing boards cut through midday glare and pitch-black highways alike, alerting you early whether merging or slowing.
sec03-card-sec03-F030.must_match_memory_hook: Day or night arrows, plus caution

visual_sync.text_span: Day or night arrows, plus caution

sec03-card-sec03-F031.question_text: What color combination marks standard construction warning signs, and how can electronic work-zone signs behave?

sec03-card-sec03-F032.question_text: In North Dakota, what minimum fee kicks in if you speed through an active work zone while workers are present?
